+## A harness error of mine, recorded per the coordinator's instruction (same class as the rest of the night)
+
+In job31 I built a boundary test for 07-F1 — "does the early branch fire when `searchmoves` leaves
+exactly ONE candidate?" — and my first version used
+
+    position startpos moves e2e4 e7e5 g1f3
+    go depth 6 searchmoves f3e5
+
+The engine answered `0000` with 6 zero-node depth lines on the base build, and my harness printed a
+warning that read like a finding: *"a zero-node answer on a ONE-candidate legal restriction -> the
+early branch is taken even when a legal candidate exists"*. That would have been a real and serious
+find. It was **false**: after `e2e4 e7e5 g1f3` it is **Black** to move, so `f3e5` was never a legal
+move for the side to move and the engine was correctly reporting an empty root.
+
+python-chess showed it in one line (`is f3e5 legal? False`, piece on f3 is `N`, piece on e5 is `p`),
+which is the habit that has caught every error of mine tonight: check the input against an independent
+oracle before believing the tool. Corrected case (`... g1f3 b8c6`, White to move, Nxe5 a real
+capture): base `f3e5` 138 nodes, PC20 `f3e5` 175 nodes — the boundary is fine (07-C25).
+
+The reason I am writing this as a FINDINGS paragraph rather than silently fixing the script: it is the
+same failure shape as the five blind controls (the go/stop cycle, eval symmetry, the SEE oracle, the
+option surface, the UBSan overflow), and as the 0-node harness bug seat 19 relayed. In every case the
+instrument, not the engine, was wrong, and in every case what caught it was a check that could say
+"no". A warning printed by a harness that has not validated its own input is not a finding.

Isolated by rebuilding a scratch copy with each `FORGE_FIX_*` switch alone: **`FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN` alone → a1a2/1067/21093** (no change), **`FORGE_FIX_HARD_LIMIT_EMERGENCY` alone → identical to base**, **`FORGE_FIX_BARE_KING_LMR_CAP` alone → a7a8q/1124/36405** (exactly the PC answer). With all three off the build matched base exactly (a1a2/1067/21093), so nothing else contributes. **The PC's answer is the better one** — it promotes immediately instead of shuffling — so this is the bare-king reduction cap doing its job on a promotion race that the base tree's reduction was hiding. Threads 1, Hash 16 throughout. |
+| 07-C30 | CLOSES the build-vs-settings caveat of 07-C28: the whole 12 % is the PC20 **options**, not the PC patch — and the attribution is an INTERACTION, not two separable contributions | job35/ (four legs) + job34/raw_base_s14; sums in job34/raw_base_s14/sum_S14_d12.json, job35/raw_base_pc20/sum_PC20_d12.json, job35/raw_pc_s14/sum_S14_d12.json, job30/raw/sum_PC20_d12.json | Four legs, set O, depth 12, **Threads 1, Hash 16**, fresh process per position, `ucinewgame`+`isready` before every `go`: **base+S14 = 9,500,069**, **base+PC20 = 9,500,069**, **PC+S14 = 9,500,069**, **PC+PC20 = 8,315,168**. So: the PC patch alone at S14 changes **nothing** (identical to base), the base cannot honour PC20 at all (it answers `unknown option` for CuckooRep, HistRework, TtPruneV2, CorrHistV2, MateAlphaGuard — verified one by one, so base+PC20 is really S14 and is *not* evidence about the settings), and **100 % of the −1,184,901 needs the PC patch AND the PC20 options together**: −1,184,901 = −1,184,901. That is an interaction, not an additive split, and saying "the patch accounts for X and the settings for Y" would be arithmetically wrong. **A consequence worth noting:** the PC patch's FORGE_FIX_* switches (drawn root, go-parse, bare-king, hard-limit) do not move a single node on this 200-position set at depth 12 S14 — they fix behaviour, not trees, which is consistent with 07-C29 where only BARE_KING_LMR_CAP changed anything and only on a promotion race. |
+| 07-C31 | ISOLATES which PC20 option drives the difference, and finds two with **opposite** signs plus two that are inert here | job35/isolate_pc20.py, raw job35/raw_isolate/isolate.json, job35/isolate.log | PC build, depth 12, **Threads 1, Hash 16**, first **40** positions of set O, S14 sum 1,687,074 as the baseline (note: the 40-position baseline, not the 200-position one). Adding ONE PC20 option at a time: **CorrHistV2 +208,947 (+12.4 %)** — it costs nodes; **TtPruneV2 −163,541 (−9.7 %)** — it saves nodes; **CuckooRep +72,364 (+4.3 %)**; HistRework 3 +15,655 (+0.9 %); **HistRework 2 +517 (+0.0 %)**; **MateAlphaGuard and OwnBookOff: exactly 0**. All six together: **−138,940 (−8.2 %)**. So the net saving is two options pulling in opposite directions and only just netting negative, **not** a broad win from the bundle. For the owner's choice of defaults, TtPruneV2 is the one earning its keep on node count and CorrHistV2 is the one paying for it; whether CorrHistV2's cost buys strength is a games question, not a node-count one, and I did not measure it. MateAlphaGuard's zero is plausible rather than suspicious: it is gated at search.cpp:2134/2159 on `is_mate_score(alpha)`, which these quiet positions rarely reach at depth 12 — so its zero here does NOT mean it is inert. |
+| 07-C32 | EXTENDS the per-option table to all 200 positions, and the bigger sample **reverses two signs** and puts 85 % of the effect on ONE option | job35/isolate_pc20.py, raw job35/raw_isolate200/isolate.json, job35/isolate200.log | PC build, depth 12, **Threads 1, Hash 16**, all **200** positions of set O, baseline S14 **9,500,069** (so these totals are directly comparable to the 07-C30 four legs). One PC20 option at a time: **TtPruneV2 −1,002,190 (−10.5 %)** — this single option is **85 %** of PC20's total −1,184,901; **CorrHistV2 +251,935 (+2.7 %)**; **HistRework 3 −128,374 (−1.4 %)**; **HistRework 2 −57,443 (−0.6 %)**; **CuckooRep −53,470 (−0.6 %)**; **MateAlphaGuard 0**; **OwnBook false 0**; all six together −1,184,901 (−12.5 %). **IMPORTANT CORRECTION to 07-C31:** on the first 40 positions two options had the opposite sign (CuckooRep +72,364 and HistRework 2/3 positive, CorrHistV2 +208,947) and the bundle looked like a near-cancellation between TtPruneV2 and CorrHistV2. On 200 positions CuckooRep and both HistRework levels are **negative**, and TtPruneV2 dominates instead of merely outweighing CorrHistV2. So the 40-position table was **not** representative: it overstated CorrHistV2's drag and understated TtPruneV2's contribution, and any reading of it as "two options cancelling" is withdrawn. The 200-position table is the one to act on. |
+| 07-C33 | The 100-position base-vs-PC differential under identical settings finds **ZERO** differences at depth 12 — and this is a real zero, proven with a control, not a blind instrument | job36/diff100.py, raw job36/raw/diff100.json, job36/run.log; controls job36/raw_control2 and raw_control3 | 100 positions of set O, depth 12, **Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false**, base vs PC r15 under **identical** settings, fresh process per run: **0 of 100 positions differ** — same bestmove, same score, same node count everywhere. **Control that the instrument can see a difference:** the same script on `8/P6k/8/8/8/8/8/K7 w` at depth 10 reports **1 of 1 differ** (base `a1a2`/cp 1067/21,093 vs PC `a7a8q`/cp 1124/36,405), and the 12-position control against a single-switch build also ran clean through the same code path. So the zero is measured, not absent. **Why it is zero, and why that is not surprising once stated:** the four `FORGE_FIX_*` switches target *special states* — a drawn root, a `go` line with a missing value, bare-king endings, a hard-limit already passed — and set O contains ordinary middlegame positions at depth 12 where none of those states occurs. The result therefore says something precise and useful: **on ordinary positions at fixed depth the PC patch is behaviour-identical to base**, which is exactly what 07-C30's four legs showed from the other direction (PC+S14 = base+S14 = 9,500,069). The patch's value is in the special states, not in tree shape. |
+| 07-F3 | 7 | **On the BASE tree, a fifty-move root with a pawn move available is declared a draw without being searched** (`cp 0`, 0 nodes, 12 depth lines) while a forced mate exists, and the PC build gets it RIGHT (`mate 6`, 15,981 nodes, same move). This is the `FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN` defect caught in the act, and it is why the fix is needed. | job37/raw/diff_targeted/diff100.json (row for `8/6qk/8/8/8/1p4p1/4K3/8 b - - 100 1`); reproduced by `python3 job37/../job36/diff100.py <base> <pc> <one-fen-file> 12` | **Builds base 6b98f217 and PC r15; Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false.** Position `8/6qk/8/8/8/1p4p1/4K3/8 b - - 100 1` (halfmove counter **100**, black to move, black has Q + pawns b3/g3 vs lone king): **base → `b3b2`, `cp 0`, 0 nodes**; **PC → `b3b2`, `mate 6`, 15,981 nodes**. **The base is WRONG**, not the PC: the fifty-move rule only draws when no capture or PAWN move has been made, and black has `b3b2` and `g3g2` available, so the counter resets on the very move played and black then mates. Applying file 6's inequality (2N−1 ≤ 100−counter) to the *raw* counter would say 11 ≤ 0 and call the mate impossible — **that inequality is only valid when the fifty-move draw cannot be reset**, and here it can. Base declaring `cp 0` is the old ROOT_DRAWN defect (a drawn root answered without searching); the PC's `mate 6` is correct. **I first read this case the opposite way** and only settled it by checking black's pawn moves — recorded because the wrong reading would have been a false accusation against the PC build. |
+| 07-C34 | GIVES THE OWNER the answer "where does the PC patch act?": **50 of 100 targeted positions differ, 0 of 100 ordinary middlegames differ** — and every difference is attributable to a named switch | job37/build_samples.py + job36/diff100.py, raw job37/raw/diff_targeted/diff100.json and job37/raw/diff_ordinary/diff100.json, logs job37/raw/targeted.log and job37/raw/ordinary.log | **Builds base 6b98f217 vs PC r15 under IDENTICAL settings; Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false; depth 12; fresh process per run.** Two samples built from real material (set G) with python-chess doing the classification: **targeted 100** = 30 bare-king endings (stripped from G), 20 fifty-move-counter-100 roots, 50 late endgames; **ordinary 100** = G middlegames with material ≥ 26 and no bare king. **Targeted: 50 of 100 differ** — **30 attributed to `FORGE_FIX_BARE_KING_LMR_CAP`** (every bare-king position), **19 to `FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN`** (every fifty-move position, 19 of 20 matching that variant exactly and 1 differing only in node count with the same move and score), **1 as a combination**. **Ordinary: 0 of 100 differ.** So the patch is **precisely targeted, not a broad rewrite**: it changes exactly the special-state positions its switches name and leaves ordinary middlegame trees bit-identical. Combined with 07-C33 (0 of 100 on set O) and 07-C30 (PC+S14 == base+S14 = 9,500,069) this is now measured three independent ways. |
+| 07-C35 | The targeted differential also shows the **base tree** failing a case the PC build gets right, i.e. direct evidence the fixes are needed rather than neutral | job37/raw/diff_targeted/diff100.json, all 20 fifty-move rows | On the 20 fifty-move-counter-100 positions the base build returns **`cp 0` with 0 nodes on all 20** — it answers a drawn root without searching, exactly the ROOT_DRAWN defect. The PC build searches them and, on at least one (`8/6qk/8/8/8/1p4p1/4K3/8 b - - 100 1`), finds **`mate 6`** where the base claimed a draw while black had a pawn move to reset the counter (07-F3). That is the fix earning its place on real material, and it is the first case tonight where the base tree is demonstrably **wrong** and the PC build demonstrably **right**. |
+| 07-F4 | 7 | **The base tree declares a draw on EVERY fifty-move root with a reset available, and on 6 of 20 the reset-probe shows a decisive result (5 losses masked, 1 win thrown away).** So `FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN` is worth having, but its practical value here is mostly in the 1 thrown-away win, not in the 6. | job38/fifty_rate.py, raw job38/raw/fifty_rate.json | **Builds base 6b98f217 and PC r15; Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false; depth 12.** All **20** fifty-move-counter-100 positions of the targeted sample have a **counter-resetting move** available (a pawn move or capture — python-chess decided this, not the engine), so **none of them is a genuine fifty-move draw** and base's `cp 0` is a declaration rather than a measured result on all 20 (`0 nodes` every time). The independent referee is the SAME board with the counter set to 0, searched to depth 12 on the base build — with the clock reset the fifty-move rule is 100 half-moves away, so its score is what the position is really worth: **decisive (\|cp\| ≥ 300 or mate) on 6 of 20** — `cp 2950` (the mate-6 case, 07-F3), and five **losses** at `cp −1601, −942, −477, −1039, −963`; **noise band (\|cp\| ≤ 50) on 4**; **inconclusive at depth 12 (51..299) on 10**. **My first version of this analysis claimed "19 of 20 base-tree errors", and that was wrong** — it counted `cp −1601` and `cp −6` alike as "a win exists". The honest rates are: decisive-error **6 of 20 (30 %)**, of which the side to move is winning in only **1** (the win thrown away) and losing in **5** (a draw declared where the engine was being beaten — wrong, but it costs the engine nothing). |
+| 07-C36 | Scans all 30 bare-king positions for a **PC regression** and finds **none** — the answer to the other seat's mate-in-10-vs-mate-in-8 worry on this sample | job38/bareking_worse.py, raw job38/raw/bareking_worse.json, job38/bareking.log | **Builds base 6b98f217, PC r15 and the `FORGE_FIX_BARE_KING_LMR_CAP`-only variant; Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false; depth 12, with a depth-18 PC reference.** Of the 30 bare-king positions: **14 NEUTRAL (within ±50 cp)**, **5 PC-BETTER**, **4 differing below the decisive margin**, and **7 where the PC's depth-12 score is more negative than base's by ≥100 cp**. Those 7 are **not regressions**: in **every one** the PC score is **closer to the depth-18 reference** than base's (e.g. `8/6k1/8/4K3/8/R5P1/5P2/8 b` base −1735, PC −2112, d18 **mate −6**; `8/3R4/3P3h6/... b` base −1612, PC −1778, d18 **mate −10**). A more negative score in a position where the side to move is being mated is *more accurate*, not worse — base was under-estimating how lost it was. **So the mate-10-vs-mate-8 regression another seat saw does not appear in these 30.** My first pass labelled all 7 "PC-WORSE: candidate regression" from the raw sign comparison; the depth-18 reference reversed every one, which is exactly why the reference was in the harness. |
+| 07-C37 | No bare-king position in this sample is one where the cap **lengthens** a mate the engine can already see — checked directly on mate distances | job38/bareking_worse.py, rows where both builds report a mate | Where both builds report a mate, the distance is compared in plies. This sample contains **no** position where base reports `mate N` and the PC reports a longer mate: base reports **no mate at all** on these (its bare-king answers are large negative `cp` or a 0-node draw), so the mate-distance regression the other seat described is **not reproducible here**. That is a negative result about *this sample*, not a refutation of their position — their case may involve a position where base's own search does find the shorter mate, which is a different shape from these stripped endgames. |
+| 07-C38 | TIGHTENS 07-F4's rate with a deeper reference, and the answer is **lower**, not higher: decisive base error **5 of 20 (25 %)**, thrown-away win **1 of 20** — and one depth-12 "decisive" case was a **depth-12 artefact** | job39/fifty_deep.py, raw job39/raw/fifty_deep.json, job39/deep18.log; convergence sweep job39/conv.log | **Base build; Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false.** Re-ran the counter-RESET reference (same board, halfmove counter 0) at **depth 18** for all twenty, and at **depths 12, 16, 20, 24** for the ten that matter. Result: **none of the 14 inconclusive-at-12 became decisive at 18**, and the decisive count went **down from 6 to 5** because position #7 read `cp −477` at depth 12 and `cp −84 / −70 / −52` at depths 16/20/24 — a depth-12 artefact, **not** a base error. Meanwhile the genuine cases only got stronger with depth: **#0** went `cp −1601` → `cp −1789` → **`mate −16`** → **`mate −9`**, and **#10** went `cp 2950` → **`mate 4`** and stayed there at depths 16, 20 and 24. At depth 24 the decisive five are **#0, #4, #10, #11, #13**, of which **#10 is the only win thrown away** and the other four are losses masked. **So the tightened rate is 5 of 20 (25 %), with 1 of 20 being a thrown-away win** — replacing 07-F4's 6 of 20, and replacing my earlier withdrawn claim of 19 of 20. Method note: the classification thresholds (±300 cp, or any mate) were fixed in the script before the run so the number could not be read generously afterwards. |

@@ -0,0 +1,124 @@
+# PC20 BASELINE — set O at depth 12, PC r15 build
+
+**Purpose:** the base tree under S14 has four published sums that let any seat prove its harness. The
+PC build has **no published sum** (file 5 publishes only PC20 *bench* numbers), so this file records
+one measured baseline with enough detail that a later seat can prove its harness against it the same
+way.
+
+Numbers in this file are **measured by seat 07**, not published by Opus. They are a reference point,
+not an authority: if your harness disagrees, check your regime before doubting either number.
+
+## The number
+
+| quantity | value |
+|---|---|
+| build | PC r15 = base `6b98f217` + `pc_r15.patch` (sha256 `d6bd72c531f785f4…`), **without** the 07-F1 patch |
+| settings | **PC20** (see below) |
+| Threads / Hash | **1 / 16** |
+| positions | 200 (set O = `forge-combo29/tests_kimi5_job3/first200.fens`, branch `for-fable-and-opus/kimi5-work`) |
+| depth | 12 |
+| **SUM** | **8,315,168** |
+| per-position sha256 (i\|fen\|nodes\|score\|best) | `e6beb5f9448f2a1a4481a794f2e28c9061c722213d112c71a9a3a221c76afd92` |
+| nodes-only sha256 (i\|fen\|nodes) | `2337b0d12b545ac07446f311a3b6679faada3bda2c589088131fc7ece1472636` |
+
+For comparison, the **base tree under S14** gives **9,500,069** for the same 200 positions at depth 12
+(published in the brief; reproduced exactly by this seat as 07-C3). They differ because the PC build
+changes search, not because either is wrong.
+
+## The exact command
+
+    cd forge-combo29/swarm/07/job30
+    python3 -u pc20_sums.py /agent/repos/pcbase/forge-combo29/build-pc/forge \
+                    /tmp/first200.fens raw 12 --pc20
+
+The driver is `job30/pc20_sums.py` in this folder. Raw output: `job30/raw/sum_PC20_d12.json`
+(every position with its fen, nodes, score and bestmove), digest: `job30/raw/baseline_digest.json`.
+
+## The option lines, in order
+
+Sent as `setoption name <line>` followed by `isready` read to `readyok`, before `ucinewgame`:
+
+    Hash value 16
+    Threads value 1
+    LmrQuietBase value 93
+    LmrQuietDivisor value 205
+    LmrNoisyBase value 13
+    LmrNoisyDivisor value 333
+    LmrHistoryDivisor value 5643
+    NullMoveBase value 5
+    LmpBase value 8
+    HistoryPruneMultiplier value 2220
+    HistoryBonusQuadratic value 24
+    HistoryBonusLinear value 54
+    HistoryBonusMax value 2212
+    SingularDepth value 6
+    IirDepth value 2
+    NonPawnCorrection value true
+    CuckooRep value true
+    HistRework value 2
+    TtPruneV2 value true
+    CorrHistV2 value true
+    MateAlphaGuard value true
+    OwnBook value false
+
+The first sixteen are Hash/Threads plus S14; the last six are the PC20 additions. `MateAlphaGuard`
+exists only because the build uses `-DFORGE_MATE_ALPHA_GUARD=1`; a build without that flag answers it
+`unknown option`, which is the quickest way to tell you are on the wrong binary.
+
+## The process discipline (this is what makes the number reproducible)
+
+1. **One fresh engine process per position.** Not one process for all 200. Seat 10 showed that a
+   second search in the same process is warm (56,720 → 4,951 → 4,516 nodes), so a shared process
+   cannot produce this number.
+2. **`ucinewgame` + `isready` before every `go`**, in addition to (1). Belt and braces; `ucinewgame`
+   restores a cold state and `Clear Hash` does **not** (it leaves the histories, seat 27's S-F4).
+3. **Never send a command while a `go` is running.** Read stdout until `bestmove`. Seat 19's 19-F12
+   is exactly what happens to a harness that pipelines: a fabricated `bestmove` with 0 nodes.
+4. **Threads 1.** A score from Threads > 1 is not reproducible (swarm rule; seat 04 measured four
+   different scores on one position at Threads 4).
+5. **No `OwnBook`** for measurements; PC20 sets it false, and it must be, or a book move answers with
+   no `info depth` line at all and the position measures nothing.
+
+## How to prove your harness against this
+
+Run your own harness over the same 200 FENs under PC20, Threads 1, and compare:
+
+- **the sum** — must be exactly `8315168`; and
+- **the per-position digest** — build `i|fen|nodes|score|best` lines in file order, join with `\n`,
+  sha256, compare with `e6beb5f9…`. A matching digest means you agree position by position, not just
+  in total, which is the stronger check: two compensating errors can hide behind an equal sum.
+
+If your total matches but the digest does not, you have a per-position disagreement worth
+investigating. If neither matches, check the six PC20 options reached the engine (no `unknown option`
+line) and that you used `-DFORGE_MATE_ALPHA_GUARD=1`.
+
+## Reproducibility check I ran on this baseline itself
+
+A baseline is worthless if its own author cannot reproduce it. I re-ran the **first 40 positions** in a
+second, independent invocation and compared position by position against the first 40 rows of the
+200-position run:
+
+    first 40 positions compared, mismatches: 0
+    full-run sum of first 40: 1548134
+    40-run sum              : 1548134
+    REPRODUCIBLE: True
+
+So the number is stable across process boundaries, which is the property that makes it usable as a
+harness test. Raw: `job30/raw40/sum_PC20_d12.json`.
+
+## What this baseline is NOT
+
+- **Not** a strength claim, and not evidence that PC20 is good; it is a finger-print of one
+  configuration.
+- **Not** published by Opus. The four S14 sums are; this is not. Treat it as a peer's measurement.
+- **Not** valid for a build carrying the 07-F1 patch *if* that patch changed any node count — it does
+  not (verified: all eight PC pins unchanged, and 07-C23), so the same sum holds, but say which binary
+  you used.
+
+## Provenance
+
+- Seat 07, area 7. Measured 2026-11-16, first run `22:28Z`.
+- Build: `/agent/repos/pcbase/forge-combo29/build-pc/forge`, from worktree `/agent/repos/pcbase`
+  (base `6b98f217` + the file-5 patch), built with
+  `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-DFORGE_MATE_ALPHA_GUARD=1`, g++ 13.3.0.
+- Timestamp: see `job30/stamps.txt`.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 10: the GUI's normal `go`/`stop` cycle, and a bug in my own test
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 UCI-loop read, prioritising what shows in normal play.
+
+**Answer:** the shape a real GUI drives — `position`, `go infinite`, `stop`, `bestmove`, next
+position — is **safe over 40 plies in one process**, including a `go ponder` + `ponderhit` round and
+a `go depth 200` + `stop` round, with `ucinewgame` interleaved every 7 rounds and a plain
+`go depth 6` afterwards that still searched properly.
+
+**How sure:** high *after* I fixed my test. My first version of the test was **blind**: it passed a
+build with the stop-flag reset deleted. I found that with a planted-fault control, fixed the test,
+and the control then failed as it must. Both runs are kept.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source changed in
+the repo; the fault build is a copy at `/tmp/stalefault`.
+
+## The result
+
+    rounds requested 40, plies played 40
+    final search after the cycle: bestmove d2d4 nodes 1155
+    RESULT: every go/stop and go/ponderhit cycle returned a legal move with nodes > 0,
+            and a plain search still worked afterwards
+
+Per round the test asserts: a `bestmove` arrives within the timeout (a hang is a failure), the move
+is **legal in the position that was sent** (python-chess), a `bestmove 0000` only when the position
+has no legal move, and a parsed `nodes` figure greater than zero.
+
+Raw: job10/raw/transcript.txt (every line the engine sent, with `>>` for commands sent).
+
+## The bug in my own test, and the control that found it
+
+The engine's stop handling is this chain in `uci.cpp`:
+
+    uci.cpp:169  auto stop_search = [&]() { ... searcher.stop(); ... worker.join();
+                                              ponder_search_active = false; };
+    uci.cpp:551  searcher.reset_stop();      // before every search
+    uci.cpp:637  } else if (command == "stop") { stop_search(); }
+
+**Planted fault:** delete `searcher.reset_stop();` from a copy of the tree, rebuild
+(`/tmp/stalefault`, built with the same CMake recipe and flags). A stale stop flag should then make
+every search after the first answer instantly.
+
+**My test did not catch it.** The control run printed:
+
+    rounds requested 12, plies played 12
+    final search after the cycle: bestmove a2a3 nodes None
+    RESULT: every go/stop and go/ponderhit cycle returned a legal move with nodes > 0 ...
+
+The tell was `nodes None` — no `info depth ... nodes` line was parsed at all — and my assertions
+treated "no nodes figure" as "not zero", i.e. as a pass. That is exactly the failure mode seat 19
+warned about: a missing measurement passing as a good result.
+
+**Fix:** a missing nodes line is now itself a failure. Re-running the control:
+
+    FAIL round 1: no 'info depth ... nodes' line was parsed, so the round measured nothing (bestmove a2a3)
+    FAIL final go depth 6 produced no nodes line: the engine never searched
+    RESULT: 2 failure(s)
+
+Only then did I re-run the real build, which passed. The committed script is the fixed one; the
+control output is kept in job10/raw_control/ so the correction is visible.
+
+## Why this matters for the engine
+
+`stop` / `ponderhit` / `quit` while a search runs is the most frequent UCI interaction a GUI makes.
+A stale stop flag there would show as an engine that answers `bestmove` instantly with a first-legal
+move — a strength bug that no bench or perft would reveal. Over 40 real cycles, plus the two special
+branches, it does not happen.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C5** in FINDINGS.md records the clean result **and** the harness bug, because the second half is
+what makes the first half trustworthy.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Round 1 of the control returned `a2a3` with no nodes line; the clean build returns a real search
+  on round 1 as well, so the difference is confined to the reset path. I did not trace it further
+  than the control shows.
+- Seat 10's warning (two searches in one process give 56,720 then 4,951 then 4,516 nodes) is a
+  *node-count* effect, not a stop-flag effect, and my cycle test does not contradict it: it only
+  asserts nodes > 0, not a specific count.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test `stop` arriving *before* `go` (a malformed GUI) — that is job1 edge-case territory.
+- Did not test `quit` during an infinite search beyond the single `ponder_quit` case in job1.
+
+## Times
+
+See job10/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job11.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job11.md
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..99f4afc76
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job11.md
@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 11: the clock in a GUI-style game, and the book trap
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read (the time manager is one of the eight files in the area's order),
+prioritising what shows in normal play.
+
+**Answer:** across nine time controls — including the nasty ones (`wtime 100`, `30`, `10`, `0`, and
+`movestogo 1 / 2 / 40`) — the engine **never overran its remaining clock and never played an illegal
+move**, and every search reported a real node count. I also found a measurement trap worth passing to
+other seats: the built-in book answers clock searches and emits **no** `info depth` line, so a clock
+harness that does not disable `OwnBook` silently measures book moves instead of searches.
+
+**How sure:** high for no-overrun / no-illegal at these controls. Moderate for the general claim: I
+tested nine controls of a few dozen plies each, on a 4-core box shared with other seats, so a very
+rare overrun could be missed. The 5 ms slack in the overrun test is stated below.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source changed.
+
+## The test
+
+`job11/clock_behaviour.py`: for each control it plays a self-game. Every move is
+`position fen <current>`, `isready` to readyok, then `go wtime .. btime .. winc .. binc [movestogo ..]`.
+The move the engine answers is played on a python-chess board and the side's clock is decremented by
+the measured wall time plus the increment. Recorded per search: wall time (`go` sent → `bestmove`
+read, monotonic), the engine's own `time` and `nodes`, legality of the move, and whether the wall time
+exceeded the clock the engine had left.
+
+**Overrun definition:** `wall_ms > left_ms + 5`. The 5 ms is measurement slack for this harness, not
+an engine allowance — a real engine budget already subtracts `Move Overhead` (default 10 ms).
+
+    sudden_1000    plies  24  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall    138.9 ms
+    sudden_10000   plies  24  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall   2278.5 ms
+    mtg_1          plies  12  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall    593.3 ms
+    mtg_2          plies  12  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall    451.1 ms
+    mtg_40         plies  16  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall     62.5 ms
+    tiny_100       plies  12  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall     11.2 ms
+    tiny_30        plies  10  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall      1.8 ms
+    tiny_10        plies   8  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall      1.2 ms
+    zero_0         plies   6  overruns 0  rows without nodes 0  worst wall      0.9 ms
+
+Per-control tables: job11/raw/<control>.txt.
+
+## The trap I fell into first, and why the numbers above are the real ones
+
+My first run reported `rows without nodes 16` of 24 in *every* control — and my script still printed
+"no overrun, no illegal move". Diagnosis: the engine was answering with a **book move**, and a book
+move prints `info string book move ...` then `bestmove` with no `info depth` line at all. The book is
+enabled by default (`OwnBook` default true) and applies precisely to clock searches
+(`uci.cpp:525-527`: `game_search` = clock or movetime, not infinite, not ponder, no searchmoves, no
+mate).
+
+Two consequences, both fixed here:
+
+1. **My test** now sets `OwnBook value false` and treats a missing nodes figure as a failure. Only
+   then do all nine controls report `rows without nodes 0`.
+2. **A general trap for the swarm:** any clock or movetime measurement that does not turn the book off
+   is measuring book lookups, not searches, and any test that silently accepts a missing `info depth`
+   line will report success while measuring nothing. This is the same class of error seat 19 flagged.
+
+## Why `movestogo` looked wrong and is not
+
+`mtg_2` row 3 showed 431 ms wall with the last reported iteration at `time 19`. That looked like a
+discarded 400 ms iteration. Re-running the identical command with per-line timing:
+
+    info depth 14 ... time 74
+    info depth 15 ... time 136
+    bestmove g1f3          (at 136.9 ms wall)
+
+The 431 ms row was a different position in the self-game (the engine's own `time` field is per
+search). The clock plan for `wtime 549 … movestogo 2` is soft ≈ 179 ms, hard ≈ 431 ms, and the search
+stopped at 137 ms, comfortably inside both. No fault.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C7** in FINDINGS.md (clean clock result, plus the book caveat).
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- `plan_clock_budget` (include/forge/clock_plan.hpp) computes `hard = std::min(available * 4 / 5,
+  soft * 4)` in the movestogo branch, and `soft` can exceed `hard` before both are clamped, after
+  which `soft = hard`. Arithmetic-wise `available * 4` cannot overflow for the parse ceiling
+  `kMaxClockMs = int64_max / 256`, so I found no overflow, but I did not prove the clamp order is
+  intended rather than merely harmless.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test book behaviour itself (only disabled it).
+- Did not measure the 99th percentile of overruns over hundreds of searches (area 8's job).
+- Did not test `movetime` in this loop; job1's edge cases covered `movetime 0/50/500`.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether a very short control (`wtime 10`) can overrun on a machine with other seats' load; my run
+  had 4 cores shared with several agents.
+
+## Times
+
+See job11/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job12.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job12.md

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 12: colour symmetry of `eval` — and two wrong versions of my own test
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read (the evaluation is one of the eight files in the area's order),
+prioritising what shows in normal play.
+
+**Answer:** the engine's static evaluation **is exactly colour-symmetric**: for every one of 200
+positions, `eval` of the position and `eval` of its colour-flipped mirror return the *same* number,
+which is the correct result given the engine's perspective convention. No asymmetry, so no colour
+bias. Getting to that answer required me to correct **two mistakes in my own test**, both recorded
+below, because a symmetry test that asserts the wrong relationship is worthless.
+
+**How sure:** high, now — the relationship is established empirically from the engine's own output
+rather than assumed, and the test carries a control proving its comparison is not dead.
+
+## The convention, established from the engine rather than assumed
+
+`src/eval.cpp:509` ends the evaluation with
+
+    return board.side_to_move() == White ? tapered : -tapered;
+
+i.e. the value is **from the side to move's point of view**. Verified directly: the same board with
+White to move prints `total 74`, and with Black to move prints `total -35`.
+
+Therefore, for a position `P` and its colour mirror `M` (colours swapped, board flipped vertically,
+side to move swapped, castling rights swapped), the correct check is
+
+    eval(P) == eval(M)
+
+because in `M` the same side that had the advantage in `P` is now the other colour *and* is also the
+side to move. That is exactly how colour symmetry manifests when the score is stm-relative.
+
+## My two wrong versions, and what exposed each
+
+1. **First version** compared `eval(P) != -eval(M)` on the assumption the score was White-positive.
+   It reported *588 "asymmetric" values* — and every single reported pair had **identical** numbers
+   (`49 vs 49`, `-79 vs -79`, `52 vs 52`). Identical numbers cannot be an asymmetry of a negated
+   relationship; that internal contradiction is what showed the bug was mine.
+2. **Second version** corrected the relationship but I also hand-typed a mirror FEN to double-check
+   and got it wrong (`r2k1b1r/... b kq` instead of `r1b1k2r/... b KQkq`), which made a hand check
+   look meaningless. Fixed by using only `chess.Board(fen).mirror().fen()` from python-chess.
+
+## The result
+
+    positions 200 (each also mirrored): 600 comparisons
+    asymmetric values: 0
+    control (two different positions must differ): 2 vs 938 -> works
+    RESULT: eval() is exactly colour-symmetric on every position tested
+
+The control matters: two clearly different positions (bare kings vs kings plus a queen) give
+different totals, so the comparison is capable of reporting a difference. The 600 comparisons are
+3 components (hce, nnue, total) × 200 positions.
+
+Raw: job12/raw/differences.txt (empty, which is the result).
+
+## Why this is worth a line even though it is clean
+
+A colour asymmetry in static evaluation is a silent strength bug: the engine would systematically
+prefer one side's structures, and no bench/perft would reveal it. It is also the kind of thing a
+tuned NNUE can break by accident, and this build's net is a residual net (seat 19's 19-F1) that adds a
+hand-crafted term to the network — two code paths that could disagree about colour. They do not.
+
+## Findings
+
+None. Recorded here rather than in FINDINGS because a clean symmetry is not a finding; the value is
+the negative result plus the verified perspective convention, which other seats need if they measure
+`eval` (several area-6 jobs do).
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- This covers `eval`'s three printed components, not the search-time evaluation with correction
+  history applied (`Worker::static_evaluate` adds `corrected_eval`, which is history-dependent and
+  therefore not mirror-symmetric by construction — that is expected, not a fault, and I did not test
+  it).
+- Area 6's job 2 (left-right mirror) is a different symmetry and I did not test it.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test the search's final scores for symmetry (area 6 job 3).
+- Did not test positions with castling rights on one side only in a systematic way; the mirror
+  carries the swapped rights through python-chess.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether the `incheck 1` suffix line (printed when the side to move is in check) can accompany a
+  different code path that changes the value; I did not isolate it.
+
+## Times
+
+See job12/stamps.txt.

@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 13: the inline legality shortcut, and a control planted in the wrong file
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read (move generator / position and move making), prioritising what
+shows in normal play.
+
+**Answer:** the shipped legality shortcut is **correct on all 289,809 pseudo-legal moves** tested
+over 40 random games. It is also the single most-executed correctness decision in the engine, since
+every node's move list passes through it, so a false "legal" here is an illegal move played.
+
+**How sure:** high, after I fixed a control that was planted in the wrong file (see below).
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source changed.
+
+## The code under test
+
+The shortcut is **inline in the header**, not in board.cpp:
+
+    include/forge/board.hpp:321  inline bool Board::is_legal(const Move& move) const {
+    include/forge/board.hpp:324      if (checkers_ == 0 && (move.flags & EnPassant) == 0U &&
+                                         piece_type(moving) != King) {
+    include/forge/board.hpp:325          if (!king_lines_.valid) refresh_king_lines();
+    include/forge/board.hpp:327          return (king_lines_.pinned & square_bb(move.from)) == 0 ||
+                                                attacks::aligned(king, move.from, move.to);
+    include/forge/board.hpp:330      return is_legal_complete(move);
+
+So: when the side to move is not in check, the move is not en passant, and the mover is not the king,
+legality is decided **only** by a pin set and one alignment test. Everything else (checks, king moves,
+en passant, castling) defers to `is_legal_complete`.
+
+## Test
+
+`job13/is_legal_probe.cpp` compares, for every pseudo-legal move generated at every ply of 40 random
+games:
+
+- `fast` = `board.is_legal(move)` — the shipped shortcut;
+- `brute` = make the move on a copy, then ask whether the mover's own king is attacked by the new
+  side to move.
+
+    games 40 seed 701
+    moves compared 289809  mismatches 0 (fast-says-legal-but-illegal 0,
+                                        fast-says-illegal-but-legal 0)
+    OK the fast legality path agreed with make/unmake brute force on every move
+
+The split matters: a fast-says-legal error would be an *illegal move played*, a fast-says-illegal
+error would be a *missed legal move* (a weaker but not broken engine). Both are zero.
+
+## The control trap, stated plainly
+
+**First attempt:** I patched `is_legal_complete` in `src/board.cpp` to `return true;` and the probe
+still passed. That is the same failure shape as the go/stop test earlier tonight: a control that
+cannot fail means the test is not testing the thing.
+
+**Diagnosis:** the shortcut is `inline` in `include/forge/board.hpp` and never calls
+`is_legal_complete` on the fast path, so a fault in the .cpp file is unreachable for the moves the
+probe exercises.
+
+**Second attempt:** plant the same fault in the header copy (`/tmp/inc_fault/forge/board.hpp`),
+keeping everything else identical:
+
+    games 10 seed 701
+    moves compared 69139  mismatches 494 (fast-says-legal-but-illegal 494, ...)
+    FIRST MISMATCH fen 3rkbnr/3bqpp1/p1pp4/1p5p/2P4P/4P1PN/PP4RP/RNBQKB2 w Qk - 0 16
+                 move e3d4 fast legal brute illegal
+
+So the probe does detect exactly the class of bug it is aimed at, and the clean run is a result.
+**Lesson for other seats:** a planted fault must go in the file the code actually lives in; for
+legality that is `board.hpp`, not `board.cpp`.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C10** in FINDINGS.md — clean result plus the control-design trap.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- `king_lines_.pinned` is computed by `refresh_king_lines()` and cached with a `valid` flag that
+  `make_move`/`make_null_move` clear (board.cpp:1106, 1165). I verified the pin logic indirectly
+  through this probe but did not test the cache-invalidation path on its own with a control.
+- `gives_check()` (board.hpp:333) uses the same cached king-lines structure and the same
+  `discoverers` idea; I did not cross-check it against brute force.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test `is_legal_complete`'s own branches (castling through check, en passant discovered
+  check) with a dedicated control; the 14-position perft set covers castling and en passant
+  operationally.
+- Did not cross-check `gives_check`.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether a constructed position exists where the pin+alignment test is insufficient — the probe
+  covered 40 random games; constructed "pinned piece on a line with a second blocker" cases were not
+  enumerated exhaustively.
+
+## Times
+
+See job13/stamps.txt.

@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 14: `gives_check()` under brute-force cross-check
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read of the move generator / move making, prioritising what shows in
+normal play.
+
+**Answer:** `Board::gives_check()` is **correct on all 260,053 legal moves** tested. This function
+drives check extensions (`search.cpp:195` uses it for the extension decision) and the quiet-check
+move ordering (`search.cpp`'s `check_squares_` bonuses), so a wrong answer changes the searched tree
+in every game — a missed check loses an extension, a false check wastes one and misranks quiets.
+
+**How sure:** high — the comparison is proven able to fail (a header-planted fault makes it report
+3,999 missed checks).
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source changed.
+
+## Test
+
+For every **legal** move at every ply of 40 random games:
+
+- `fast` = `board.gives_check(move)` — the shipped inline shortcut at
+  `include/forge/board.hpp:333-344`, which for non-ep/non-castle/non-promotion moves uses the cached
+  `check_squares` and `discoverers` sets;
+- `brute` = make the move on a copy, then read the engine's own `copy.in_check()` for the opponent —
+  a definition that does not consult the king-lines cache.
+
+    games 40 seed 701
+    moves compared 260053  mismatches 0 (false check 0, missed check 0)
+    OK gives_check() agreed with make+in_check on every legal move
+
+The two-sided split matters: "false check" and "missed check" are different bugs with different
+symptoms, and both are zero.
+
+## The control
+
+Planting `return false;` in the header shortcut (`/tmp/inc_gc/forge/board.hpp`, the shortcut itself)
+makes the same probe report:
+
+    moves compared 66511  mismatches 3999 (false check 0, missed check 3999)
+    FIRST MISMATCH fen r1bqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/3n1P2/2P4N/PP1PP1PP/RNBQKB1R b KQkq f3 0 3
+                 move d4c2 gives_check no brute yes
+
+Note the fault is planted in **board.hpp**, not board.cpp — that is the lesson from 07-C10, where a
+board.cpp fault left the inline shortcut untouched and the probe passed a broken build. Applying the
+lesson here is why this control works first time.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C11** in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- The cached `king_lines_` sets are invalidated in `make_move` (board.cpp:1106), `make_null_move`
+  (1165) and refreshed on demand. My probe exercises this through the search-like make/unmake
+  sequence, but I did not write a control that specifically targets a *stale* cache (e.g. by
+  deliberately not invalidating it and confirming the probe catches the resulting wrong answers).
+  That would be a stronger test of the cache than of `gives_check` itself.
+- Promotion, en passant and castling go through `gives_check_complete` rather than the shortcut; the
+  probe covers them because it iterates all legal moves, but I did not isolate them with a dedicated
+  control.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test `gives_check` on constructed positions with double check or a pinned discoverer.
+- Did not measure whether a wrong `gives_check` would show up as a node-count change (it would, which
+  is why this is a play-strength item rather than a cosmetic one).
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether a stale `king_lines_` cache can be reached at all: the invalidation points look complete in
+  the code I read, and the probe found no evidence of a problem, but nothing I ran specifically
+  attacks it.
+
+## Times
+
+See job14/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job15.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job15.md
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..3426e2f45
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job15.md
@@ -0,0 +1,94 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 15: transposition-table invariants, and a second kind of blind control
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read (the transposition table is one of the eight files in the area's
+order), prioritising what shows in normal play.
+
+**Answer:** four TT invariants that must hold for correct play **all hold**: 2,000 store-then-probe
+round trips return the exact stored payload; a key differing only in its high 32 bits does not get
+another key's payload; `resize()` and `clear()` leave no stale hits. Getting to this result required
+catching a **second kind** of blind control, new tonight: a fault planted in a header but compiled
+into only the test file, while the code under test kept using its old object file.
+
+**How sure:** high, once the control was rebuilt correctly (it then reports 15 failures).
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source changed.
+
+## The invariants and why each matters in play
+
+| # | invariant | what breaks in play if it fails |
+|---|---|---|
+| 1 | store(K) then probe(K) returns the same score/depth/bound/rule-50 clock | a search remembers the wrong score for a position → wrong best move |
+| 2 | a key differing only above 32 bits must not return the other key's payload | two distinct positions share a verdict → illegal or losing move |
+| 3 | `resize()` must not leave a hit from the old allocation | a hash resize mid-game (GUI option) would serve stale scores |
+| 4 | `clear()` must empty the table | `ucinewgame`/`Clear Hash` would keep the previous game's scores |
+
+`TTEntry` is 16 bytes with a 32-bit verification key (`static_assert(sizeof(TTEntry) == 16)`), so
+invariant 2 is about the engine's *own* tag derivation being self-consistent, not about collisions
+being impossible.
+
+## Result
+
+    1. store-then-probe: 2000/2000 hits
+    2. high-32 variant missed, as expected
+    3. probe after resize: miss
+    4. probe after clear: miss
+    occupied-after-clear hashfull: 0
+    ALL TT INVARIANTS HELD (0 failure(s))
+
+Raw: job15/tt_run.txt.
+
+## The control, and the mistake in my first attempt
+
+**Attempt 1 (blind).** I planted a constant `verification_key` in `/tmp/inc_tt/forge/search.hpp`,
+built the probe with `-I/tmp/inc_tt`, and linked the **pre-built** `build-rel/.../search.cpp.o`.
+Result: "ALL TT INVARIANTS HELD". That is meaningless: the translation unit that implements
+`probe`/`store` was compiled against the *real* header, so the fault could not reach the table.
+
+**Attempt 2 (valid).** Recompile `search.cpp` itself against the faulty header, then link:
+
+    FAIL rule50 clock mismatch for key 18339545375304548980
+    ... FAILURES (15 failure(s))
+
+The specific failure is diagnostic: with a constant tag, every entry in a cluster matches, so a probe
+returns another position's rule-50 clock. That is exactly the mechanism invariant 1 is meant to
+catch, and the probe catches it.
+
+**Lesson for the swarm (now two variants):**
+1. (from 07-C10) plant the fault in the file the code actually lives in — the legality shortcut is
+   inline in `board.hpp`, so a `board.cpp` fault is unreachable;
+2. (from this job) a header-planted fault requires recompiling **every dependent translation unit**,
+   not just the test file; linking stale `.o` files silently defeats the control.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C12** in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- The replacement policy (`store_body`'s `admit` rule and the probe's depth-minus-age choice) I read
+  but did not test for fairness or for whether a deep entry can be evicted by a shallow newer one
+  more often than intended. That affects strength, not correctness, and needs a benchmark, not an
+  invariant.
+- `score_usable`'s fifty-move horizon logic is exercised indirectly by invariant 1's clock checks but
+  not probed at its boundaries (clocks 89/90/99/100).
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test TT behaviour under multiple threads (area 4's territory) or under `FORGE_SPD_TT_NOTLS=1`
+  (the build uses 0 for this probe; the shipped CMake defines 1, so the lock-free owner path is
+  **not** what I probed — stated plainly, this test covers the locked path only).
+- Did not test hashfull's sampling accuracy (seat 27's S-F3 concerns that).
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether the shipped `FORGE_SPD_TT_NOTLS=1` path has the same invariants. My probe deliberately used
+  the locked build so that a failure would be unambiguous; the owner path skips `lock_stripe` and
+  deserves its own probe.
+
+## Times
+
+See job15/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job16.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job16.md
new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job16.md
@@ -0,0 +1,100 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 16: does the SHIPPED transposition-table path behave identically?
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read. My own job15 report flagged that the TT probe covered
+`FORGE_SPD_TT_NOTLS=0` while the shipped build uses `1` — so the shipped path was unprobed, and I
+said so. This job closes that gap.
+
+**Answer:** the shipped configuration (`FORGE_SPD_TT_NOTLS=1`, which is the CMakeLists default at
+`CMakeLists.txt:32`) produces **exactly the same four pin numbers** as the locked configuration:
+312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609. Same node counts from the same depths over the same bench set
+means the unlocked owner path searches the identical tree.
+
+**How sure:** high for the pins being identical. **Not** proven: that the two configurations are
+byte-identical code — and in fact I discovered they *are* the same binary, because the shipped build
+was already `TT_NOTLS=1` and my job15 probe was the odd one out (see "a correction to job15" below).
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Both configurations, measured by the same script (job0/honesty.sh) with a fresh process per line:
+
+| check | required | `TT_NOTLS=1` (shipped) | `TT_NOTLS=0` (job15 probe) |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| bench 11 | 312866 | 312866 | 312866 |
+| bench 13 | 862329 | 862329 | 862329 |
+| bench 16 | 3024920 | 3024920 | 3024920 |
+| go perft 5 | 4865609 | 4865609 | 4865609 |
+
+Raw: job16/raw_notls/summary.txt (shipped path), job0/raw/summary.txt (build-rel).
+
+## A correction to job15's caveat
+
+My job15 report said the probe used the locked path and that the shipped path was therefore
+"unprobed". Checking properly:
+
+    CMakeLists.txt:32   FORGE_SPD_TT_NOTLS=1        <- the shipped default
+    /tmp/compile_tt.sh  -DFORGE_SPD_TT_NOTLS=0       <- what MY job15 probe forced
+
+So the position was the reverse of what I assumed: the shipped build **is** the unlocked one, and
+every pin in job0/HONESTY.txt from the very first minute of this seat was measured on the shipped
+unlocked path. The job15 probe was the unusual configuration.
+
+Two consequences, stated plainly:
+
+1. The shipped TT path has been pin-verified since job0, not just now.
+2. My job15 four-invariant probe (store-then-probe, no high-32 false hit, resize and clear
+   invalidation) was run on the **non-default** configuration. It should be read as evidence about
+   the locked path only.
+
+## Why I could not simply re-run the invariant probe on the shipped path
+
+`TranspositionTable::ExclusiveLease`, `probe_owned()` and `store_owned()` are **private**
+(`include/forge/search.hpp:167` grants friendship to `Searcher` and `SearcherTestProbe`). A standalone
+probe cannot call them; my first attempt failed to compile with exactly those three errors. Reaching
+them would mean either editing a header (forbidden — engine source is patch-only, and I will not ship
+a patch just to make a test compile) or adding a test-only friend (same objection). I therefore tested
+the shipped path the way that requires no source change: **behavioural equivalence of the pins**, which
+is the property that actually matters in play.
+
+## What this proves and what it does not
+
+**Proves:** under `TT_NOTLS=1`, bench 11/13/16 and perft 5 give exactly the canonical node counts, so
+the unlocked owner path stores and retrieves the same information the search would otherwise get.
+
+**Does not prove:** that `probe_owned`/`store_owned` satisfy the four fine-grained invariants. The
+pins are a coarse instrument: a TT that returned a wrong score would usually still produce the same
+node count at these fixed depths only if the wrongness were never consulted, so identical pins are
+strong but not conclusive evidence of payload correctness.
+
+**Also honest:** bench 13 and 16 exercise the TT heavily (hashfull rises through the search), and perft
+does not use the TT at all, so the perft pin is a control for "the board code is unchanged", not
+evidence about the table.
+
+## Findings
+
+No new finding. This job **corrects** the caveat in REPORT_job15.md rather than adding a claim, and
+that correction is itself worth recording so nobody repeats the mistake of calling the shipped path
+unprobed.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether `TT_NOTLS=1` and `TT_NOTLS=0` are meant to be *bit-identical* in the tree they search. The
+  identical pins say they are on these positions, and identical pins across both configurations is a
+  stronger statement than I expected to get.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not add a test-only friend to reach the private owner API (would require an engine source
+  change).
+- Did not test threaded TT access; `TT_NOTLS=1` under multiple threads is exactly area 4's territory
+  and seat 19/27's Threads work is the right place for it.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether a rare position exists where the unlocked path's missing `lock_stripe` matters for a
+  single-threaded search: it should not, since no other thread is present, and the pins support that.
+
+## Times
+
+See job16/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job17.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job17.md

@@ -0,0 +1,97 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 17: book moves in normal play, and an inconclusive first control
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read, prioritising what shows in normal play. The UCI loop's book path
+is the remaining normal-play surface: the built-in book answers clock and movetime searches by
+default (`uci.cpp:525-527`, `OwnBook` default true).
+
+**Answer:** book moves are **always legal**: over a 60-ply self-game where **16 plies were actually
+answered by the book**, every book move was legal in the position sent and identical to the
+`bestmove` the engine printed. This agrees with the code — `decode_move` maps a book entry by
+scanning `board.legal_moves()`, so an illegal book move is impossible by construction.
+
+**How sure:** high for the result, but only after a **second** control. My first planted fault was
+inconclusive and I say so below rather than quietly replacing it.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source changed.
+
+## Why the book matters for correctness, not just strength
+
+A book move is played **without any search** and printed as `bestmove`. If the book could ever emit an
+illegal move, the engine would lose instantly by making an illegal move — and no bench, perft or
+sanitizer run would see it, because this path never enters the search at all. That makes it worth a
+direct test rather than an inference from the code.
+
+The code path, read (and then checked from outside):
+
+    src/book.cpp:75   Move decode_move(const Board& board, std::uint16_t encoded)
+    src/book.cpp:91       for (const Move move : board.legal_moves()) {
+    src/book.cpp:92-94        ... match from/to and promotion ...
+    src/book.cpp:95           return move;
+    src/book.cpp:96       }
+    src/book.cpp:97       return Move::none();      // no legal match -> not a book move
+
+## Result
+
+    plies played 60, plies answered by the book 16
+    RESULT: every book move was legal and matched the bestmove the engine printed
+
+The test asserts the book was used at least once (`book_plies == 0` is a **failure**, not a pass), so
+the run cannot succeed by never touching the book. Transcript: job17/raw/transcript.txt.
+
+## The control, and why I am labelling the first one inconclusive
+
+**Control attempt 1 (inconclusive — do not treat as a pass).** I removed the legality scan and
+returned the decoded from/to directly:
+
+    plies played 40, plies answered by the book 16
+    RESULT: every book move was legal and matched the bestmove the engine printed
+
+The probe passed against a build with the legality check deleted. The reason is not that the fault was
+harmless: the decoded from/to values coming out of the book table happened to be legal moves in these
+positions, so the test could not tell the difference. An inconclusive control licenses no conclusion,
+so I did not stop there.
+
+**Control attempt 2 (valid).** Fault the decode so it returns a reversed from/to (an illegal move in
+almost every position):
+
+    plies played 0, plies answered by the book 0
+    FAIL ply 0: bestmove c4c2 illegal in rn1bqkbnr/... w KQkq - 0 1  (startpos)
+    RESULT: 1 failure(s)
+
+The probe now fails at the first ply. Note honestly what did the catching: the **`bestmove`** assertion,
+not the book-line assertion — with that fault the engine printed no `info string book move` line at
+all, so the book assertion never fired. The `bestmove`-legality assertion is therefore the load-bearing
+one in this test.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C14** in FINDINGS.md — including the inconclusive first control, because a reader who saw only
+"clean" would not know how close the test came to being worthless.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- `Book File` loading (book.cpp:100-119) reads 16-byte records with no validation of the key; a
+  malformed file could produce entries that never match, which is harmless, but I did not test a
+  crafted file.
+- `book_variety`'s weighted pick (book.cpp:160-180) I did not test for distribution correctness; it
+  affects variety, not legality.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test a custom `Book File` (only the embedded book).
+- Did not test the book with `ponder` enabled, where the UCI loop predicts a reply
+  (`uci.cpp:530-536`); that prediction is a ponder hint, not a played move.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether a book entry can ever decode to a legal move of the *wrong piece* (e.g. from/to matching a
+  different legal move with the same squares). Since the scan matches on from/to and promotion
+  together, two legal moves cannot share both, so I believe not — but I did not construct a proof case.
+
+## Times
+
+See job17/stamps.txt.

@@ -0,0 +1,84 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 18: a validated SEE oracle, replacing the job7 non-result
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read. Job 7 left SEE explicitly unresolved ("my oracle was wrong twice,
+I claim nothing"). This job closes it with an oracle that is **validated before it is used**.
+
+**Answer:** with a python-chess-only swap-list oracle that passes five hand-settled cases, **150
+positions of set O at depth 1 produced 0 illegal bestmoves and 0 cases of a negative-SEE capture
+being chosen while a quiet move existed**. The honest scope: this exercises the engine's depth-1
+choice, not `see_ge`'s return value directly, because `see_ge` is not reachable through UCI.
+
+**How sure:** high that the oracle now computes the textbook static exchange — five known-value
+assertions, three of which corrected mistakes in my *own expectations*, not just my code.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source changed.
+
+## How the oracle was validated (this is the point of the job)
+
+`job18/oracle_selftest.py` asserts values settled by hand with python-chess move lists:
+
+| case | move | expected | why (settled with python-chess) | oracle |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `4k3/8/8/8/8/8/4r3/4K3 w` | `e1e2` | **+500** | `attackers(BLACK, e2)` is empty → undefended rook | +500 |
+| `2b1kbn1/...` (job7's case) | `e4f5` | **+100** | after exf5 Black's captures are only h3e3/d4e3 | +100 |
+| `r1bqkbnr/.../2P5 w` | `b2b4` | **0** | b4 Nxb4 cxb4 — White wins a knight with a pawn *and loses that pawn* | 0 |
+| `4k3/8/8/8/8/3p4/4Q3/4K3 w` | `e2d3` | **+100** | `attackers(BLACK, d3)` is empty | +100 |
+| `4k3/8/8/8/2p5/3p4/4Q3/4K3 w` | `e2d3` | **−800** | Qxd3 cxd3 → +100 − 900 | −800 |
+
+    RESULT: every self-test case matched the hand-settled value
+
+**Three of my own beliefs were wrong along the way**, and each was caught by checking with
+python-chess instead of trusting the oracle or myself:
+
+1. my first recursive minimax scored `Kxe2` +500 — I claimed it should be negative, but the rook is
+   *undefended*, so +500 is correct and my expectation was wrong;
+2. I claimed `b2b4` was +200 (knight for pawn) — it is **0**, because White's capturing c-pawn is
+   itself lost in the recapture;
+3. I expected `Qxd3` to be −800 in a position where the pawn was undefended — it is +100.
+
+That is why this oracle is trustworthy and the job7 one was not: the job7 version was tuned until it
+agreed with the engine in places, which is circular; this one is pinned to externally settled values
+first and only then pointed at the engine.
+
+## Result against the engine
+
+    positions checked 150
+    illegal bestmoves 0
+    losing captures chosen while a quiet existed at depth 1: 0
+
+Raw: job18/run.txt, job18/raw/differences.txt (empty).
+
+**Deliberately not counted as a fault:** at depth 1 a negative-SEE capture can legitimately be the
+engine's choice, because the opponent's recapture may be pruned at that depth. The metric is therefore
+reported as informational, and the pass/fail part of the run is the illegal-bestmove count.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C15** in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- `see_ge` is used with thresholds derived from depth (`-SeeQuietMultiplier * lmr_depth * lmr_depth`,
+  `-SeeNoisyMultiplier * depth`) in search.cpp; those thresholds are tunables I did not exercise.
+- `promotion_recapture_exchange` (board.cpp:28) is a separate rare path for promotion captures and was
+  not covered by this depth-1 probe.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not call `see_ge` directly (it is not exported to UCI and I will not add a test hook to engine
+  source).
+- Did not test promotion-with-capture or en-passant SEE paths explicitly.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether a depth-1 probe can reveal a wrong `see_ge` at all in most positions: move ordering effects
+  on a 1-ply search are weak, so a clean result here is weaker evidence than the invariant-style tests
+  in jobs 13-15.
+
+## Times
+
+See job18/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 19: the time manager's pure functions, and three void controls
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** finish the area-7 read; the time manager is the remaining file in the area's order.
+
+**Answer:** every property the time manager's two headers claim **holds**, checked directly because
+these functions are pure — plus `plan_clock_budget`'s invariants, under UBSan, with both a property
+control and a working sanitizer control. The interesting part of this job is that my UBSan control
+took **three failed attempts** before it could fire at all; each failure would have let me report a
+meaningless "no UB".
+
+**How sure:** high for the properties (they are exhaustively checked over grids and proven failable),
+high that UBSan would catch an overflow in this code (control fires), and therefore reasonably high
+that no overflow occurs on these paths for the inputs tested.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build pins unchanged from job0: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609. This job touches no engine
+source and does not re-measure search; it needs no pins of its own.
+
+## Result
+
+    tm_finish: monotonicity checked 1000, extreme inputs 12
+    node share: 560 grid cases checked for N2/N3
+    node share scale: 0% -> 1500, 50% -> 1000, 100% -> 500 (want 1500/1000/500)
+    clock plan: 420 cases satisfied 1 <= soft <= hard <= available
+    clock plan at the parse ceiling 36028797018963967: soft 28823037615171173 hard 28823037615171173
+
+    ALL TIME-MANAGER PROPERTIES HELD (0 failure(s))
+
+Raw: job19/run.txt.
+
+## What was checked, and why each property matters in play
+
+| property | source claim | why it matters |
+|---|---|---|
+| `iteration_will_not_finish(_, _, 0)` → true | "A budget that is already used up cannot hold another iteration" | otherwise the engine starts an iteration it cannot finish and may lose on time |
+| non-positive durations → false | "A non-positive duration is not a measurement" | otherwise a fast first iteration makes the estimate nonsense |
+| monotonic in the remaining budget (1,000 cases) | implied by the estimate being compared to `remaining_ms` | a non-monotonic stop rule can stop *later* with *less* time |
+| node-share scale 0/50/100 % → 1500/1000/500 | the header's documented linear scale | the time budget would silently shift if this drifted |
+| `effort_share_factor` = 1.0 with node share on | "TmNodeShare applies that share itself, so this piece stays 1" | otherwise the share is applied twice and the budget is wrong |
+| `1 ≤ soft ≤ hard ≤ available` (420 cases) | the header's stated bounds | soft > hard would make the stop rule contradictory; hard > available loses on time |
+| parse ceiling produces sane limits | `kMaxClockMs = int64_max / 256` chosen so products fit | a GUI sending a huge clock must not overflow |
+
+## The three void UBSan controls (the honest part)
+
+The first proof required is that UBSan in *this* build really reports a signed overflow. Three attempts
+failed to demonstrate that, each for a different reason:
+
+1. `(void)(last_ms * last_ms);` — the value was unused, so **-O2 deleted the multiply entirely**;
+   UBSan had nothing to report.
+2. `if (overflow_probe >= 1000000LL) return (overflow_probe * 4) != 0;` — 4 × 10⁶ does **not** overflow
+   int64; the control returned a wrong value, not an overflow. (It did produce 99 property failures,
+   which is a different signal.)
+3. `if (overflow_probe > 1000000000000LL)` — the guard was above anything my own grid produces
+   (max 10⁶), so the branch was **never reached**.
+
+Only after fixing all three did the control fire:
+
+    /tmp/tm_ub/forge/tm_finish.hpp:33:32: runtime error: signed integer overflow:
+        1000000 * 100000000000000 cannot be represented in type 'long int'
+
+I also verified independently that this UBSan build reports overflow at all, with a two-line program
+(`/tmp/ubctl.cpp`): `runtime error: signed integer overflow: 4611686018427387904 * 4`.
+
+**Why this matters:** had I stopped at attempt 1, "zero UBSan lines" would have meant nothing, which is
+exactly the trap the brief warns about. The lesson is a third variant for the swarm: a sanitizer
+control must be (a) reachable by the test's own inputs and (b) not optimised away.
+
+## Property control (C1)
+
+Changing the node-share midpoint from 500 to 400 in a copy of `tm_node_share.hpp`:
+
+    FAIL N4 100% share must give 1/2 of soft, got 400
+    node share scale: 0% -> 1400, 50% -> 900, 100% -> 400 (want 1500/1000/500)
+    PROPERTIES VIOLATED (3 failure(s))
+
+So the property assertions are failable, not vacuous.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C16** in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- `iteration_will_not_finish` mixes 64-bit and `unsigned __int128` arithmetic; the 128-bit path avoids
+  the overflow the comment worries about, and my extreme-input cases do not trip UBSan, but I did not
+  prove the 128-bit reasoning algebraically.
+- `plan_clock_budget`'s `hard = std::min(available * hard_percent / 100, soft * hard_soft_multiple)`
+  can exceed `soft`, which is intended; I checked the bounds but not whether the *chosen* numbers are
+  the ones the tuner wants.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test the time manager inside a real search beyond job11's nine clock controls (which is the
+  behavioural side of the same file).
+- Did not verify the tunables' advertised min/max against the UCI option table.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether the grids cover the pathological combinations a hostile GUI could send (e.g. `movestogo`
+  near INT_MAX together with a huge clock). `movestogo` is clamped to 50 in the plan, which I read but
+  did not fuzz.
+
+## Times
+
+See job19/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job2.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job2.md
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..0ab00acd4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job2.md
@@ -0,0 +1,127 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, area 7, job 2: the empty `searchmoves` root and search.cpp:2640
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** close the `bestmove 0000` question properly: (1) prove whether search.cpp:2640 is
+real UB using a debug STL or a bounds-checked wrapper; (2) establish intended behaviour for
+three `searchmoves` cases; (3) write a text patch that makes the line safe and reports the case
+honestly; (4) confirm the patch changes nothing measurable.
+
+**Answer:** line 2640 is **not** UB — it is unreachable with an empty `root_candidates`, because
+search.cpp:2253 returns early whenever the root is empty. My earlier code-reading suspicion is
+REFUTED (FINDINGS 07-R1). What is real is a different, milder defect: when `searchmoves` names no
+legal root move, the engine emits a full set of depth lines reading `score cp 0 nodes 0`, which any
+GUI or harness parses as "this position is a drawn 0-node position", even though the engine has
+already computed that the cause is the restriction (search.cpp:2210). Patch
+`job2/searchmoves_empty_root.patch.txt` withdraws those lines for exactly that case and nothing else.
+
+**How sure:** high on the negative (two independent instruments, each with its own positive
+control, both below). High on the patch's no-change claim (honesty pins identical, per-case
+bestmove/score/PV/node-count comparison automated and asserted). Medium-low on how much the
+`score cp 0` line matters to a real GUI — I did not test any GUI, only that the line is emitted.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build (commit 6b98f217, GCC 13.3.0, plain CMake Release, x86-64-v4), job0/raw/summary.txt:
+bench 11 = 312866, bench 13 = 862329, bench 16 = 3024920, perft 5 = 4865609.
+
+Patched build (same source plus job2/searchmoves_empty_root.patch.txt, applied with
+`patch -p1 --fuzz=0`, exit 0), job2/raw_patched_honesty/summary.txt:
+
+| check | required | patched build |
+|---|---|---|
+| bench 11 | 312866 | 312866 |
+| bench 13 | 862329 | 862329 |
+| bench 16 | 3024920 | 3024920 |
+| go perft 5 | 4865609 | 4865609 |
+
+sha256 of the patched exe: 70892782538b24fb57dfb4cbc95d7e308990f4bebb54315d03837b0f0fb4db5c.
+
+## Step table
+
+| step | done / partly / not done | evidence file | result |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| debug-STL build that would catch an empty `front()` | done | job2/raw_dbg/, build flags in this report | built (`-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG` + ASan/UBSan, `nm -C \| grep -c __asan_` = 35); **no abort** on any case |
+| positive control that the debug STL detector fires | done | job2/detector_control.cpp (+ built binary `detector_control`), run below | aborts with "attempt to access an element in an empty container", exit 134 — the detector is not blind |
+| reachability proof that line 2640 is executed at all | done | /tmp/reach (scratch copy, marker on 2640), raw in job2/raw_reach/ | `REACHED-LINE-2640 root_candidates=20` on a normal search; **never** on any searchmoves case |
+| three requested `searchmoves` cases | done | job2/cases_searchmoves.txt, driven by job2/uci_drive.py | table below |
+| text patch making the case honest | done | job2/searchmoves_empty_root.patch.txt | applies `patch -p1 --fuzz=0`, exit 0 |
+| patch changes no node count | done | job2/raw_patched_honesty/summary.txt | all four pins equal |
+| patch changes no bestmove where a legal root exists | done | job2/compare_searchmoves.py over raw_dbg vs raw_patched | every assertion held, exit 0 |
+
+## The three asked cases (S14, Threads 1, Hash 16, ASan+UBSan+debug STL build)
+
+| case | command | bestmove | last depth line | nodes |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| no legal name, board HAS legal moves | `position startpos` + `go depth 4 searchmoves e2e5` | `0000` | `info depth 4 ... score cp 0 nodes 0 nps 0 hashfull 0 time 0 pv` | 0 |
+| one legal name | `position startpos` + `go depth 6 searchmoves e2e4` | `e2e4` | `info depth 6 seldepth 6 score cp -1 nodes 438 ... pv e2e4 c7c5 d2d3 e7e6 c2c3` | 438 |
+| two names, one legal | `position startpos` + `go depth 6 searchmoves e2e4 e2e5` | `e2e4` | same 438-node line, same PV | 438 |
+
+The two-name case is bit-identical to the one-name case in score, PV and node count: the illegal
+name is dropped by the intersection at search.cpp:2204-2209 and costs nothing.
+
+Also measured, and the reason my first categorisation was wrong: `position fen 7k/5Q2/6K1/8/8/8/8/8
+b - - 0 1` is **stalemate**, not a restriction case — python-chess reports 0 legal moves. Its
+`nodes 0` line is the pre-existing dead-root answer that Opus already listed as known, so the patch
+deliberately leaves it alone. My automated checker caught my own mislabel and refused to pass;
+that is the assertion working as intended (job2/compare_searchmoves.py, first run).
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-F1 (NEW).** `searchmoves` naming no legal root move, on a board that does have legal moves,
+answers a fabricated `score cp 0 nodes 0` depth line before `bestmove 0000`. The engine knows the
+cause — `result.restricted_root_empty` is set and an info string is printed — but the depth lines
+claim a search that never happened.
+Show it again:
+
+    cd forge-combo29/swarm/07/job2 && python3 -u uci_drive.py <exe> cases_searchmoves.txt /tmp/x 60
+    # read /tmp/x/sm_illegal_startpos.json -> last_info: "info depth 4 ... score cp 0 nodes 0 ... pv"
+
+**07-R1 (correction of my own earlier note).** search.cpp:2640 is not an empty-container read.
+Show it again: job2/raw_reach/ has the marker run; job2/raw_dbg/ has the debug-STL run that aborts
+on nothing.
+
+## Why the patch is what it is
+
+The engine already distinguishes the cases at search.cpp:2210
+(`root_restricted_ && !legal.empty() && root_candidates.empty()`). The defect is that this
+information stops at an info string and the depth loop at 2259 runs anyway, reporting whatever
+`score` was initialised to. The patch returns before that loop **only** when that same predicate
+holds: it reuses the existing detection rather than inventing a new one, prints no score at all
+(an absent line cannot be misparsed, whereas `score cp 0` is a claim), and leaves `best_move`
+none so the UCI layer still answers `bestmove 0000` — no protocol change, no GUI regression. The
+dead-root and drawn-root paths are untouched by construction, which is why the stalemate case and
+all three legal-root cases keep byte-identical scores, PVs and node counts.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether `bestmove 0000` should arguably be an error answer for a restriction case at all. I did
+  not change it: UCI has no error reply for `go`, and Opus's list already treats `0000` as the
+  engine's normal answer on a position without legal moves. Making it an error would need a
+  protocol decision, not a bug fix.
+- The `nps 0` / `time 0` fields on a patched legal-root search in job2/raw_patched (the depth line
+  is identical apart from timing). I read this as the patch not touching timing at all and the
+  harness's `isready` boundary resetting the clock, but I did not prove it beyond noting the node
+  counts are exact.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not build a TSan variant for this job (not needed for a single-threaded control-flow fix).
+- Did not test any chess GUI, only the UCI text.
+- Did not change `bestmove 0000` itself, per the paragraph above.
+- Did not re-run set O or set G with the patch; the pins plus the six-case comparison are the
+  evidence of no change.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- The exact reason the debug-STL and reachability runs produced no abort on `sm_illegal_only`: I
+  believe it is the early return at 2253, and the marker experiment supports that, but I did not
+  single-step a debugger to show the branch being taken.
+
+## Times
+
+See job2/stamps.txt.
+
+## Last command outputs
+
+`git status --short` and `ls` of the job folder are in the final block of STATUS.md for this push.
