@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 20: increment-heavy clock plans, and a share worth a human's judgement
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** finish the area-7 read; job19's clock-plan arithmetic raised a question about
+increment-heavy time controls that only a real clock game can answer.
+
+**Answer:** the plan **never loses on time** in five increment-heavy controls (160 plies), but it is
+**aggressive**: with `movestogo 40`, a 1000 ms clock and a 1000 ms increment it will spend up to
+**79.6 %** of the remaining clock on one move (average 36.6 %). I am reporting that as a
+behavioural observation for Opus to judge, **not** as a fault, because the increment refunds the
+time and no control lost on time.
+
+**How sure:** high on the measurement (real decrementing clock, real increment, per-move wall times in
+job20/raw/). Deliberately *not* claiming it is wrong — I have no evidence the policy is unintentional,
+and the header documents the increment term.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build pins unchanged (job0/raw/summary.txt: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609). No engine
+source changed; this job measures behaviour only.
+
+## The arithmetic, from the code
+
+include/forge/clock_plan.hpp, movestogo branch:
+
+    soft = available / (mtg + 1) + increment * 3 / 4
+    hard = std::min(available * 4 / 5, soft * 4)
+
+For `wtime 1000 btime 1000 winc 1000 binc 1000 movestogo 40`, with the default 10 ms Move Overhead:
+available = 990, so soft = 990/41 + 1000·3/4 = **24 + 750 = 774**, hard = min(792, 3096) = **792**.
+
+That is 78 % of the usable clock for one move out of forty. It is bounded (`hard ≤ available`), and
+the increment returns 1000 ms afterwards, so it is not obviously wrong — it is aggressive.
+
+## Result
+
+    inc_eq_clock_mtg40     plies  40  max share of clock  0.796  average  0.366  losses 0
+    inc_eq_clock_sudden    plies  30  max share of clock  0.599  average  0.271  losses 0
+    inc_gt_clock           plies  30  max share of clock  0.598  average  0.344  losses 0
+    inc_half_clock_mtg40   plies  40  max share of clock  0.494  average  0.184  losses 0
+    inc_tiny_clock         plies  20  max share of clock  0.582  average  0.341  losses 0
+
+    RESULT: no loss on time in any increment-heavy control; shares reported above
+
+Per-move tables (ply, remaining clock, wall time, share, lost): job20/raw/<control>.txt.
+
+## Why I am not filing this as a finding
+
+Three reasons, stated so a reader can disagree with me:
+
+1. `hard ≤ available` holds in every case I checked (420 grid cases in job19 plus these games), so the
+   engine cannot exceed its own clock from this arithmetic alone.
+2. The increment is refunded **after** the move; spending 774 ms of a 990 ms clock with a 1000 ms
+   increment leaves the clock higher than it started.
+3. The term is explicitly in the code with a documented meaning (`increment * 3 / 4` in the movestogo
+   branch, `increment * increment_percent / 100` in the sudden-death branch), so it looks intended.
+
+What I *can* say is that a 0.8 share of the clock on one move is the kind of policy that shows up as
+time-trouble losses in fast games against strong opponents, and Opus is better placed than I am to
+judge whether that is the intent.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C17** in FINDINGS.md — clean result plus the recorded share.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether the increment term should be capped relative to `available`. Not proven either way.
+- `Move Overhead` default 10 ms is subtracted once per move; at 50 ms clocks that is already 20 % of
+  the budget, which is why `inc_tiny_clock` shows a 0.582 peak share.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not run these as games against an opponent, so I cannot say whether the aggressive policy wins
+  or loses games — only that it does not lose on time.
+- Did not vary `TmSoftDivisor` / `TmIncrementPercent` tunables.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether a real GUI's measured clock differs from my model (I decrement by measured wall time, which
+  is a fair model of a GUI that starts the clock at `go`).
+
+## Times
+
+See job20/stamps.txt.

@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 21: check of seat 27's S-F7 (the UCI option surface)
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** (cycle step 2a) check another seat's NEW finding that nobody has checked, reproducing it
+from its claim with a harness of my own. I searched all the seats I could fetch and found **no** C
+line for 27-S-F7, so it was unclaimed.
+
+**Answer:** **CONFIRMS** 27-S-F7 — the UCI option surface really does match its advertisement — on a
+wider sweep than the original: **82 advertised options, 437 setoption cases, 0 in-range values
+refused, 0 advertised options reported unknown**, and a control that fails the check when a handler
+is missing.
+
+**How sure:** high. The check reads the advertised list from the engine itself (so it cannot go stale
+against a changed option table) and the control proves the failure mode is detected.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build pins unchanged (job0/raw/summary.txt: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609). No engine
+source changed; the fault build is a copy at `/tmp/optfault`.
+
+## The claim, and what my harness does differently
+
+Seat 27's claim: *"The UCI option surface matches its advertisement: all 81 advertised options
+exercised with 291 setoption cases give 0 refusals of an advertised min/max value and 0 `unknown
+option` lines."*
+
+I wrote my own harness rather than re-running theirs. It:
+
+1. parses the `option name ... type spin/check/string/button ... min ... max ...` lines out of the
+   engine's own `uci` answer (82 options here);
+2. for every spin option sends **min, max, min−1, max+1, a word, and no value**;
+3. for every check option sends **true, false, `yes`, and no value**;
+4. for every string option sends **`<empty>` and no value**;
+5. for every button sends **no value**;
+6. after each, sends `isready` and reads **every line up to `readyok`**, then classifies.
+
+Classification, with the two bug classes separated:
+
+- **ACCEPTED** — no complaint;
+- **CLAMPED** — `info string invalid value for option <name>`, which is the engine's documented
+  behaviour for out-of-range and non-numeric values;
+- **REFUSED-VALID** — a complaint for a value *inside* the advertised range → would refute S-F7;
+- **UNKNOWN** — `info string unknown option <name>` for an *advertised* name → would also refute it.
+
+## Result
+
+    advertised options 82, cases 437
+      ACCEPTED: 163
+      CLAMPED: 274
+      REFUSED-VALID: 0
+      UNKNOWN: 0
+    RESULT: CONFIRMS 27-S-F7 - every advertised option was recognised and every in-range value was
+            accepted; out-of-range and junk values were reported as the engine documents
+
+Raw: job21/raw/summary.txt, which also lists every advertised option with its type, default, min and
+max so a later seat can diff the surface if it changes.
+
+## The control
+
+A copy of the tree that **advertises an option it does not handle** — `PhantomOption`, added to the
+`uci` answer only:
+
+    UNKNOWN: 6
+    BUG UNKNOWN for advertised option [PhantomOption] value [1] :: info string unknown option PhantomOption
+    ... (same for 10, 0, 11, word, no-value)
+    RESULT: REFUTED - 0 valid value(s) refused, 6 advertised option(s) unknown
+
+So the `UNKNOWN` class is detected when it exists.
+
+**Second control, run later in the same job because I had flagged the first one's gap.** I made
+`apply_spin` refuse each spin option's advertised **maximum** — a value that is inside the advertised
+range, which is precisely the `REFUSED-VALID` class:
+
+    BUG REFUSED-VALID [NullMoveDepthDivisor] value [10] (inside advertised range 1..10 for spin) :: info string invalid value for option NullMoveDepthDivisor
+    BUG REFUSED-VALID [RfpDepth], [RfpMargin], [RazorDepth] ... (one line per spin option, 58 in total)
+    RESULT: REFUTED - 58 valid value(s) refused, 0 advertised option(s) unknown
+
+So **both** bug classes are now proven detectable: 6 UNKNOWN detections from the phantom-option
+build, and 58 REFUSED-VALID detections from the refuse-max build. With both controls in hand the
+437-case clean result is meaningful in both directions, not just one.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C19** in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- The `REFUSED-VALID` half of the check is unproven by a control (see above). It is also the half that
+  would matter most for a tuner: an in-range value silently clamped would corrupt a tuning run.
+- My sweep sends one value per case; it does not test values exactly at the boundary of the *stored*
+  type (e.g. a spin whose C++ type is `int` but whose advertised max is near INT_MAX).
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test options during a running search (that is 27-S-F9's territory).
+- Did not verify that each accepted value actually *takes effect*; only that it is not refused. S-F7
+  is about the surface, and effect is a different claim.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether seat 27's 81st option was the `Clear Hash` button or one I parse differently; my parser counts
+  82 and lists them all in the summary, so the discrepancy is visible rather than hidden.
+
+## Times
+
+See job21/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 22: does the boolean `NonPawnCorrection` option actually take effect?
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read of the UCI loop. My job9 result (all four S14 sums exact) proves
+the spin options reach the search, but S14 also relies on **one boolean** option,
+`NonPawnCorrection`, which `uci.cpp` handles through a different branch. So the sums did not prove
+that particular flag applies.
+
+**Answer:** it does. Same position, same depth, cold, only the flag differing:
+**false → 56,720 nodes (cp 30)**; **true → 33,066 nodes (cp 29)**. A silently ignored flag would
+produce identical numbers.
+
+**How sure:** high. Difference is large and reproducible in one cold process each.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build pins unchanged (job0/raw/summary.txt: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609).
+**Cross-check:** the `false` figure, 56,720 nodes, is exactly the cold-start number seat 10
+independently reported for this engine — two seats, two harnesses, same number.
+
+## Why this needed its own test
+
+    uci.cpp:289   for (const forge::tune::Parameter& parameter : forge::tune::parameters()) { ... apply_spin ... }
+    uci.cpp:403   } else if (name == "ContHist4PlyRead" || name == "NonPawnCorrection" || ... ) {
+    uci.cpp:407       bool* target = name == "ContHist4PlyRead" ? &forge::tune::ContHist4PlyRead
+    uci.cpp:408                    : name == "NonPawnCorrection" ? &forge::tune::NonPawnCorrection ...
+
+The tunable table holds **spins only**; every boolean goes through a name-comparison chain and a
+`bool*` lookup. A typo in that chain (or a bool missing from it) would silently ignore the option and
+leave the S14 configuration un-reproduced in a way a *sum* would catch only if the option mattered —
+and if it does not matter, the sum would hide the bug.
+
+## Result
+
+    NonPawnCorrection false: nodes 56720 score ('cp', 30)
+    NonPawnCorrection true : nodes 33066 score ('cp', 29)
+    RESULT: the flag measurably changes the search, so it takes effect
+
+Raw: job22/raw/result.txt.
+
+## What this does and does not prove
+
+**Proves:** the bool branch applies `NonPawnCorrection` for the S14 value (`true`).
+
+**Does not prove:** that the other ten booleans in that same `else if` chain apply. The chain shares
+its structure, and job21's option-surface check confirmed every advertised name is *recognised* (no
+`unknown option`), but "recognised" and "assigned to the right variable" are different claims: a
+`bool* target` mis-wired to the wrong variable would be accepted silently. Testing each of the
+eleven by effect is the natural follow-up, and I state the gap rather than imply coverage.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C20** in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- The `bool* target` ternary chain (uci.cpp:407-421) assigns by name; a mismatch between the `if`
+  condition's name list and the ternary's name list would route one option to the wrong flag. I read
+  both lists and they appear to match for all eleven names, but I did not verify by effect for the
+  other ten.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test the other ten boolean options by effect (see above).
+- Did not test `TmNodeShare`/`TmFinishIteration`, which only matter under a running clock.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether the 56,720 → 33,066 change is all from `NonPawnCorrection` or partly from a hash/cache
+  interaction; each run was a fresh process with `ucinewgame`, so I believe it is the flag alone.
+
+## Times
+
+See job22/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job24.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job24.md

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,116 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 24: `LmrSignedCorrection` is dead code
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** the area-7 read continued into the UCI option surface. Job 23 verified every boolean
+option **by effect** and found five that changed nothing; four were explainable (they only matter on
+a clock, or in a dead-material position), but **`LmrSignedCorrection`** should have mattered and did
+not.
+
+**Answer:** `LmrSignedCorrection` **can never have any effect.** Its adjustment arithmetic computes
+`delta = correction_cp / 64` from a quantity that is mathematically bounded to `[-32, 32]`, so
+`delta` is always **0**, and the function returns the untouched reduction. This is a real defect — an
+advertised, tunable, gated option that is inert — though a *harmless* one: turning it on does not
+make the engine worse, it does nothing.
+
+**How sure:** proven two independent ways — an exhaustive enumeration of the whole reachable
+`(correction, reduction)` space, and an end-to-end measurement showing identical node counts with the
+option off and on at three searches. Plus a control showing the arithmetic *would* bite if the
+divisor were smaller.
+
+## The defect, exactly
+
+    include/forge/search.hpp:389   constexpr int CorrectionGrain = 256;
+    include/forge/search.hpp:390   constexpr int CorrectionLimit = 32 * CorrectionGrain;   // 8192
+    include/forge/search.hpp:362   inline int apply_lmr_signed_correction(int reduction_plies, int correction_cp) {
+    include/forge/search.hpp:363       int delta = correction_cp / 64;      // <-- always 0
+    include/forge/search.hpp:366       const int adjusted = reduction_plies - delta;
+    include/forge/search.hpp:367       return adjusted > 0 ? adjusted : 0;
+
+    src/search.cpp:1226   return std::clamp(raw_eval + correction / CorrectionGrain, ...);
+    src/search.cpp:2005   const int correction_cp = ss->static_eval - ss->raw_eval;
+
+The chain: `corrected_eval` adds `correction / 256` to the raw eval, so
+`correction_cp = static_eval - raw_eval = correction / 256`. With `correction` clamped to ±8192,
+`correction_cp` is confined to **±32**. Then `32 / 64 == 0` in C++ integer division, for every
+possible correction, positive or negative.
+
+`src/search.cpp:2006` guards with `if (correction_cp != 0)`, so the call is sometimes made — but the
+call cannot change `r`.
+
+## Proof 1: exhaustive over the reachable space
+
+job24/lmrdead.cpp copies the constants and the function verbatim and enumerates every reachable
+`correction` in `[-8192, 8192]` against every reduction `0..30`:
+
+    correction range [-8192, 8192]
+    correction_cp range [-32, 32]
+    values of correction giving a NONZERO delta: 0
+    (reduction, correction) pairs where the reduction CHANGES: 0 of 507935
+
+**Control:** changing only the divisor, `/64` → `/8`, gives
+
+    values of correction giving a NONZERO delta: 12290
+    (reduction, correction) pairs where the reduction CHANGES: 374845 of 507935
+
+so the zero is a property of the chosen constant, not of my enumeration.
+
+## Proof 2: end-to-end, the node count does not move
+
+job23/run.log, cold process each time, startpos `go depth 12`:
+
+    LmrSignedCorrection      false   56720  true   56720  NO EFFECT
+
+and extended on purpose to deeper and non-starting positions:
+
+    LmrSignedCorrection    midsgame d14 : false 149295 true 149295 NO EFFECT
+    LmrSignedCorrection    stpos d16    : false 267839 true 267839 NO EFFECT
+
+For contrast, options that *do* work in the same harness: `ThreatHistory` 56720→32209,
+`EvasionOrdering` 56720→28490, `AspArmLate` 56720→29009, `SoundMatePruning` 56720→80946,
+`EvalRule50Damp` 56720→62247, `UseNNUE` 68426→56720.
+
+## A repair, as a text patch (NOT applied, and NOT honesty-neutral)
+
+The obvious repair is to divide by a constant small enough to act — `/8` would make
+`correction_cp = -4..4` give `delta = 0..1`. **I did not write that patch**, deliberately:
+
+- any change to this function changes the search tree, so it would fail the brief's requirement that
+  a patch keep the honesty numbers identical (312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609);
+- a repair therefore needs a strength test against a real opponent, which is Fable/Opus's call, not a
+  text patch I can validate here.
+
+What I can say is that the *current* code is inert, so the tuner's reported optimum for
+`LmrSignedCorrection` — whatever it is — was measured with an option that did nothing. Anyone tuning
+it again should know that before spending games on it.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-F2** in FINDINGS.md — my second real finding, and the first that is purely a defect rather than
+a reporting issue.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether the intended divisor was `/8` or whether `correction_cp` was meant to be the raw
+  `correction` (in which case `/64` would give a range of ±128, still mostly saturated by the ±1
+  clamp). Both readings are guesses; I did not find a commit that shows the intent.
+- `NullThreatVerify` also showed no effect at startpos d12 but **does** differ on a middlegame at d14
+  (149295 → 149315) and at startpos d16 (267839 → 267855), so it is live — a depth/position
+  coincidence, not a defect. Recorded so nobody re-reports it.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not fix `LmrSignedCorrection` (reasons above).
+- Did not test `TmFinishIteration`, `TmNodeShare` or `DeadMaterial` further; the first two need a
+  running clock (`time_managed_` is false for `go depth`) and `DeadMaterial` needs a drawn-material
+  position, so their null result on this harness is expected rather than suspicious.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether some other caller reaches `apply_lmr_signed_correction` with a `correction_cp` outside the
+  range I derived. `grep` shows exactly one call site, `search.cpp:2006`, fed by
+  `ss->static_eval - ss->raw_eval` at line 2005, so the bound holds.
+
+## Times
+
+See job24/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job25.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job25.md
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..dec42b46f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job25.md
@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 25: 07-F2 WITHDRAWN — the repository already documented this option
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** search the repository for any record of `LmrSignedCorrection` having been tuned, and
+report it: evidence of tuning means quote it in FINDINGS; absence means say the absence supports the
+reading that the option was added and never activated.
+
+**Answer:** **there is a record, and it refutes my own finding 07-F2.** `forge-combo29/REPORT_r3_03.md`
+is a full report on this option; it states the very arithmetic I got wrong, records the divisor being
+deliberately changed from `/8` to `/64` in a follow-up, and explains why the option does not move the
+depth-13 bench tree. The repository also ships a unit test for the function. **07-F2 is withdrawn in
+full (07-R2).**
+
+**How sure:** very high — the refutation is a quoted document in the tree plus a unit test with
+`{3, 64, 2, "64cp better subtracts one ply"}` among its cases, and I re-derived the bound by hand and
+in code.
+
+## Where my proof was wrong
+
+07-F2 enumerated **one** correction table:
+
+    per-table cap: 32 cp
+
+and concluded `correction_cp ∈ [-32, 32]`, so `correction_cp / 64 == 0` always. But
+`corrected_eval` (`src/search.cpp:1217-1226`) builds `correction` as a **sum**:
+
+    std::int32_t correction = pawn_table[...];
+    if (MaterialCorrectionWeight > 0) correction += material_table[...] * weight / 100;
+    if (NonPawnCorrection)            correction += (np_w + np_b) / 2;
+    return std::clamp(raw_eval + correction / CorrectionGrain, ...);
+
+So the reachable bound is the sum, not one table:
+
+    default tables summed (pawn + material): 64 cp
+    with NonPawnCorrection (pawn + material + avg of 2 nonpawn): 96 cp
+    reachable (reduction, correction_cp) pairs where the reduction CHANGES: 2013 of 5983
+
+At ±64 cp the step is exactly one ply, so the option is **live** — just rarely. That is precisely what
+the existing report says.
+
+## The record, quoted
+
+From `forge-combo29/REPORT_r3_03.md`:
+
+- line 78: *"The previous adjustment subtracted `correction_cp / 8` with no cap, so a large
+  correction moved the reduction by several plies. The follow-up rule subtracts `correction_cp / 64`,
+  rounded toward zero, then limits that adjustment to -1..+1."*
+- line 79: *"A correction inside -63..+63 centipawns changes nothing."*
+- line 87: *"bench 13 with `LmrSignedCorrection` on: 862329. The same count as option off. A one-ply
+  step needs 64 centipawns, and each correction table caps at 32, so the step happens only when the
+  pawn and material corrections are both saturated on the same side. That did not change the
+  depth-13 bench tree."*
+- line 49 (an earlier build, divisor /8): *"bench 13: 1244366 nodes ... The count differs from 862329,
+  so the option is live."*
+- line 10: *"It was not tuned for strength, and this report does not claim a strength result."*
+
+And the unit test `forge-combo29/tests_r3_03/lmr_signed_correction_test.cpp` asserts the intended
+behaviour directly, including `{3, 64, 2, "64cp better subtracts one ply"}` and
+`{3, 1000, 2, "a large positive correction is limited to one ply"}`.
+
+## What I checked at the end to be sure
+
+Re-ran the exact command the report used, on my build:
+
+    bench 13 with LmrSignedCorrection ON : nodes 862329
+    bench 13 with LmrSignedCorrection OFF: nodes 862329
+
+Identical — matching the report's own line 87. So the observation was right; my *explanation* of it
+(dead code) was wrong.
+
+## Answer to the question the owner actually asked
+
+**Whether to delete the option or repair the divisor:** neither, on this evidence. The divisor was
+already repaired once (from `/8` to `/64`, documented in the same file), the current constant was
+chosen deliberately with its consequence stated, and the option can act when the correction tables
+saturate together. **The option should be left alone**, and `REPORT_r3_03.md` is the document to read
+before touching it.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-R2** in FINDINGS.md, and the 07-F2 row is rewritten to say WITHDRAWN in its first words so a
+reader scanning the table cannot pick up the dead conclusion.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether the option ever fires in real games on this build. Its inertness on bench 13 is documented;
+  its frequency elsewhere is not, and no strength result was claimed by the original report either.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not re-run the original screening matches (`screen_r3fu_03/`); the report itself says they are
+  screening, not a strength claim.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Nothing that affects this withdrawal: the record, the code and my re-run all agree.
+
+## Times
+
+See job25/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 26: the PC r15 build, verified against its own numbers
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** fetch `handoff/fable-opus-combo29-all-20261114`, read `FABLE_TO_swarm_5.md` before the next
+step, build the PC's engine from the patch it carries in a SEPARATE copy with
+`-DFORGE_MATE_ALPHA_GUARD=1`, and check the bench numbers it must give.
+
+**Answer:** built and **all eight published numbers match exactly**, in all three regimes the file
+distinguishes. Patch sha256 verified before use.
+
+**How sure:** very high — the numbers are exact integer matches in a fresh process per line, and the
+file itself tells us a mismatch would mean a wrong regime, so I checked all three.
+
+## Patch provenance
+
+    source:  forge-combo29/soak_all/FABLE_TO_swarm_5.md on handoff/fable-opus-combo29-all-20261114
+    block:   the fenced diff, from its first `diff` line to its last line
+    bytes:   2319 lines
+    sha256:  d6bd72c531f785f40421be1cc542743922a944fb0973d05831788440309c1a1a
+    expected prefix per file 5: d6bd72c531f785f4   -> MATCH
+
+Applied in a **separate worktree** (`/agent/repos/pcbase`, base `6b98f217`) so the copy I build the
+base engine from is untouched, exactly as instructed. `patch -p1` reported **11 files** and no rejects.
+
+Build: `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-DFORGE_MATE_ALPHA_GUARD=1` with g++ 13.3.0,
+`-j4`. The flag is required: without it `MateAlphaGuard` does not exist and PC20 would print
+`unknown option`.
+
+## Results (Threads 1, Hash 16, one fresh process per line)
+
+| settings | check | got | published | |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| none (no setoption at all) | bench 11 | 312866 | 312866 | OK |
+| none | bench 13 | 862329 | 862329 | OK |
+| none | bench 16 | 3024920 | 3024920 | OK |
+| none | go perft 5 | 4865609 | 4865609 | OK |
+| S14 (14 settings) | bench 11 | 242796 | 242796 | OK |
+| S14 | bench 13 | 656517 | 656517 | OK |
+| PC20 (S14 + 6) | bench 11 | 278024 | 278024 | OK |
+| PC20 | bench 13 | 587276 | 587276 | OK |
+
+No `unknown option`, `invalid value` or `ERROR` line appeared in any regime, which is the second thing
+file 5 asks to be checked (every option name must exist in the exe's own `uci` list).
+
+Raw: job26/raw/pc_pins.json.
+
+## Why the three-regime check matters
+
+File 4 records that the pins are **default-option** numbers while the known node sums are taken **under
+S14**, and that seat 10 saw a false mismatch by mixing them. File 5 adds a third regime, PC20. So the
+same build legitimately gives three different bench-13 values (862329 / 656517 / 587276) and all three
+are correct in their own regime. Checking only one would have left the others unproven, and a reader
+could easily think one of them is a bug.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C21** in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- The S14 bench 11 figure here (242796) matches the number seat 10 measured on the **base** tree, which
+  suggests the S14 settings dominate that measurement; I did not test why they coincide.
+- PC20's six extra options are all exercised for existence, but only `MateAlphaGuard` and `OwnBook`
+  are boolean/simple; `HistRework` takes 0..3 and I set 2 as specified without testing other levels.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test the new search options' behaviour (CuckooRep, HistRework, TtPruneV2, CorrHistV2) beyond
+  confirming the engine accepts them and that PC20 reproduces its numbers.
+- Did not touch evaluation-dependent results; the PC plays with its own trained net which is not shared
+  (file 5), so the built-in evaluation remains, and file 2's rule 2 applies.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether any of the PC patch's FORGE_FIX_* switches other than the defaults documented are on in this
+  build. I built exactly as instructed and the pins match, so the configuration is the intended one.
+
+## Times
+
+See job26/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 29: the PC-tree patch for 07-F1, and proof it cures the defect on r15
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** (cycle work) 07-F1 was found on the base tree. Since it survives on the PC build under PC20
+(07-C22), the useful next step is a patch that fixes it **there**, with its published numbers intact.
+
+**Answer:** the base-tree patch does **not** apply to the PC tree (hunk 3 conflicts with the
+`FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN` block), so I wrote a **separate PC-tree patch**, three edits, applying cleanly
+with `patch -p1 --fuzz=0`. On the patched PC build: **all eight published numbers unchanged**, the
+empty-root cases go from **64 zero-node depth lines to 0**, `bestmove 0000` still returned, and every
+control behaves exactly as before — including the 19-F12 abort case, which this patch deliberately
+does not touch.
+
+**How sure:** high. Pins are exact; before/after behaviour is measured with the same harness; the
+controls in the same run are unchanged.
+
+## Why a second patch was needed
+
+    base tree: hunk 1 at 2200, hunk 2 at 2208, hunk 3 at 2256   -> applies with --fuzz=0
+    PC tree  : hunks 1 and 2 succeed with offset +321, hunk 3 FAILED at 2260
+
+The PC tree wraps the drawn-root score in `#if !FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN ... #endif`, so the anchor text
+for hunk 3 moved. Rather than weaken the patch with fuzz, I regenerated it against the PC tree's own
+text.
+
+## The patch (job29/job29_pc_searchmoves_empty_root.patch.txt)
+
+Three edits, identical in intent to the base patch:
+
+1. a local `bool restricted_root_empty = false;` beside `root_candidates`;
+2. `restricted_root_empty = result.restricted_root_empty;` right after the existing detection at
+   search.cpp:2531 — reusing the engine's **own** predicate, not inventing one;
+3. inside the empty-root branch, before the depth loop: return without emitting any depth line, with
+   `result.nodes` and `result.elapsed_ms` still filled in.
+
+`best_move` is left `none` on purpose, so the UCI layer keeps printing `bestmove 0000` exactly as
+before — no protocol change, nothing for a GUI to relearn.
+
+## Results on the patched PC build (PC20, Threads 1, Hash 16)
+
+Pins — every published number still exact:
+
+    none  bench11 312866  bench13 862329  bench16 3024920  perft5 4865609
+    S14   bench11 242796  bench13 656517
+    PC20  bench11 278024  bench13 587276
+
+Behaviour — the defect is gone, the controls are untouched:
+
+| case | before | after |
+|---|---|---|
+| 07-F1 `go searchmoves e2e5` | `0000`, **64** zero-node depth lines | `0000`, **0** depth lines |
+| no-match + node budget | `0000`, **64** zero-node depth lines | `0000`, **0** depth lines |
+| 19-F12 `go depth 12` + quit | `a2a3`, 0 depth lines | `a2a3`, 0 depth lines (**unchanged, different path**) |
+| control `searchmoves e2e4` | 33 depth lines, 50,224,817 nodes | identical |
+| discriminator 2a/2b/2c/2d | 21600 / 11458 / 17308 / 11191 nodes | identical |
+
+## What this proves and what it does not
+
+**Proves:** 07-F1 exists on the PC build and a three-edit patch removes the fabricated score line
+without moving a single node count on any published bench, and without disturbing the abort path.
+
+**Does not prove:** that the owner wants this behaviour. Withdrawing the depth line is a judgement:
+I chose "print no score at all" over "print a score with the real explanation", because an absent line
+cannot be misparsed while `score cp 0` is a false claim. `REPORT_job2.md` argues this from the code
+(2210/2531 already detects the state); Opus may still prefer a different presentation.
+
+**Also not proven:** that this is the only remaining instance of the pattern. 07-C22 shows the abort
+path at 3017 is a *different* fallback, and I have not patched that one.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C22** (three reported symptoms = two paths) and **07-C23** (this patch, verified on r15).
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- The 19-F12 fallback (`root_candidates.front()` at 3017) answers a legal move with no score. That is
+  arguably acceptable for an aborted search, but seat 19's report and my discriminator both show the
+  move is the *first in generation order*, which is not a searched move. Whether that deserves a fix
+  is a judgement I have not made.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not patch the 19-F12 path.
+- Did not test the patch under ASan/UBSan on the PC build (the change is three lines of control flow
+  with no arithmetic; the base patch's reasoning carries over, but I did not re-run the sanitizer).
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether the owner's PC build has other divergences from this patched copy (file 5 says the patch
+  reproduces the PC source byte for byte, and my pins match, so I believe not).
+
+## Times
+
+See job29/stamps.txt.

@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 3: check of seat 17's finding S-F2
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** (area 7, cycle step 2a) check a NEW finding by another seat that nobody has checked
+yet, reproducing it from its command file, with a harness of my own.
+
+**Answer:** checked **17-S-F2**, which claims `src/search.cpp:2640` reads `front()` of an EMPTY
+`MoveList` when `root_candidates` is empty but legal moves exist. **REFUTED.** Line 2640 never
+executes with an empty root, because search.cpp:2253 returns early whenever
+`root_candidates.empty()`. The *symptom* 17-S-F1 describes (an illegal `bestmove 0000` after
+`searchmoves`) is real, and I measured it myself; the *cause* is not a `front()` on an empty list
+but the fabricated `score cp 0 nodes 0` depth line emitted at search.cpp:2259. That is my 07-F1.
+
+**How sure:** high. Both instruments carry their own positive control in this same report, so
+"nothing happened" means the code path does not exist rather than that the detector is blind.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build, job0/raw/summary.txt: bench 11 = 312866, bench 13 = 862329, bench 16 = 3024920,
+perft 5 = 4865609. The two builds used here are the same source with extra flags:
+`build-dbg` (`-D_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS -D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG -fsanitize=address,undefined`,
+`nm -C | grep -c __asan_` = 35) and `/tmp/reach/build-dbg` (same plus a stderr marker at 2640).
+
+## Step table
+
+| step | done / partly / not done | evidence file | result |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| read 17-S-F2's own command file | done | `git show FETCH_HEAD:forge-combo29/swarm/17/job1/finding_searchmoves.py` | it is a *symptom* script; the S-F2 cause claim is a `sed`/code-reading claim with no test |
+| harness of my own (never a copy) | done | job3/cases_17sf2.txt + job3/check_17SF2.py, driving job2/uci_drive.py | every `go` is followed by reading until `bestmove` |
+| instrument A: container check | done | job3/raw_dbg/, verdict in check_17SF2.py stdout | **no abort on any case** |
+| instrument A positive control | done | job2/detector_control.cpp (compiled with the same flags) | aborts: "attempt to access an element in an empty container", exit 134 |
+| instrument B: reachability marker | done | job3/reach_2640.py over /tmp/reach/build-dbg, raw in job3/raw_reach2/ | **0 hits with size 0**; positive control fires at size 20 |
+| instrument B positive control | done | case `control_plain_nodes` in cases_17sf2.txt | `REACHED-LINE-2640 root_candidates=20` |
+| guard precondition (marker really in the binary) | done | reach_2640.py runs `strings` first and exits if absent | marker present; script refuses to report otherwise |
+
+## What the engine actually answers (ASan + debug STL build, S14, Threads 1, Hash 16)
+
+| case | command | bestmove | depth line | nodes |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 17's empty-root case | `position startpos` + `go depth 5 searchmoves e7e5` | `0000` | `info depth 5 seldepth 5 score cp 0 nodes 0 nps 0 hashfull 0 time 0 pv` | 0 |
+| garbage name | `position startpos` + `go depth 5 searchmoves zzzz` | `0000` | same 0-node line | 0 |
+| legal control | `position startpos` + `go depth 5 searchmoves e2e4` | `e2e4` | `info depth 5 seldepth 5 score cp 23 nodes 252 ... pv e2e4 c7c5 c2c3 e7e6` | 252 |
+| mate position | `... b KQkq - 0 4` + `go depth 5 searchmoves a7a6` | `0000` | 0-node line | 0 |
+| black to move, White's move named | `... b KQkq - 0 1` + `go depth 5 searchmoves e2e4` | `0000` | 0-node line | 0 |
+| empty list | `position startpos` + `go depth 5 searchmoves` | `0000` | 0-node line | 0 |
+
+## Why 2640 is unreachable-empty (the mechanism, with lines)
+
+    search.cpp:2203  MoveList root_candidates;            // filled by the restriction intersection
+    search.cpp:2210  result.restricted_root_empty = root_restricted_ && !legal.empty() && root_candidates.empty();
+    search.cpp:2253  if (root_candidates.empty() || root_drawn) { ... return result; }   // <-- the guard
+    search.cpp:2459  if (!result.pv.empty()) result.best_move = result.pv.front();
+    search.cpp:2640  if (result.best_move.is_none()) result.best_move = root_candidates.front();
+
+Every path that reaches 2640 has passed 2253 with a non-empty `root_candidates`. The marker run
+confirms this empirically: the only hit in the whole matrix is `go nodes 5`, where the search stops
+before any iteration publishes a PV, so 2460 leaves `best_move` none and 2640 fills it in from a
+root that is (correctly) size 20.
+
+That last observation is a small extra: line 2640 is what makes `go nodes 5` answer `a2a3`, the
+first legal move in generation order — consistent with seat 27's S-F2, which I have not checked.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C1 — REFUTES 17-S-F2, CONFIRMS the symptom of 17-S-F1.** In FINDINGS.md.
+Show it again:
+
+    cd forge-combo29/swarm/07/job3 && python3 -u reach_2640.py /tmp/reach/build-dbg/forge /tmp/reachcheck
+    # expects: control_plain_nodes marker hits=1 sizes=[20]; all s17_* cases 0 hits
+    python3 -u check_17SF2.py /agent/repos/base/forge-combo29/build-dbg/forge /tmp/dbgcheck
+    # expects: aborted False on every case
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- I did not examine seat 17's own build or flags, so I cannot say whether their `front()` claim came
+  from a build whose `root_candidates` could actually be empty (e.g. an older commit). I refuted the
+  claim against 6b98f217, the commit the brief pins.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not re-check 17-S-F1's GUI-facing argument (whether a GUI should treat `0000` as an error).
+- Did not check seat 27's S-F2 (`go nodes` below one iteration), only noticed that 2640 explains it.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether 2640 can be reached with an empty root on any input at all. I covered the searchmoves
+  family, mate/stalemate roots and the node-budget path; I did not exhaustively enumerate
+  `MultiPV` + `searchmoves` + clock combinations.
+
+## Times
+
+See job3/stamps.txt.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job31.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job31.md
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..81827a872
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job31.md
@@ -0,0 +1,87 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 31: what `bestmove 0000` should mean, and the one-candidate boundary
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** (1) state in the patch header the design choice about `bestmove 0000`, recommend an answer
+and its consequence for a GUI, as seat 12 did for the abort fix; (2) then the C-series re-checks, and
+if time remains test whether the early branch prints a score when the restriction names a move that
+IS legal but leaves exactly one candidate.
+
+**Answer:** all four candidate answers measured, recommendation and its GUI consequence written into
+the patch header. The one-candidate boundary is **handled correctly** — a legal single candidate is
+searched normally on both builds.
+
+**How sure:** high; every number is from a fresh process, Threads 1, Hash 16, and the recommendation
+rests on measurement (A/B/C) rather than taste.
+
+## The design question, measured on startpos (20 legal moves), `go depth 6 searchmoves e2e5`
+
+| | answer | depth lines | nodes |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **A** unpatched | `bestmove 0000` | 6, all `score cp 0 nodes 0` | 0 |
+| **B** this seat's patch | `bestmove 0000` + `info string searchmoves restriction has no legal root moves` | **0** | 0 |
+| **C** full-root search | `bestmove d2d4` | 6, real | **1703** |
+| **D** no answer | — | — | GUI hangs |
+
+C was measured by running the same engine **without** the restriction, which is exactly the answer C
+would give; no second engine was needed to state its consequence.
+
+## The recommendation, in one sentence
+
+**Ship B.** A fabricated score is a defect; an honest `0000` is not. B changes nothing a GUI does
+today — the GUI already received `0000` in A — it removes the false score, not the move.
+
+**If the owner wants a playable move instead**, that is a *separate* decision and it must announce
+itself: `bestmove d2d4` plus `info string searchmoves matched no legal move; searched the full root`.
+A GUI must never be handed a move outside the set it asked for without being told.
+
+D is rejected for the same reason seat 12 rejected it in S-F11: a GUI that never receives a
+`bestmove` is worse off than one that receives a poor answer.
+
+## Why B rather than C, though C is friendlier
+
+`searchmoves` exists so a caller can **forbid** moves — it is how a training or analysis harness
+restricts the root. Silently searching the full root would produce a move the caller explicitly
+excluded, which is a louder lie than an honest "I could not honour your restriction". B keeps the
+engine truthful and leaves the policy choice where it belongs, with whoever sent the restriction.
+
+## The one-candidate boundary (asked second)
+
+| case | base 6b98f217 | PC r15 + patch, PC20 |
+|---|---|---|
+| `searchmoves e2e4` on startpos | `e2e4`, 6 depth lines, **438** nodes | `e2e4`, 6 depth lines, **344** nodes |
+| `searchmoves f3e5`, a real capture, single candidate | `f3e5`, 6 depth lines, **138** nodes | `f3e5`, 6 depth lines, **175** nodes |
+
+Both nonzero on both builds, so a one-candidate legal restriction is **not** routed through the
+empty-root branch. The branch keys on `root_candidates.empty()`, i.e. on emptiness rather than on
+smallness — which is the correct criterion, and this is the boundary that would have exposed it if
+the implementation had used a size test like `size() <= 1`.
+
+**Honest note on my own test:** my first version used `position startpos moves e2e4 e7e5 g1f3` with
+`searchmoves f3e5`, where it is **Black** to move, so `f3e5` was never legal and the harness printed a
+false warning. python-chess showed the move illegal and the case was corrected. Nothing in the final
+table depends on the bad case.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C24** (the design answer) and **07-C25** (the boundary) in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether any GUI actually acts destructively on `0000` in a live position. Seat 12 asserts some may
+  resign, adjudicate or crash; I did not test a GUI, only reasoned from the UCI meaning of `0000`.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not implement option C (ignore the restriction), by choice — it needs the owner's decision.
+- Did not test a restriction that names one legal move *plus* several illegal ones beyond the two
+  cases above.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether a training harness (the PC's own use of `searchmoves`) would prefer C. If the PC's loop
+  restricts the root for label quality, C could be actively harmful there; that is an argument for B.
+
+## Times
+
+See job31/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 34: how broad is the PC's search change? (per-position, not aggregate)
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** report the **per-set** difference between PC20 and S14 rather than one aggregate, so a later
+seat can see which positions changed and by how much — that is what tells the owner whether the PC's
+search changes are broad or narrow.
+
+**Answer:** **broad and systemic.** Every one of the 200 positions changed node count; 60 of 200
+changed bestmove; 195 of 200 changed score.
+
+**How sure:** high — both sides were re-measured with the *same* driver and schema, and the base leg
+reproduced the published 9,500,069 exactly, which is the check that the comparison is sound.
+
+## The two runs being compared
+
+| side | build | settings | sum |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| base | 6b98f217 | S14 | **9,500,069** (matches the published value, 07-C3) |
+| PC | r15 | PC20 | **8,315,168** (07-C26) |
+
+Both: Threads 1, Hash 16, one fresh process per position, `ucinewgame` + `isready` before every `go`,
+set O (200 positions), depth 12.
+
+Difference: **−1,184,901 nodes** on the PC side.
+
+## Per-position result
+
+    positions where the node count changed : 200 of 200   (100.0%)
+      increased on PC                      :  74
+      decreased on PC                      : 126
+      identical                            :   0
+    positions where the BESTMOVE changed   :  60 of 200   ( 30.0%)
+    positions where the SCORE changed      : 195 of 200   ( 97.5%)
+
+    delta nodes:  min -69,363   median -4,888   max +76,082   mean -5,924
+    |delta|     :  median 11,684   90th pct 30,949   max 76,082
+
+## What "broad" means here, concretely
+
+There is **no subset of positions that is untouched**. A localised change would show a cluster of
+identical rows and a cluster of changed rows; this run has 0 identical rows out of 200. That is what
+one expects from a build that alters move-ordering history, correction history and pruning together —
+it changes nearly every tree, and the totals happen to land 12 % lower because more positions got
+cheaper (126 down) than dearer (74 up), not because a few positions changed a lot.
+
+The largest single movers, for anyone wanting to look at a specific tree:
+
+| index | position | base → PC nodes | Δ | bestmove |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 143 | `r1bqkb1r/ppp1nppp/3p1n2/3Pp3/2P1P3/2N2N2/PP3PPP/R1BQ…` | 27,342 → 103,424 | **+76,082** | `e7g6` → `h7h6` |
+| 87 | `r1bqkb1r/pppp1p1p/5np1/4p3/2BnP3/3P4/PPP2PPP/RNBQK1N…` | 115,882 → 46,519 | **−69,363** | `b7b5` → `d7d5` |
+| 80 | `rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3p3b/2PP4/2N2N1P/PP2PPP1/R1BQK…` | 137,007 → 67,696 | **−69,311** | `d1b3` → `g2g4` |
+
+Full table: job34/raw/sum_delta.txt (all 200 rows with fens, node counts, deltas and any bestmove
+change) and job34/raw/sum_delta.json.
+
+## The caveat I am not hiding
+
+The two runs differ in **both** build and settings (base+S14 vs PC+PC20). So each per-position delta is
+a property of the **pair of configurations the owner actually uses**, not of the PC's search alone.
+Separating build from settings needs two further full runs — base under PC20, and PC under S14 — which
+I did not complete in this job. A reader should not read these deltas as "what the PC patch changed";
+they are "what the owner's configuration differs by".
+
+## The one unexplained base-vs-PC difference, and it is a good one (07-C29)
+
+A 20-case sweep under identical settings found five differences. Four map to switches file 5 names.
+The fifth, `8/P6k/8/8/8/8/8/K7 w` at `go depth 10`, had no named cause:
+
+    base          a1a2    cp 1067   21,093 nodes
+    PC            a7a8q   cp 1124   36,405 nodes
+
+Isolated by rebuilding a scratch copy with each `FORGE_FIX_*` switch **alone**:
+
+| switch alone | result |
+|---|---|
+| `FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN` | a1a2 / 1067 / 21093 — same as base |
+| `FORGE_FIX_HARD_LIMIT_EMERGENCY` | a1a2 / 1067 / 21093 — same as base |
+| **`FORGE_FIX_BARE_KING_LMR_CAP`** | **a7a8q / 1124 / 36405 — exactly the PC answer** |
+
+With all three off the build matched base exactly. So this difference is that single cap, and **the
+PC's answer is the better one**: it promotes immediately instead of shuffling the king. That is the
+bare-king reduction cap doing its job on a promotion race that the base tree's reduction was hiding —
+a small independent confirmation that the PC's bare-king work helps in at least one position.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C28** (per-position breadth) and **07-C29** (the isolated, benign difference).
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether the 30 % of positions with a changed bestmove are better or worse on the PC. Measuring that
+  needs games, which is not area 7's job and not something a node count can answer.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not run base+PC20 or PC+S14 sums, which is what would separate build from settings (stated above).
+- Did not investigate the remaining score changes; 97.5 % of positions changing score is consistent
+  with a systemic ordering change and needs no per-position account.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether some of the 200 deltas are inflated by clock-free depth-12 searches hitting different
+  aspiration orders; I did not control for that, and it would not change the breadth conclusion.
+
+## Times
+
+See job34/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 35: closing the build-vs-settings caveat, and which PC20 option earns its keep
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** (1) run the two missing legs so the four together make the deltas attributable, and say how
+much of the 12 % is the patch and how much is the settings; (2) then the 20-case differential at 100
+cases.
+
+**Answer (1):** the split is **not additive — it is an interaction**. Base and PC both give exactly
+**9,500,069** under S14, and **100 %** of the −1,184,901 needs the patch *and* the PC20 options
+together. Saying "the patch accounts for X, the settings for Y" would be arithmetically wrong, and the
+four legs show why: the base build cannot even honour PC20 (it answers `unknown option` for all five
+PC-only options).
+
+**Answer (2):** in progress below (the differential at 100 positions).
+
+**How sure:** very high for (1) — three legs are identical integers, which is not a coincidence that
+noise can produce. Threads 1, Hash 16, fresh process per position, `ucinewgame` before every `go`.
+
+## The four legs (set O, depth 12, Threads 1, Hash 16)
+
+| build | settings | sum | note |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| base | S14 | **9,500,069** | matches the published value |
+| base | PC20 | **9,500,069** | but the base **rejects** CuckooRep, HistRework, TtPruneV2, CorrHistV2, MateAlphaGuard (`unknown option`, verified one by one), so this leg is really S14 |
+| PC r15 | S14 | **9,500,069** | **identical to base** — the patch alone changes nothing here |
+| PC r15 | PC20 | **8,315,168** | the only leg that differs |
+
+    settings effect on BASE (S14 -> PC20): 0        (cannot apply them)
+    settings effect on PC   (S14 -> PC20): -1,184,901
+    build effect at S14  (base -> PC)    : 0
+    build effect at PC20 (base -> PC)    : -1,184,901   (but base "PC20" == S14)
+
+The cleanest single sentence: **on this 200-position set at depth 12, the PC patch's fixes move no
+nodes at all, and the whole difference is the PC-only options acting on the patched search.** They
+need each other, so the honest statement is an interaction, not a split.
+
+That is also consistent with 07-C29: the one base-vs-PC difference found in the 20-case sweep was
+caused by `FORGE_FIX_BARE_KING_LMR_CAP`, on a **promotion race** — a behaviour fix, not a
+tree-shape fix.
+
+## Which PC20 option actually does the work (07-C31)
+
+PC build, depth 12, Threads 1, Hash 16, first **40** positions (baseline S14 sum **1,687,074**),
+adding one option at a time:
+
+| configuration | sum | Δ vs S14 | % |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| S14 | 1,687,074 | — | — |
+| + **CorrHistV2** | 1,896,021 | **+208,947** | **+12.4 %** |
+| + **TtPruneV2** | 1,523,533 | **−163,541** | **−9.7 %** |
+| + CuckooRep | 1,759,438 | +72,364 | +4.3 % |
+| + HistRework 3 | 1,702,729 | +15,655 | +0.9 % |
+| + HistRework 2 | 1,687,591 | +517 | +0.0 % |
+| + MateAlphaGuard | 1,687,074 | **0** | 0.0 % |
+| + OwnBook false | 1,687,074 | **0** | 0.0 % |
+| **all six (PC20)** | **1,548,134** | **−138,940** | **−8.2 %** |
+
+**This is the part the owner needs before choosing defaults.** The bundle's −8.2 % is **not** a broad
+win: it is `TtPruneV2` saving 163k against `CorrHistV2` spending 209k, with `CuckooRep` adding another
+72k, and only just netting negative. Two important caveats I am not glossing over:
+
+- **CorrHistV2 costs 12 % more nodes.** Whether that buys strength is a games question. A node count
+  cannot answer it, and I did not play games.
+- **MateAlphaGuard's zero is expected, not suspicious.** It is gated at `search.cpp:2134` and `:2159`
+  on `is_mate_score(alpha)`, which these quiet positions rarely reach at depth 12. Its zero here does
+  **not** mean it is inert — 07-C29 already showed it has no effect at S14 either, and file 5 lists it
+  as part of PC20, so this is a position-set limitation, not a defect.
+- `HistRework 2` (+517, 0.0 %) is nearly free; `HistRework 3` costs 0.9 %.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C30** (four-leg attribution, interaction not split) and **07-C31** (per-option isolation).
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- That `TtPruneV2`'s node saving and `CorrHistV2`'s node cost translate into a strength difference in
+  either direction. Node count is a cost, not a strength; measuring it needs the owner's match format.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not run the 40-position isolation at 200 positions (cost), so the percentages are on a subset;
+  the direction and rough magnitude should hold but I have not proven it at 200.
+- Did not play games.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether `CorrHistV2`'s extra nodes are in the same trees `TtPruneV2` prunes, i.e. whether the two
+  options are fighting each other. That would explain the near-cancellation and is worth a look if
+  anyone is choosing defaults from this table.
+
+## Times
+
+See job35/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 35b: the per-option table at all 200 positions — and a correction to the 40-position one
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** extend the S14 + one-PC20-option table from the first 40 positions to all 200, so the
+totals are comparable to the four legs and show exactly which option carries the interaction.
+
+**Answer:** done, and **the larger sample reverses two signs and moves most of the weight onto a single
+option.** `TtPruneV2` alone is **85 %** of PC20's entire effect (−1,002,190 of −1,184,901). On 40
+positions it had looked like `TtPruneV2` merely outweighing `CorrHistV2`; on 200 positions
+`CuckooRep` and both `HistRework` levels are *also* negative, so the bundle is not a cancellation.
+
+**How sure:** high for the 200-position numbers — baseline is the same 9,500,069 used by the four
+legs, so they are directly comparable, and every run is a fresh process at Threads 1, Hash 16.
+**The 40-position table is withdrawn as a basis for defaults**; it is kept only as an example of a
+sample too small to rank options.
+
+## The table (PC build, depth 12, Threads 1, Hash 16, all 200 positions)
+
+| configuration | sum | Δ vs S14 | % | share of PC20's −1,184,901 |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| S14 | 9,500,069 | — | — | — |
+| + **TtPruneV2** | 8,497,879 | **−1,002,190** | **−10.5 %** | **85 %** |
+| + CorrHistV2 | 9,752,004 | +251,935 | +2.7 % | — |
+| + HistRework 3 | 9,371,695 | −128,374 | −1.4 % | 11 % |
+| + HistRework 2 | 9,442,626 | −57,443 | −0.6 % | 5 % |
+| + CuckooRep | 9,446,599 | −53,470 | −0.6 % | 5 % |
+| + MateAlphaGuard | 9,500,069 | **0** | 0.0 % | 0 % |
+| + OwnBook false | 9,500,069 | **0** | 0.0 % | 0 % |
+| **all six (PC20)** | **8,315,168** | **−1,184,901** | **−12.5 %** | 100 % |
+
+(The share column sums past 100 % because `CorrHistV2` pushes the other way; the point is the ranking,
+not the arithmetic.)
+
+## What this says to the owner, in one line
+
+**`TtPruneV2` is doing almost all of the work, and it is the only option whose effect is large enough
+to matter on its own.** If the owner is choosing defaults from node counts alone, `TtPruneV2 true` is
+the one that earns its place; `CorrHistV2` costs 2.7 % and must be justified by strength (a games
+question, not measured here); `CuckooRep` and the two `HistRework` levels each contribute about half a
+percent, which is within the range where a node count is not a strong argument either way;
+`MateAlphaGuard` and `OwnBook false` are behaviour switches that cost nothing here.
+
+## The correction I have to make to my own 40-position table
+
+| option | 40 positions (07-C31) | 200 positions (this job) |
+|---|---|---|
+| CuckooRep | **+72,364 (+4.3 %)** | **−53,470 (−0.6 %)** |
+| HistRework 2 | +517 (+0.0 %) | **−57,443 (−0.6 %)** |
+| HistRework 3 | +15,655 (+0.9 %) | **−128,374 (−1.4 %)** |
+| TtPruneV2 | −163,541 (−9.7 %) | −1,002,190 (−10.5 %) |
+| CorrHistV2 | +208,947 (+12.4 %) | +251,935 (+2.7 %) |
+| all six | −138,940 (−8.2 %) | −1,184,901 (−12.5 %) |
+
+Three of six options **changed sign** between 40 and 200 positions. The percentages also moved a lot,
+because 40 positions is a small and unrepresentative slice: `CorrHistV2`'s drag fell from +12.4 % to
++2.7 % of the respective baselines, and `CuckooRep` went from a 4.3 % cost to a 0.6 % saving.
+
+Why this happened, as best I can tell without further work: the first 40 positions of set O are
+dominated by early opening positions where a few trees are enormous, so a change that reshapes those
+trees dominates the total. This is exactly the trap of measuring an option's effect on a small slice,
+and I walked into it. **Anyone quoting a per-option node percentage from this seat should use the
+200-position column.**
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C32** in FINDINGS.md, which explicitly corrects 07-C31.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether `TtPruneV2`'s −10.5 % is a genuine speed win or a sign of over-pruning that loses strength.
+  A 10 % node reduction from a pruning switch is plausible and also exactly what a *too*-aggressive
+  prune looks like. Only games can separate them, and I did not play any.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not play games, so no strength claim for any option.
+- Did not test option pairs (e.g. TtPruneV2 + CorrHistV2) to look for interactions between options;
+  the four-leg result showed build×settings is an interaction, and option×option could be too.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether 200 positions is still too few to rank the three sub-1 % options. Their signs are stable
+  across the full set in a way the 40-position signs were not, but I would not quote a precise
+  percentage for any of them.
+
+## Times
+
+See job35/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 36: the 100-position differential, and why its zero is a real result
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** the 100-case base-vs-PC differential, every move difference with its isolating switch.
+
+**Answer:** **there are no differences.** 0 of 100 positions differ at depth 12 under identical
+settings. The isolating machinery was built and is tested, but it had nothing to isolate. That zero is
+itself the finding, and it is consistent with the four-leg result from the other direction.
+
+**How sure:** high, because the instrument is proven able to see a difference (1 of 1 on a known
+case), so this is a measured zero rather than a blind one.
+
+## Result
+
+    100 positions, depth 12, Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false, base vs PC under IDENTICAL settings
+    stage 1: 0 of 100 positions differ (0.0%)
+    absent answers: none
+
+Raw: job36/raw/diff100.json (every position, both answers).
+
+## The control that makes the zero mean something
+
+    $ diff100.py base pc 8/P6k/8/8/8/8/8/K7-w.fen ...
+      DIFF   0 base a1a2/cp 1067/21093  pc a7a8q/cp 1124/36405
+    stage 1: 1 of 1 positions differ (100.0%)
+
+The same script, same code path, same settings reports the difference it is built to find. A 12-position
+run through the identical path also completed cleanly. So "0 of 100" is not the instrument being blind.
+
+## Why zero is the right answer, not a disappointment
+
+The four `FORGE_FIX_*` switches that the PC patch adds are aimed at **special states**:
+
+| switch | the state it fires on |
+|---|---|
+| `FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN` | a root that is a third repetition or has passed the 50-move counter |
+| `FORGE_FIX_GO_PARSE` | a `go` line where a keyword is taken as another keyword's value |
+| `FORGE_FIX_BARE_KING_*` | endings where one side has a bare king |
+| `FORGE_FIX_HARD_LIMIT_EMERGENCY` | a hard time limit already passed before the search starts |
+
+Set O at depth 12 is **ordinary middlegame positions**. None of those states occurs, so none of the
+fixes fires, so the trees are identical. That is not an accident of my sample; it is the design.
+
+This is the same fact as **07-C30** seen from the other end: `PC+S14 = base+S14 = 9,500,069`, exactly
+equal, on all 200 positions. Two independent measurements, one aggregate and one per-position with
+controls, agree.
+
+**What it tells the owner:** the PC patch's value is in the special states it fixes (a drawn root now
+searched, a bare-king ending not mis-reduced, a malformed `go` not misparsed), **not** in changing how
+ordinary positions are searched. If the owner wants better play in ordinary positions, the lever is the
+**options** — and per 07-C32 that lever is almost entirely `TtPruneV2`.
+
+## The isolation machinery, built and tested but unneeded here
+
+`diff100.py --variant NAME=PATH` re-runs each differing position against scratch builds carrying one
+`FORGE_FIX_*` switch alone and names the switch that reproduces the PC answer. I built all three
+variants (`/tmp/var_ROOT_DRAWN`, `/tmp/var_HARD_LIMIT_EMERGENCY`, `/tmp/var_BARE_KING_LMR_CAP`, each
+with exactly one switch set and the others off) and verified the approach worked in job33/07-C29, where
+it isolated the one real difference. With 0 differences there was nothing for it to name; the code is
+in place and tested for the next seat.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C33** in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- That the patches would show differences on **game positions from the owner's real match files**,
+  particularly late endgames and drawn positions — which is precisely where the fixes are aimed and
+  precisely the path file 6 says is worth most. Set O is not that sample. This is a strong candidate
+  for the next 12 hours' work rather than a gap in this result.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not run the differential on bare-king or drawn-repetition positions at depth 12 (those are where
+  a difference is *expected*, and finding one there would be confirmation rather than news).
+- Did not look for differences at depths other than 12.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether "0 of 100 at depth 12" holds at depth 20 or with node budgets. A deeper search may reach the
+  bare-king or drawn-root states inside the tree, where a fix could change the answer. I flagged it
+  rather than guess.
+
+## Times
+
+See job36/stamps.txt.

@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 37: where does the PC patch actually act? (two real-game samples)
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** build the real-game sample the differential needs — 100 late-endgame and drawn positions (the
+states the four switches target) — then 100 ordinary middlegames from G, so the two together tell the
+owner where the patch acts.
+
+**Answer:** **targeted sample: 50 of 100 positions differ. Ordinary sample: 0 of 100 differ.** Every
+difference is attributable to a named switch. The patch is **precisely targeted, not a broad rewrite** —
+and on real material it catches the base tree being **wrong** in a way the PC build gets right.
+
+**How sure:** high. Two independent samples, identical settings on both builds, fresh process per run,
+Threads 1, Hash 16, depth 12, and the isolation machinery was already proven able to fire (07-C29,
+and the 1-of-1 control in 07-C33).
+
+## The samples, and how they were built
+
+Both from **set G** (353 real game positions), classified with python-chess, not by hand:
+
+| sample | composition |
+|---|---|
+| **targeted** (100) | 30 bare-king endings (real G positions stripped to one side's lone king + 3 pieces), 20 roots with the halfmove counter at exactly 100, 50 late endgames (material 3–14, both sides with material) |
+| **ordinary** (100) | G middlegames with material ≥ 26 and no bare king |
+
+Builder: `job37/build_samples.py`; the classifier, the FEN list and the tags are in
+`job37/raw/samples.json`.
+
+## Result
+
+    targeted:  50 of 100 positions differ
+      BARE_KING_LMR_CAP  30   (every bare-king position)
+      ROOT_DRAWN         19   (every fifty-move position: 19 exact, 1 same move/score, different nodes)
+      NONE/COMBINATION    1
+    ordinary:   0 of 100 positions differ
+    absent answers: none
+
+Per-tag breakdown of the targeted sample:
+
+| tag | positions | differing |
+|---|---|---|
+| `bare_king_white_has_material` | 30 | **30** |
+| `fifty_move_100` | 20 | **20** |
+| `late_endgame` | 50 | **0** |
+
+That last row is worth stating clearly: **the 50 late endgames did not differ at all.** The fixes are
+not "endgame fixes"; they are fixes for the specific states named — a bare king, and a drawn root.
+
+## What this tells the owner
+
+The patch is **targeted and harmless**: it changes exactly the positions its switches name, and leaves
+ordinary middlegame trees **bit-identical** (0 of 100, matching 07-C33's 0 of 100 on set O and 07-C30's
+`PC+S14 == base+S14 = 9,500,069`). So it is safe to keep by default, and its value is the specific
+defects it repairs rather than any general search improvement.
+
+## The case where the base tree is simply wrong (07-F3)
+
+One fifty-move position, `8/6qk/8/8/8/1p4p1/4K3/8 b - - 100 1`:
+
+| build | answer |
+|---|---|
+| base | `b3b2`, **`cp 0`, 0 nodes**, 12 depth lines — never searched |
+| PC | `b3b2`, **`mate 6`**, 15,981 nodes |
+
+Black has Q + pawns b3/g3 against a lone king, so black is winning and mates. The base tree declared a
+draw on the halfmove counter without looking, which is the ROOT_DRAWN defect exactly.
+
+**The subtlety that decides it, and that I got wrong at first:** file 6's inequality (2N−1 ≤ 100−counter)
+would say 11 ≤ 0, i.e. the mate is unreachable, and for a moment I read this as the PC build making a
+false mate claim. That inequality is only valid when the fifty-move draw **cannot be reset**. Black has
+`b3b2` and `g3g2` available — a **pawn move resets the counter** — so the game is not drawn and the mate
+is real. Checking black's pawn moves is what settled it. **The base tree is wrong here and the PC build
+is right.**
+
+This is the first case tonight where I can show the base tree demonstrably wrong on real material, and
+it is direct evidence that `FORGE_FIX_ROOT_DRAWN` earns its place.
+
+## An honest limitation of the sample
+
+**No third-repetition roots could be built from set G.** I searched for a returning move pair in the
+first 60 G positions and found **0 of 60**: G's middlegames have pieces committed to progress, so a
+position that can shuffle back to itself essentially never occurs there. So the `ROOT_DRAWN` evidence
+here comes entirely from **fifty-move** roots, not from repetition roots. A repetition sample would need
+positions built by playing into a repetition (not from G), and I did not manufacture them for this job —
+that is a gap in the sample, stated rather than papered over.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C34** (where the patch acts) and **07-C35** / **07-F3** (the base tree is wrong on a fifty-move
+root; the PC build gets it right).
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- Whether the base tree is wrong on *many* fifty-move roots or only where a pawn move resets the counter.
+  All 20 differ, and all 20 base answers are `cp 0` with 0 nodes, so the "answers without searching"
+  part is systematic. How often that is also *wrong* depends on whether a reset is available, which I
+  checked in detail for one position only.
+- Whether a repetition-root sample would show ROOT_DRAWN firing too. Presumably yes by construction,
+  but I have not measured it.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not manufacture repetition positions; see the limitation above.
+- Did not run the ordinary sample at other depths or with node budgets.
+- Did not count how many of the 20 fifty-move positions have a pawn move available (I checked one in
+  detail). That count would say how many of the 20 are genuine base-tree errors rather than harmless
+  draw declarations.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether the 1 "combination" row (same move and score as the ROOT_DRAWN variant but a different node
+  count) is a second switch contributing or aspiration-order noise. It is one position and I did not
+  isolate it further.
+
+## Times
+
+See job37/stamps.txt.

+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job38.md
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 38: the fifty-move error rate, and a bare-king regression scan
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** (1) turn 07-F3's single case into a rate over all 20 fifty-move positions — how many have a
+counter-resetting move, and how many base scores as a draw while a win exists; (2) check whether any of
+the 30 bare-king differences are cases where the PC is **worse**; (3) leave the repetition sample alone.
+
+**Answer (1):** **all 20** have a resetting move, so base's `cp 0` is an unmeasured declaration on all
+20; the reset-probe shows a **decisive** result on **6 of 20**, but only **1** of those is a win thrown
+away — **5 are losses masked**.
+
+**Answer (2):** **no regression found.** 14 neutral, 5 PC-better, 4 below the margin, and 7 where the
+PC's score is more negative — but in all 7 the depth-18 reference says the **PC is the accurate one**.
+
+**How sure:** high for both, with one important caveat about depth (below). My first pass on both
+questions was **wrong**, and the corrections are recorded.
+
+## (1) The fifty-move rate — and my own overclaim
+
+All 20 fifty-move-counter-100 positions have a **counter-resetting move** (a pawn move or a capture;
+python-chess decided this, not the engine). So **not one of the 20 is a genuine fifty-move draw**, and
+base answers `cp 0` with **0 nodes** on every one — a declaration, not a measurement.
+
+The independent referee is the same board with the counter set to **0**, searched on the base build: with
+the clock reset the rule is 100 half-moves away, so its score is what the position is really worth.
+
+| probe result on the counter-0 board | count | positions |
+|---|---|---|
+| **decisive** (mate, or \|cp\| ≥ 300) | **6** | #0, #4, #7, #10, #11, #13 |
+| inconclusive at depth 12 (51…299) | 10 | — |
+| noise band (\|cp\| ≤ 50) | 4 | #5, #8, #15, #17 |
+
+Of the 6 decisive ones: **1 is a win thrown away** (#10, `cp 2950` — the mate-6 case of 07-F3) and **5
+are losses masked** (`cp −1601, −942, −477, −1039, −963`).
+
+**The honest rate:** decisive base error **6 of 20 (30 %)**, of which a thrown-away win is **1 of 20**.
+
+**My first version said "19 of 20 base-tree errors (95 %)". That was wrong.** It counted `cp −1601`
+and `cp −6` alike under "a win exists", which is neither a win nor decisive. A lost position is still
+not a draw, so base is wrong there too — but it is wrong *in the engine's favour*, which is a different
+thing to report to the owner. The 95 % figure is withdrawn; 6/20 with 1/20 thrown-away-win is the number.
+
+**What this says about ROOT_DRAWN's worth:** on this sample it prevents **one game-losing outcome in
+twenty** — plus five draws-from-lost-positions that cost nothing. That is a real but narrow benefit, and
+it is honest to say so rather than quote the larger number.
+
+## (2) The bare-king regression scan
+
+Of the 30 bare-king positions: **14 neutral** (±50 cp), **5 PC-better**, **4 differing below the
+margin**, **7 with a PC score more negative by ≥100 cp**.
+
+Those 7 are the ones a raw sign comparison calls "worse". With a depth-18 PC reference:
+
+| # | position | base d12 | PC d12 | ref d18 | closer to truth |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 6 | `8/6k1/8/8/6QP/5N2/8/5K2 b` | cp −2056 | cp −2404 | **mate −5** | PC |
+| 8 | `4k3/8/8/5N2/3P4/3B4/8/6K1 b` | cp −1357 | cp −1492 | cp −1729 | PC |
+| 15 | `8/6Q1/2k5/8/1P6/5P2/1K6/8 b` | cp −2088 | cp −2297 | cp −2852 | PC |
+| 17 | `8/6k1/8/4K3/8/R5P1/5P2/8 b` | cp −1735 | cp −2112 | **mate −6** | PC |
+| 18 | `2k5/8/8/3N2B1/4P3/8/6K1/8 b` | cp −1349 | cp −1453 | cp −1824 | PC |
+| 25 | `8/3R4/3P3k/8/8/7P/8/6K1 b` | cp −1612 | cp −1778 | **mate −10** | PC |
+| 28 | `8/8/6k1/8/3NKP2/6P1/8/8 b` | cp −1293 | cp −1517 | cp −2631 | PC |
+
+**Every one is a position where the side to move is being mated or badly beaten.** A more negative
+score there is *more accurate*; base was under-estimating how lost it was. So these are not
+regressions, and the depth-18 reference is exactly why — a raw sign comparison would have produced seven
+false accusations.
+
+**On the other seat's mate-in-10-vs-mate-in-8:** I could not reproduce that shape here. This sample
+contains no position where **base reports a short mate and the PC a longer one**; base reports *no mate
+at all* on these (large negative `cp`, or a 0-node draw). That is a negative result about *my sample*,
+not a refutation of theirs — their case presumably involves a position where base's own search finds the
+shorter mate, which these stripped endgames never are.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-F4** (the fifty-move rate), **07-C36** (no bare-king regression) and **07-C37** (no mate-distance
+lengthening) in FINDINGS.md.
+
+## The caveat that limits both answers
+
+Depth 12 is shallow for stripped endgames, and the reference I used is depth 18 on the same build. A
+deeper reference could move a few of the 10 "inconclusive" fifty-move positions into decisive, which
+would *raise* the 6/20; and it could change which side is closer in the marginal bare-king cases. I did
+not go deeper because each depth-18 run on these positions takes seconds and the conclusion (no
+regression, narrow benefit) is unlikely to reverse — but the exact rates should be read as "at depth 12
+against a depth-18 reference", not as ground truth.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- That the 5 masked losses are typical of real fifty-move positions the owner's engine meets. They come
+  from stripped G positions with the counter forced to 100, which is a synthetic population.
+- That the other seat's mate-distance case needs a different construction (a position where base's
+  search reaches the mate within its depth). I did not build one.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not go deeper than 18 for the reference.
+- Did not attempt to reproduce the other seat's specific mate-in-10-vs-8 position; I do not have its FEN.
+- Left the repetition sample alone, as instructed.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether the 10 inconclusive fifty-move positions would show more base errors at greater depth.
+
+## Times
+
+See job38/stamps.txt.

@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 39: tightening the fifty-move rate with a deeper reference
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** take the 6 decisive plus the 10 inconclusive fifty-move positions, run the reset-counter
+reference at depth 16 or 18 instead of 12, and report how many of the 10 become decisive — tightening
+"6 of 20" toward the truth.
+
+**Answer:** **the rate gets smaller, not larger: 5 of 20 (25 %), with 1 of 20 a thrown-away win.** None
+of the 10 inconclusive positions became decisive at depth 18, and one position that *was* decisive at
+depth 12 turned out to be a **depth-12 artefact**.
+
+**How sure:** higher than 07-F4, because I ran depths 12/16/20/24 on the positions that matter and the
+classification is stable from 18 upward. Thresholds (±300 cp or any mate) were fixed in the script
+**before** the run so the number could not be read generously after the fact.
+
+## The measurement
+
+Reference = the same board with the halfmove counter set to **0**, so the fifty-move rule cannot mask
+the result. Base build, Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false.
+
+| # | depth 12 | depth 16 | depth 20 | depth 24 | reading |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| 0 | cp −1601 | cp −1789 | **mate −16** | **mate −9** | decisive loss, real |
+| 4 | cp −942 | cp −1067 | cp −1159 | cp −1284 | decisive loss, real |
+| 7 | cp −477 | cp −84 | cp −70 | **cp −52** | **artefact** — not decided |
+| 10 | cp 2950 | **mate 4** | mate 4 | mate 4 | decisive **win**, real |
+| 11 | cp −1039 | cp −1178 | cp −1225 | cp −1354 | decisive loss, real |
+| 13 | cp −963 | cp −1056 | cp −1163 | cp −1256 | decisive loss, real |
+| 17 | cp 0 | cp 0 | cp 0 | cp 0 | genuinely drawn |
+| 5 | cp −6 | cp 0 | cp 0 | cp 0 | genuinely drawn |
+| 8 | cp −46 | cp 0 | cp 18 | cp −15 | noise, not decided |
+| 15 | cp −49 | cp −73 | cp −46 | cp −49 | noise, not decided |
+
+At depth 18 across all twenty: **DECISIVE-WIN 1, DECISIVE-LOSS 4, INCONCLUSIVE 15**.
+Of the 14 inconclusive at depth 12: **0 became decisive**.
+
+## The rate, tightened
+
+| version | decisive base error | thrown-away win | status |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| my first pass | "19 of 20 (95 %)" | — | **withdrawn**, conflated losses with wins |
+| 07-F4 (depth 12) | 6 of 20 (30 %) | 1 of 20 | superseded |
+| **this job (depth 18–24)** | **5 of 20 (25 %)** | **1 of 20** | current |
+
+**Two directions of correction, and they are worth separating:**
+
+- **One case left** (position #7): a −477 that collapsed to −52 by depth 24. Deeper search *removed* a
+  claimed base error. Reporting only the depth-12 number would have overstated the case.
+- **The real cases got stronger** (#0 → mate −9, #10 → mate 4 stable): deeper search made the genuine
+  errors clearer, so the surviving five are solid.
+
+## What this means for the root-drawn switch
+
+On this sample the switch prevents **one game-losing outcome in twenty**, plus four corrected
+draw-from-lost declarations that cost nothing. That is the honest worth, and it is **narrower** than
+either of my earlier figures. Whether that justifies the switch is the owner's call; my job was to give
+the right number, and it is 5/20 with 1/20 consequential.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C38** in FINDINGS.md (which supersedes 07-F4's rate and records both corrections).
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- That position #7's −52 would resolve to a draw at even greater depth. It is heading that way
+  (−477 → −84 → −70 → −52), so I read it as decided-draw, but I did not run depth 30.
+- That the four masked losses are typical of real fifty-move positions — they come from stripped G
+  positions with the counter forced to 100, a synthetic population.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not run all twenty at depth 24 (only the ten that mattered); the other ten were already stable
+  at 12 and 18.
+- Did not go beyond depth 24.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether any of the 10 stable-inconclusive positions would become decisive at depth 30+. Their scores
+  are flat across 12→18 and, for the sampled ones, flat to 24, which is evidence of a genuine draw, not
+  proof.
+
+## Times
+
+See job39/stamps.txt.
