@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 5: settling seat 01 vs. seat 07 on search.cpp:2640
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** seats 01 and 07 make contradictory claims about search.cpp:2640. Settle it with the
+marker instrument; quote raw marker output; note that ASan silence is not evidence either way;
+record the resolution in FINDINGS naming seat 01; report one line to the coordinator.
+
+**Answer:** **seat 01's claim does not hold, mine does.** Line 2640 is never reached with an empty
+`root_candidates`, because search.cpp:2253 returns first. The `bestmove 0000` comes from
+`best_move` legitimately staying `none` (the UCI layer renders a none move as `0000`), not from a
+garbage `Move` read out of a `front()` on an empty list.
+
+**How sure:** very high. The instrument is a single binary with a marker on **both** branches, so
+whichever path executes announces itself. Seat 01's exact commands fire the 2253 marker and never
+the 2640 marker, and the 2640 marker is proven able to fire in the same binary.
+
+## The instrument
+
+`/tmp/branch` = 6b98f217 plus two stderr markers, nothing else:
+
+    search.cpp:2253  if (root_candidates.empty() || root_drawn) {
+    +    std::cerr << "MARK-2253-EARLY-RETURN root_candidates=" << root_candidates.size()
+    +              << " legal=" << legal.size() << " restricted=" << int(result.restricted_root_empty)
+    +              << " drawn=" << int(root_drawn) << std::endl;
+    search.cpp:2640  if (result.best_move.is_none()) {
+    +    std::cerr << "MARK-2640-GUARD-TRUE root_candidates=" << root_candidates.size() << std::endl;
+         result.best_move = root_candidates.front();
+
+Built plain RelWithDebInfo with g++-13, no sanitizers (a sanitizer is irrelevant to which branch
+runs, and would only slow the marker down). Driver: job2/uci_drive.py, which never pipelines a
+command behind `go`.
+
+## Raw marker output (verbatim, from job5/raw/*.err)
+
+| case | command | MARK-2253 fired | MARK-2640 fired | bestmove |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| s01_c1_plain_control | `go depth 2` | no | no | `d2d4` |
+| s01_c2_searchmoves_no_names | `go searchmoves depth 2` | **yes**, `root_candidates=0 legal=20 restricted=1 drawn=0` | no | `0000` |
+| s01_c3_one_legal_name | `go searchmoves e2e4 depth 2` | no | no | `e2e4` |
+| s01_c4_not_a_move | `go searchmoves a1a1 depth 2` | **yes**, `root_candidates=0 legal=20 restricted=1 drawn=0` | no | `0000` |
+| s01_c5_illegal_pair | `go searchmoves e2e5 depth 2` | **yes**, `root_candidates=0 legal=20 restricted=1 drawn=0` | no | `0000` |
+| s01_c6_restricted_illegal_only | `go searchmoves e7e5 depth 2` | **yes**, `root_candidates=0 legal=20 restricted=1 drawn=0` | no | `0000` |
+| s01_c7_two_legal | `go searchmoves e2e4 d2d4 depth 2` | no | no | `d2d4` |
+| s01_c8_marker_positive_control_nodes | `go nodes 5` | no | **yes**, `root_candidates=20` | `a2a3` |
+
+The last row is the positive control: it proves the 2640 marker in this very binary is capable of
+printing, so the absence of 2640 lines in rows 2, 4, 5 and 6 means the branch was not taken, not
+that the instrument was dead. Rows 1, 3 and 7 are the controls showing plain and legal-restricted
+searches reach neither marker.
+
+## On ASan silence
+
+Seat 01 is right that "ASan reported nothing" proves nothing here, and I do not use it as proof.
+An out-of-range read into a mapped slot need not trap. The disagreement was therefore never
+settleable by sanitizers, which is why both seats' sanitizer observations are set aside and only
+the branch markers are used. (For the record, my earlier debug-STL run also produced no abort, and
+I likewise do not treat that as the proof — see the note below.)
+
+## Why 2640 cannot see the empty list, in lines
+
+    2203  MoveList root_candidates;                 // filled by the searchmoves intersection
+    2210  result.restricted_root_empty = root_restricted_ && !legal.empty() && root_candidates.empty();
+    2253  if (root_candidates.empty() || root_drawn) { ... return result; }  // <-- fires, marker proves it
+    2459  if (!result.pv.empty()) result.best_move = result.pv.front();
+    2640  if (result.best_move.is_none()) result.best_move = root_candidates.front();
+
+Every path to 2640 has already passed 2253 with a non-empty root. `best_move` being `none` at 2640
+happens on the `go nodes 5` path, where no iteration publishes a PV — and there the root is
+size 20, exactly as the control shows.
+
+## One correction to my own earlier evidence
+
+My 07-C1 line leaned partly on a debug-STL build not aborting. Given seat 01's correct point that
+sanitizer/abort silence is weak evidence, the load-bearing evidence is now the two-branch marker
+run in this report (07-C2). The 07-C1 conclusion is unchanged and now rests on the stronger
+instrument; the debug-STL non-abort is retained only as consistent supporting observation.
+
+## Findings
+
+**07-C2 — REFUTES seat 01's S-C3 (2640 half), AGREES on the ASan method point.** In FINDINGS.md.
+Show it again:
+
+    cd forge-combo29/swarm/07/job5 && python3 -u ../job2/uci_drive.py /tmp/branch/build/forge cases_s01.txt /tmp/x 60
+    grep -E "MARK-" /tmp/x/*.err
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not attempt to build seat 01's exact binary or flags; the claim is about 6b98f217's control
+  flow, so it is refuted at the pinned commit.
+- Did not change `bestmove 0000` semantics; that stays the patch's business (07-F1), not this check.
+
+## Times
+
+See job5/stamps.txt.

--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job6.md
@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 6: reading src/board.cpp (castling, en passant, king square)
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** spend the window on the board.cpp read, prioritising faults that would show in normal
+play, in this order of severity: (1) castling rights surviving a rook capture on its home square,
+(2) en-passant squares set after a double push when no capturer exists, (3) a king position going
+stale after a null move. If nothing is found, say so with the probes run.
+
+**Answer:** **all three are clean, and the probes are shown to be able to fail.** Beyond the three,
+I found and closed one *real* latent weakness that is not a wrong answer today but is an unguarded
+invariant in shipped code: `Board::key_after()` (the early TT-prefetch key) is verified in-tree
+only by an `assert` that `NDEBUG` removes, and it is on by default. I proved the function itself is
+correct over 1,520,927 move cases, so this is a robustness finding, not a bug.
+
+**How sure:** high for all three areas — each probe has a positive control that makes it fail on a
+planted fault, so "pass" is meaningful. High for the key_after correctness result (exhaustive over
+random legal play, with a planted fault detected 608 times). Medium that `key_after`'s missing
+runtime check ever matters, since nothing currently consumes a wrong key.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build (6b98f217, GCC 13.3.0, plain CMake Release): bench 11 = 312866, bench 13 = 862329,
+bench 16 = 3024920, perft 5 = 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source was modified for any
+probe here; every program below is a standalone `.cpp` compiled against the unmodified
+`src/board.cpp` + `src/bitboard.cpp`.
+
+## Step table
+
+| step | done / partly / not done | evidence file | result |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| read set_fen / make_move / unmake_move / null-move / repetition / see_ge | done | this report cites line numbers | see "what the read covered" |
+| perft vs python-chess on castling / ep / promotion positions | done | job4/perft_board.py, job4/raw/all.json | 14 positions, every total and every divide line equal, no stderr |
+| probe 1: castling right after a rook is captured on its home square | done | job6/board_probes.cpp, job6/board_probes_run.txt | pass, with a planted-fault control that fails |
+| probe 2: ep square set with no legal capturer | done | job6/board_probes.cpp + job6/epkey_probe.cpp, job6/epkey_run.txt | pass, with controls in both directions |
+| probe 3: king square across a null move | done | job6/board_probes.cpp, job6/board_probes_run.txt | pass |
+| key_after vs make_move over random legal play | done | job6/key_after_test.cpp, job6/key_after_run.txt | 1,520,927 checked, 0 mismatches, planted fault caught 608 times |
+
+## Probe 1 — castling rights vs. a rook captured on its home square
+
+`CastlingMasks` (board.cpp:166-177) clears a side's right on any move **from** or **to** the corner.
+The dangerous case is a capture landing on the corner, so the test is a real capture.
+
+    position r3k2r/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K2R b KQkq - 0 1, then a8a1
+    rights after = 5  ->  1 (White king-side) + 4 (Black king-side)
+    fen after    = 4k2r/8/8/8/8/8/8/r3K2R w Kk - 0 2
+
+White's queen-side right is gone (its rook was captured on a1), White's king-side right survives,
+and Black's king-side right survives because only the **queen-side** rook left a8. `unmake_move`
+restores the original FEN byte for byte.
+
+Note honestly: my first version of this probe asserted that right 4 must also be cleared. That was
+my error — a8 is the queen-side rook — and the corrected assertion is in the committed file with a
+comment saying so.
+
+**Control:** rebuilding with `masks[0] = 0xFF` (a planted fault: a1 no longer clears White's
+queen-side right) makes this probe fail with `FAIL probe1 White queen-side right cleared by Rxa1
+[4k2r/8/8/8/8/8/8/r3K2R w KQk - 0 2]`. So the probe detects the class of bug it is aimed at.
+
+## Probe 2 — en-passant square set with no capturer
+
+`make_move` sets `ep_square_` on every double push (board.cpp:1086), which is lawful; the thing that
+must not drift is the **key**, which includes the ep term only when a legal ep capture exists
+(board.cpp:1040-1042, 1090-1092, and `has_legal_en_passant_capture` at 979-993).
+
+- A double push with no enemy pawn at all (`4k3/8/8/8/8/8/4P3/4K3 w`, play `e2e4`) leaves the FEN
+  showing `- e3` but the key **identical** to the same board written with `- -`:
+  both `14344340005152966589`.
+- **Control that this is not vacuous** (`job6/epkey_probe.cpp`): the same position pair differing
+  *only* in the ep field, with a legal ep capture available, gives **different** keys
+  (`631853344440671074` vs `13845825276157828580`). So the ep term really is included when it should be.
+- **Control in the other direction:** with the capturing pawn pinned (black pawn d4 pinned to its
+  king on d8 by a rook on d1), the ep field is present but the capture is illegal, and the keys are
+  **equal** (`10860499126821786208` both ways). That is exactly the documented rule.
+
+## Probe 3 — king square across a null move
+
+`make_null_move` / `unmake_null_move` (board.cpp:1145-1180) deliberately do not touch
+`king_squares_`; the king does not move. Verified: `king_square(White)` = 4 before, during and after
+a null move, equal to the square the bitboard scan reports, and the FEN round-trips exactly.
+Then the case that could actually go stale: after `e1e2`, the square is 12; a null move keeps 12;
+`unmake_null_move` keeps 12; `unmake_move` restores 4 and the original FEN.
+
+## The one thing worth Opus's attention: `key_after` has no runtime check in Release
+
+`Board::key_after` (board.cpp:996-1020) predicts the child position's Zobrist key **without making
+the move**, so the search can prefetch the right TT cluster a few instructions earlier. It is used
+at search.cpp:1504 and 1964, and it is **enabled in the shipped build**
+(`FORGE_SPD_PREFETCH_EARLY=1` in the CMake definitions; the header default at board.hpp:30 is 0).
+
+Its only verification in the tree is
+
+    search.cpp:1505 / :1965   assert(!early_key || child_key == board.key());
+
+and the Release build defines `NDEBUG`, so in the shipped engine that assertion does not exist. If
+`key_after` were ever wrong, the search would prefetch the wrong cluster — a silent slowdown, and a
+landmine for anyone who later trusts the value as a key.
+
+**I tested the function itself:** `job6/key_after_test.cpp` walks 200 random legal games, and for
+every legal move at every ply compares `key_after(move)` against `make_move(move).key()`.
+
+    games 200 seed 701
+    key_after checked 1520927  refused 40778
+    mismatches 0
+
+The 40,778 refusals are the documented conservative cases (an ep square present, an ep capture, or a
+double push next to an enemy pawn) where the function correctly declines.
+
+**Control:** with the rook term removed from the castling branch of a scratch copy
+(`next ^= 0;` replacing the rook piece_key pair), the same test reports **608 mismatches** and names
+the first one precisely: `fen 2bk1bn1/5r2/p1Pp1q2/5pp1/3pPP2/NP1BQ2r/P1RB3P/R3K3 w Q - 2 32 move e1c1
+got 13247982611084509182 want 3430718038044698871`. So the zero above is a real zero.
+
+**Why I am not filing this as a fault:** the function is correct on 1.52M cases and nothing consumes
+the predicted key; the defect is that a compiled-out assertion is the only guard on an optimisation
+that shipping code relies on. That belongs in "suspicions / hardening", not in FINDINGS as a bug.
+
+## Findings
+
+Nothing new for FINDINGS from the three probed areas — they are clean. The `key_after` observation
+is recorded here as a hardening note, with the full control evidence, rather than as a finding,
+because it does not produce a wrong answer.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- `key_after`'s missing Release-time check (above). Concretely: a `Debug`/`RelWithDebInfo` CI run
+  would exercise the assertion; a Release-only CI would not.
+- `is_repetition(std::size_t root_index)` (board.cpp:1235-1248) counts a repetition as a draw when
+  it has seen the same key twice *or* when a match lies at or after the root index. I read this as
+  intentional (twofold within the search, repetition at/below the root) and did not test it; it is
+  the kind of rule that silently changes play strength, so it is worth a dedicated check.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test `see_ge`'s exchange walk beyond the perft agreement (SEE does not affect perft).
+- Did not test the repetition rule (see suspicions).
+- Did not run the probes under a sanitizer; they are deterministic logic checks with controls, and a
+  sanitizer would not add to what the planted-fault controls already establish.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether any future caller will trust `key_after`'s output as a key. Today none does.
+
+## Times
+
+See job6/stamps.txt (and job4/stamps.txt for the perft part).

+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/REPORT_job7.md
@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+# REPORT — seat 07, job 7: repetition rule and a failed SEE cross-check
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** (continuation of the board.cpp read, highest normal-play risk first) test
+`Board::is_repetition()` and anything else in board.cpp that silently changes play.
+
+**Answer:** `is_repetition()` **agrees with python-chess threefold at all 62 plies** tested,
+including the two cases that matter most in play: a twofold must not be declared a draw, and a
+counter reset by a pawn move must break the repetition. My SEE cross-check **failed to become a
+usable oracle** and I draw **no conclusion** about `see_ge` from it; that is written up as a
+non-result, not a finding.
+
+**How sure:** high for the repetition result (a planted fault makes the same comparison report 17
+disagreements, so the clean result is not vacuous). For SEE: nothing claimed either way.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build, job0/raw/summary.txt: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609. No engine source changed;
+both programs compile against the unmodified `src/board.cpp` + `src/bitboard.cpp`.
+
+## Step table
+
+| step | done / partly / not done | evidence file | result |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| read `is_repetition()` and both overloads | done | board.cpp:1224-1248, callers search.cpp:1308/1317/2251/2256 | see below |
+| compare `is_repetition()` with python-chess threefold | done | job7/repetition_probe.cpp + job7/check_repetition.py | 62 plies, 0 disagreements |
+| prove that comparison can fail | done | planted fault below | 17 disagreements reported |
+| cross-check `see_ge` against an independent reference | **not done (failed)** | job7/see_crosscheck.cpp + job7/SEE_NOTES.txt | my oracle was wrong twice; no result drawn |
+
+## The repetition rule, as the code states it
+
+    board.cpp:1224  is_repetition()            count earlier occurrences of key_ in the
+                                               halfmove-limited window; draw at >= 2
+                                               (i.e. this position plus two earlier ones)
+    board.cpp:1235  is_repetition(root_index)  span limited by min(halfmove, plies_from_null);
+                                               true on a match at/after the root, else >= 2
+
+Callers: `Worker::is_draw` (search.cpp:1308), `draw_leaf_score` (1317), and the root-drawn
+special case (2251, 2256). So the rule decides real scores, not just a display field.
+
+## Test
+
+Six move lists, each played from startpos, comparing `is_repetition()` against python-chess
+`is_repetition(3)` after **every** ply:
+
+1. `g1f3 g8f6 f3g1 f6g8 g1f3 g8f6 f3g1 f6g8` — a genuine threefold.
+2. the same with `e2e4 e7e5` in the middle — a counter reset, so the later shuffles are **not** a draw.
+3. `g1f3 g8f6 f3g1 f6g8` — a twofold only, which must **not** be a draw.
+4. a queen shuffle repeating twice.
+5. eight reversible plies, a pawn move, then more — the fifty-move-counter interaction.
+6. a long shuffle repeating many times.
+
+    plies compared: 62
+    RESULT: engine is_repetition() agrees with python-chess threefold at every ply
+
+The checker asserts a `rep=` column and a key exist on every ply and refuses to run if any move
+list is illegal, so a missing line cannot pass as agreement.
+
+**Control (this is what makes the clean run meaningful):** rebuilding with `return matches >= 1;`
+in `is_repetition()` — a planted fault that declares a twofold as a draw — makes the same checker
+report **17 disagreements**, each naming the ply and FEN, e.g.
+`list 4 ply 7 move c3b1: engine rep=True python-chess threefold=False fen
+r1bqkbnr/pppppppp/2n5/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR b KQkq - 7 4`. So the comparison detects exactly the
+class of bug it is aimed at.
+
+## The SEE cross-check: a non-result, stated plainly
+
+I wrote `see_crosscheck.cpp`, an independent swap-list static-exchange evaluator, to compare with
+`Board::see_ge()`. It disagreed on captures. Rather than report that as an engine finding, I checked
+its first disagreeing cases by hand with python-chess:
+
+- `fen 2b1kbn1/2r3p1/p1Pp1q2/5p2/2BpPP2/1P2Q2r/P1R4P/RNB1K3 w Q - 2 29`, move `e4f5`:
+  after `exf5`, Black's **only** legal captures are `h3e3` and `d4e3`; nothing recaptures on f5.
+  So `see_ge(exf5, 100) = true` is **correct** and my reference invented a recapture.
+- `fen r1bqkbnr/pppppppp/2n5/8/8/2P5/PP1PPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 1 2`, move `b2b4`:
+  White wins a knight for a pawn (+200 by piece count after `b4 Nxb4 cxb4`), so the engine was
+  right and my first reference version was wrong.
+
+I fixed two bugs in the reference (the standing-piece bookkeeping in the swap list, and matching
+the engine's documented choice that a king is worth 0 in SEE, `include/forge/eval.hpp:32`), and it
+still differs, so it is not fit to be an oracle. **I therefore claim nothing about `see_ge`** beyond
+this: it is exercised indirectly by the 14-position perft agreement and by the honesty pins, both
+of which are unchanged. A real SEE check needs an oracle that is itself validated move by move
+against python-chess's legality — which is what my two hand checks did, and both went the engine's
+way.
+
+## Findings
+
+No new FINDINGS. `is_repetition()` is clean under a failable test; SEE is unresolved rather than
+faulty, and an unresolved check is not a finding.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- `is_repetition(root_index)`'s rule ("a match at or after the root is a draw, even the first one")
+  is a deliberate search-side rule, not FIDE threefold. I did not test it separately; the no-argument
+  overload I did test is the one the UI-facing root check uses.
+- `key_after` has no runtime check in Release (job6 report). Unchanged conclusion.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not produce a trustworthy SEE oracle; explicitly abandoned rather than tuned until it agreed
+  (tuning until agreement would have been circular).
+- Did not test `is_repetition(root_index)` at search depth.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether the engine's SEE mishandles pinned attackers in some position; my oracle could not tell me.
+
+## Times
+
+See job7/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 8: `has_legal_move()` (checkmate/stalemate detector)
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the board.cpp read, prioritising what shows up in normal play.
+
+**Answer:** `Board::has_legal_move()` is **correct on all 9,118 positions tested**, agreeing both
+with python-chess and with the engine's own `legal_moves().size() > 0`. This function decides
+checkmate and stalemate at the search root and inside `is_draw()` / `draw_leaf_score()`, so it was
+the highest-value remaining item in board.cpp: a false answer is a wrong game result, not a display
+quirk.
+
+**How sure:** high — the comparison is proven able to fail (a planted fault produces 26
+disagreements, each naming the FEN).
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+Base build: 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609 (job0/raw/summary.txt). No engine source changed;
+the probe compiles against the unmodified `src/board.cpp` + `src/bitboard.cpp`.
+
+## Why this function deserves its own job
+
+    board.cpp:721  bool Board::has_legal_move() const {
+    board.cpp:725      const Bitboard pushes = pawn_push(side_, pieces(side_, Pawn)) &
+                                              ~occupied() & ~(Rank1BB | Rank8BB);
+    board.cpp:726      if (pushes != 0) {    // fast witness: try ONE quiet pawn push
+    board.cpp:730          if (is_legal(witness)) return true;
+    board.cpp:731      }
+    board.cpp:733      MoveList moves; generate_pseudo_legal(moves, false);   // full fallback
+    board.cpp:735      for (...) if (is_legal(move)) return true;
+    board.cpp:737      return false;
+
+The fast path returns `true` early on a single witness move. If that witness were ever accepted
+when the position is actually terminal, the engine would report a mate/stalemate position as
+playable. The fallback path is the one that has to be right for genuinely terminal positions.
+
+## Test
+
+`job8/legal_move_probe.cpp` emits `fen | has_legal_move | legal_count` for:
+
+- start of every random game;
+- every position in the last phase of each game (≤ 12 pieces), where promotion races, blocked
+  pawns and lone kings live — this is the territory the fast witness path mishandles if anything does;
+- a sample of 1 position in 8 through the middlegame;
+- seven hand-built families: stalemate, checkmate, lone king, promotion-only, blocked pawn with a
+  stalemated king, en passant as the only legal move, pinned pawn with no king square.
+
+`job8/check_legal_move.py` recomputes the truth from each printed FEN with python-chess and also
+cross-checks the engine against itself (`has_legal_move` vs `legal_count > 0`), so an inconsistent
+engine would be caught even if python-chess disagreed with both.
+
+    positions checked: 9118
+    RESULT: has_legal_move() agreed with python-chess and with legal_moves().size()
+            on every position
+
+## The control that makes that a result
+
+Rebuilding with the fallback's `return false;` replaced by `return true;` — a planted fault that
+makes every terminal position look playable — makes the same checker report **26 disagreements**,
+each naming the FEN, for example:
+
+    has_legal_move=1 but python-chess says False for 8/8/8/8/8/5k2/5p2/5K2 w - - 0 1
+    INTERNAL: has_legal_move=1 vs legal_count=0 for 7k/6Q1/6K1/8/8/8/8/8 b - - 0 1
+
+So the zero in the real run is a measured zero, not an absent measurement.
+
+## One honest wart in my own test
+
+The run prints `REFUSED 8/8/8/8/8/8/6p1/6Kk b - - 0 1` — my hand-built promotion family had kings
+on adjacent squares, which the engine correctly refuses at FEN validation. That is my construction
+error, not an engine fault, and the checker prints it as a problem rather than hiding it. The other
+six families were accepted and compared.
+
+## Findings
+
+None. `has_legal_move()` is clean under a failable test. This is a useful negative result because the
+function is a natural place for a fast-path bug.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- `is_legal_complete()`'s fast branch at board.cpp:747-751 is exercised by the same positions
+  indirectly (via `is_legal`), but I did not isolate it with its own control.
+- `refresh_king_lines()` (board.cpp:925) recomputes five check-square sets that `has_legal_move`'s
+  pinned test does not need; seat 29 measured this as 0.056 % of instructions and bit-exact to
+  remove. I did not verify their measurement.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not test positions with more than the piece counts random play reaches early (e.g. constructed
+  32-piece middlegames with all pawns blocked).
+- Did not test `is_legal_complete` in isolation.
+
+## What I am NOT sure about
+
+- Whether some rare constructed position defeats the single-witness fast path in a way random play
+  and my seven families never reach.
+
+## Times
+
+See job8/stamps.txt.

+# REPORT — seat 07, job 9: S14 known sums (validates the setoption path and my cold-start hygiene)
+
+## What was asked / the answer / how sure
+
+**Asked:** continue the area-7 read of the UCI loop; the specific worry being that a `setoption`
+silently fails to apply, or that a harness measures warm without saying so.
+
+**Answer:** the brief's published S14 sum for set O at depth 12 reproduces **exactly**:
+**9,500,069** nodes, with the first three positions at **41,311 / 24,872 / 28,574** — all four
+numbers identical to the brief. That is a joint check: it can only land on those numbers if every
+one of the fourteen S14 options reached the engine through `uci.cpp`'s `setoption` path, and if
+every position was searched cold.
+
+**How sure:** very high for the sum (it is an exact integer match on four independent figures).
+Moderate for the general claim that *no* option is silently ignored — I validated the path with the
+options S14 uses, not with all ~50 advertised ones.
+
+## Cold-start hygiene (response to seat 10's warning)
+
+Seat 10 reported that two unrestricted searches in one process give 56,720 then 4,951 then 4,516
+nodes, that `ucinewgame` restores cold exactly, and that `Clear Hash` does **not** (it gives a third,
+deterministic value).
+
+Audit of my own work for that trap:
+
+| my harness | baseline used | verdict |
+|---|---|---|
+| job0/honesty.sh | one fresh process per check (`bench 11` … `go perft 5`) | cold, correct |
+| job1/search_stress.py | one process, but `ucinewgame` + `isready` before **every** `go` | cold per position; node figures are per-search and not compared across positions |
+| job2/uci_drive.py, job3, job5 | one process per case | cold |
+| job4/perft_board.py, job7, job8 | one process per case / no node comparison across searches | cold |
+| job9/s14_sums.py | one process per position, plus `ucinewgame` + `isready` before each `go` | cold twice over |
+
+**I never used `Clear Hash` as a baseline**, and no table of mine compares node counts across two
+searches in one warm process. The `grep` for `Clear Hash` in my folders hits only the engine's own
+`uci` option list echoed into raw output files. So no result of mine needs relabelling.
+
+## Honesty numbers
+
+All four pins still exact on this build (job0/raw/summary.txt): 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609.
+This job's figure is a **search** sum, not a bench pin, so it is evidence about options and cold
+starts rather than about node-count identity of the build itself.
+
+## The result
+
+    positions 200 depth 12
+    SUM 9500069
+      first1: nodes 41311
+      first2: nodes 24872
+      first3: nodes 28574
+
+Brief's published values: O depth 12 = 9,500,069, first three 41,311 / 24,872 / 28,574. **All four
+match exactly.**
+
+Raw: job9/run_d12.log, job9/raw/sum_d12.json (per-position nodes and the last score line for every
+position). Set O is `forge-combo29/tests_kimi5_job3/first200.fens` from branch
+`for-fable-and-opus/kimi5-work`.
+
+## What this does and does not prove
+
+**Proves:** the fourteen S14 options used here — including the boolean `NonPawnCorrection`, which is
+handled by a different branch of `setoption` than the spin options — all reach the search. A single
+one failing to apply would change the node count and could not reproduce 9,500,069.
+
+**Does not prove:** that every advertised option applies. Note in particular that `uci.cpp:289`
+resolves tunables through a **spin** parser (`apply_spin`) over `forge::tune::parameters()`, while
+the boolean `NonPawnCorrection` lives in a separate `else if` chain at `uci.cpp:403-421`. So
+`NonPawnCorrection` is *not* in the tunable table; it is a check option handled by string compare.
+That is consistent, but it does mean the two families of option go through different code, and only
+the ones S14 touches are covered by this sum.
+
+## Suspicions, not proven
+
+- An option that is *advertised* but falls through to `unknown option` would be invisible to a GUI.
+  My job1 edge-case run recorded no `unknown option` for any name I sent, but I did not send all ~50.
+- Whether `Clear Hash`'s third value (seat 10) is a defect or simply expected, since the histories are
+  not cleared: that is seat 27's S-F4 territory, which I have not checked.
+
+## What I did NOT do
+
+- Did not recompute the G depth-12 sum (18,466,239); set G is a different file and the run is longer.
+- Did not recompute O/G at depth 14.
+
+## Times
+
+See job9/stamps.txt, job9/run_d12.log.

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job0/honesty.sh b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job0/honesty.sh
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..3f8330189
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job0/honesty.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# honesty.sh EXE OUTDIR : fresh process per line, raw output saved
+set -u
+EXE="$1"; OUT="$2"
+mkdir -p "$OUT"
+run_one() {
+  name="$1"; shift
+  { printf 'uci\n'; printf 'setoption name Hash value 16\n'; printf 'setoption name Threads value 1\n';
+    printf 'isready\n'; printf 'ucinewgame\n'; printf 'isready\n'; printf '%s\n' "$@"; printf 'quit\n'; } > "$OUT/$name.in"
+  "$EXE" < "$OUT/$name.in" > "$OUT/$name.out" 2> "$OUT/$name.err"
+  echo "== $name exit=$?" >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
+  grep -E '^(info|bestmove|readyok|id )' "$OUT/$name.out" | tail -3 >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
+  grep -oE 'nodes [0-9]+' "$OUT/$name.out" | tail -1 >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
+}
+: > "$OUT/summary.txt"
+sha256sum "$EXE" >> "$OUT/summary.txt"
+run_one bench11 "bench 11"
+run_one bench13 "bench 13"
+run_one bench16 "bench 16"
+run_one perft5 "go perft 5"
+echo "--- summary ---"; cat "$OUT/summary.txt"

@@ -0,0 +1,6 @@
+These two harnesses pipelined a `go` with the following isready/quit and are INVALID.
+Seat 19 (19-F12, relayed by the coordinator 2026-11-16) showed this build answers a
+fabricated `bestmove ... 0 nodes` when stdin closes mid-search.
+  job1/limits_probe.sh   - kept for the record, its output raw_limits/ is NOT a result
+  job1/searchstress.sh   - kept for the record, its output raw_asan/ is NOT a result
+Replacement harnesses that never pipeline: job1/uci_drive.py, job1/search_stress.py.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/PREDICTION_job1.md b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/PREDICTION_job1.md
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..71a3e1d04
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/PREDICTION_job1.md
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+# PREDICTION — seat 07, area 7, job 1 (read src/search.cpp, 2753 lines, at 6b98f217)
+
+Written before reading src/search.cpp beyond `wc -l` and before any measuring command of this job.
+Falsifiers in brackets; a number outside its range kills that prediction and is reported as such.
+
+1. Suspicious lines worth a FINDINGS line: 3 to 9. [0-2 or >=10 kills it]
+2. Suspicious lines I can turn into a TEST with a demonstrable command (a position + UCI line, or a sanitizer
+   report): 1 to 4. [0 or >=5 kills it]
+3. Of those tested, at least one is in the time manager or in the `go`-parameter parsing path rather than in
+   alpha-beta pruning proper. [none there kills it]
+4. A TEXT PATCH (unified diff, `patch -p1`, no fuzz) is produced for at least one fault, and with the patch applied
+   all four honesty numbers stay equal (312866 / 862329 / 3024920 / 4865609). [a changed number or a non-applying
+   patch kills it]
+5. The patch changes no node count on any of the three benches. [any delta kills it]
+
+Predicted (guess, not a result): the NNUE accumulator update path is the likeliest place for an uninitialised read,
+because refresh-vs-incremental has to agree exactly; the time manager is the likeliest place for an overflow when the
+clock is tiny.
+
+stamp of writing: see stamps.txt line 1 (date -u, written by the script that follows this commit).

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/cap_probe.sh b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/cap_probe.sh
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..aac429ad2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/cap_probe.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# cap_probe.sh EXE OUTDIR : feed FENs with many mobile pieces; count pseudo-legal/legal moves via perft 1
+set -u
+EXE="$1"; OUT="$2"; mkdir -p "$OUT"
+i=0
+while IFS='|' read -r name fen; do
+  [ -z "${name:-}" ] && continue
+  i=$((i+1))
+  { echo uci; echo "setoption name Hash value 16"; echo "setoption name Threads value 1"; echo isready
+    echo ucinewgame; echo isready
+    echo "position fen $fen"
+    echo isready
+    echo "go perft 1"
+    echo isready
+    echo "go depth 4"
+    echo isready
+    echo quit; } > "$OUT/$name.in"
+  timeout 120 "$EXE" < "$OUT/$name.in" > "$OUT/$name.out" 2> "$OUT/$name.err"
+  rc=$?
+  n=$(grep -c '^[a-h][1-8][a-h][1-8]' "$OUT/$name.out")
+  echo "$name rc=$rc rootmoves=$n errlines=$(wc -l < "$OUT/$name.err")" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"
+done < "$3"

+# Candidate high-branching positions. The engine's MoveList capacity is 256 (board.hpp:108) and
+# MovePicker::moves_ is a 256-slot array (search.cpp). A legal position cannot exceed 218 moves,
+# so perft must stay under 256; this file checks the engine agrees with python-chess where the
+# generator is stressed most.
+plain_queens|QQQQBBNN/RRRRBBBB/NNNNPPPP/QQQQPPPP/8/8/pppppppp/pppppppp w - - 0 1
+promo_heavy|4k3/PPPPPPPP/PPPPPPPP/8/8/8/pppppppp/pppppppp w - - 0 1
+knight_swarm|NNNNNNNN/8/8/8/8/8/8/nnnnnnnn w - - 0 1
+many_rooks|4k3/RRRRRRRR/8/8/8/8/8/rrrrrrrK w - - 0 1

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/limits_probe.sh b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/limits_probe.sh
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..1f30e5845
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/limits_probe.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,63 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# limits_probe.sh EXE OUTDIR : one engine process per case; each case is a committed .in file.
+# Every case: uci, Hash 16, Threads 1, isready, ucinewgame, isready, <lines>, isready, quit.
+set -u
+EXE="$1"; OUT="$2"; mkdir -p "$OUT"; : > "$OUT/summary.txt"
+CASES="$OUT/cases"
+mkdir -p "$CASES"
+run() {
+  name="$1"; shift
+  {
+    echo uci; echo "setoption name Hash value 16"; echo "setoption name Threads value 1"; echo isready
+    echo ucinewgame; echo isready
+    for line in "$@"; do echo "$line"; echo isready; done
+    echo quit
+  } > "$CASES/$name.in"
+  timeout 300 "$EXE" < "$CASES/$name.in" > "$CASES/$name.out" 2> "$CASES/$name.err"
+  rc=$?
+  san=$(grep -cE 'AddressSanitizer|runtime error|LeakSanitizer' "$CASES/$name.err" || true)
+  bm=$(grep -c '^bestmove' "$CASES/$name.out" || true)
+  inf_bad=$(grep -cE 'info string (invalid|unknown|illegal)' "$CASES/$name.out" || true)
+  printf '%-26s rc=%-3s sanitizer=%-2s bestmove=%-2s infostrings=%s\n' "$name" "$rc" "$san" "$bm" "$inf_bad" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"
+  if [ "$san" != 0 ]; then echo "  --- sanitizer output: $CASES/$name.err ---" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"; fi
+}
+P="position startpos"
+run depth0              "$P" "go depth 0"
+run depth_huge          "$P" "go depth 999999"
+run nodes0              "$P" "go nodes 0"
+run nodes_max           "$P" "go nodes 18446744073709551615"
+run nodes_overflow      "$P" "go nodes 99999999999999999999999999"
+run movetime0           "$P" "go movetime 0"
+run movetime_neg        "$P" "go movetime -5"
+run movetime_huge       "$P" "go movetime 9223372036854775807"
+run mate0               "$P" "go mate 0"
+run mate2               "$P" "go mate 2"
+run wtime0              "$P" "go wtime 0 btime 0"
+run wtime1              "$P" "go wtime 1 btime 1"
+run wtime_noval         "$P" "go wtime"
+run movestogo0          "$P" "go wtime 1000 btime 1000 movestogo 0"
+run movestogo_huge      "$P" "go wtime 1000 btime 1000 movestogo 2147483647"
+run movestogo_neg       "$P" "go wtime 1000 btime 1000 movestogo -3"
+run searchmoves_none    "$P" "go depth 4 searchmoves"
+run searchmoves_one     "$P" "go depth 4 searchmoves e2e4"
+run searchmoves_all     "$P" "go depth 3 searchmoves a2a3 a2a4 b1a3 b1c3 b2b3 b2b4 c2c3 c2c4 d2d3 d2d4 e2e3 e2e4 f2f3 f2f4 g1f3 g1h3 g2g3 g2g4 h2h3 h2h4"
+run searchmoves_illegal "$P" "go depth 4 searchmoves e2e5"
+run softnodes0          "$P" "go softnodes 0"
+run softnodes100        "$P" "go softnodes 100"
+run infinite_stop       "$P" "go infinite" "stop"
+run ponder_quit         "$P" "go ponder depth 5" "quit"
+run depth_and_mate      "$P" "go depth 6 mate 1"
+run multipv0            "setoption name MultiPV value 0" "$P" "go depth 4"
+run multipv8            "setoption name MultiPV value 8" "$P" "go depth 5"
+run multipv8_mate       "setoption name MultiPV value 8" "$P" "position fen 7k/5KQ1/8/8/8/8/8/8 w - - 0 1" "go depth 4"
+run multipv8_1move      "setoption name MultiPV value 8" "$P" "position fen 7k/6Q1/6K1/8/8/8/8/8 b - - 0 1" "go depth 4"
+run stalemate_root      "position fen 7k/5Q2/6K1/8/8/8/8/8 b - - 0 1" "go depth 5"
+run mate_root           "position fen 7k/6Q1/6K1/8/8/8/8/8 b - - 0 1" "go depth 5"
+run no_legal_moves_d1   "position fen 7k/5Q2/6K1/8/8/8/8/8 b - - 0 1" "go depth 1"
+run restricted_empty    "position fen 7k/5Q2/6K1/8/8/8/8/8 b - - 0 1" "go depth 3 searchmoves a1a2"
+run halfmove99          "position fen 8/8/8/4k3/8/8/4K3/R7 w - - 99 80" "go depth 10"
+run halfmove100         "position fen 8/8/8/4k3/8/8/4K3/R7 w - - 100 80" "go depth 6"
+run repeated_threefold  "$P moves e2e4 e7e5 e1e2 e8e7 e2e1 e7e8 e1e2 e8e7 e2e1 e7e8" "go depth 8"
+run fifty_clock_wrap    "position fen 8/8/8/4k3/8/8/4K3/R7 w - - 65535 1" "go depth 6"
+run mate_distance_deep  "position fen 8/8/8/8/8/8/8/K6k w - - 0 1" "go depth 64"
+run depth64_start       "$P" "go depth 64 nodes 200000"

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/search_stress.py b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/search_stress.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..37b848c61
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/search_stress.py
@@ -0,0 +1,131 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""search_stress.py EXE FENS OUTDIR DEPTH [TIMEOUT_S]
+
+For every FEN: fresh `position fen`, `isready` to readyok, `go depth D`, then read
+stdout until `bestmove` before the next command. Nothing is ever pipelined and
+stdin is never closed mid-search. Each bestmove is checked with python-chess; a
+bestmove that is illegal, or `0000` on a position that has legal moves, is recorded.
+
+Writes OUTDIR/<index>.json and OUTDIR/all.json.
+"""
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+
+import chess
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
+from uci_drive import LineReader  # noqa: E402
+import subprocess  # noqa: E402
+import time  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def main():
+    exe, fens_path, outdir, depth = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], int(sys.argv[4])
+    timeout_s = float(sys.argv[5]) if len(sys.argv) > 5 else 120.0
+    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
+    fens = [l.strip() for l in open(fens_path, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
+    rows = []
+    errpath = os.path.join(outdir, "stderr_all.txt")
+    errfh = open(errpath, "w", encoding="utf-8")
+    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                            stderr=errfh, text=True, bufsize=1)
+    reader = LineReader(proc.stdout)
+
+    def send(cmd):
+        proc.stdin.write(cmd + "\n")
+        proc.stdin.flush()
+
+    def drain(tag, timeout=120):
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+        while True:
+            line = reader.readline(deadline)
+            if line is None:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"no readyok after {tag}")
+            if line.strip() == "readyok":
+                return
+
+    send("uci")
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 60
+    while True:
+        line = reader.readline(deadline)
+        if line is None or line.strip() == "uciok":
+            break
+    for opt in ["Hash value 16", "Threads value 1",
+                "LmrQuietBase value 93", "LmrQuietDivisor value 205",
+                "LmrNoisyBase value 13", "LmrNoisyDivisor value 333",
+                "LmrHistoryDivisor value 5643", "NullMoveBase value 5",
+                "LmpBase value 8", "HistoryPruneMultiplier value 2220",
+                "HistoryBonusQuadratic value 24", "HistoryBonusLinear value 54",
+                "HistoryBonusMax value 2212", "SingularDepth value 6",
+                "IirDepth value 2", "NonPawnCorrection value true"]:
+        send("setoption name " + opt)
+        send("isready")
+        drain("setoption " + opt)
+    send("ucinewgame")
+    send("isready")
+    drain("ucinewgame")
+
+    for index, fen in enumerate(fens):
+        rec = {"index": index, "fen": fen, "depth": depth}
+        try:
+            board = chess.Board(fen)
+            rec["pythonchess_ok"] = True
+        except ValueError as exc:
+            board = None
+            rec["pythonchess_ok"] = False
+            rec["pythonchess_error"] = str(exc)
+        send("position fen " + fen)
+        send("isready")
+        drain("position " + fen)
+        send(f"go depth {depth}")
+        best = None
+        nodes = None
+        last_info = None
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
+        while True:
+            line = reader.readline(deadline)
+            if line is None:
+                rec["hang"] = True
+                break
+            if line.startswith("info ") and " nodes " in line:
+                m = re.search(r" nodes (\d+)", line)
+                if m:
+                    nodes = int(m.group(1))
+                last_info = line.strip()
+            if line.startswith("bestmove"):
+                best = line.split()[1]
+                break
+        rec["best"] = best
+        rec["nodes"] = nodes
+        rec["last_info"] = last_info
+        rec["illegal_answer"] = False
+        if board is not None and best and best != "0000":
+            try:
+                move = chess.Move.from_uci(best)
+                rec["illegal_answer"] = move not in board.legal_moves
+            except ValueError:
+                rec["illegal_answer"] = True
+        elif board is not None and best == "0000":
+            rec["illegal_answer"] = board.legal_moves.count() > 0
+        rows.append(rec)
+        if index % 25 == 0:
+            print(f"{index}/{len(fens)} {fen} -> {best} nodes={nodes}", flush=True)
+        json.dump(rec, open(os.path.join(outdir, f"{index:04d}.json"), "w"), indent=1)
+    send("quit")
+    try:
+        proc.wait(timeout=60)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        proc.kill()
+    errfh.close()
+    json.dump(rows, open(os.path.join(outdir, "all.json"), "w"), indent=1)
+    hangs = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("hang"))
+    bad = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("illegal_answer"))
+    zero = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("nodes") == 0)
+    print(f"SUMMARY cases={len(rows)} hangs={hangs} illegal_answers={bad} zero_nodes={zero}", flush=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/searchstress.sh b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/searchstress.sh
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..5436d0936
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/searchstress.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# searchstress.sh EXE FENS OUTDIR : run every FEN at go depth 10 S14, one process per 25 FENs,
+# report ASan/UBSan lines and illegal bestmoves (checked by python-chess).
+set -u
+EXE="$1"; FENS="$2"; OUT="$3"
+mkdir -p "$OUT"
+S14="setoption name LmrQuietBase value 93
+setoption name LmrQuietDivisor value 205
+setoption name LmrNoisyBase value 13
+setoption name LmrNoisyDivisor value 333
+setoption name LmrHistoryDivisor value 5643
+setoption name NullMoveBase value 5
+setoption name LmpBase value 8
+setoption name HistoryPruneMultiplier value 2220
+setoption name HistoryBonusQuadratic value 24
+setoption name HistoryBonusLinear value 54
+setoption name HistoryBonusMax value 2212
+setoption name SingularDepth value 6
+setoption name IirDepth value 2
+setoption name NonPawnCorrection value true"
+: > "$OUT/summary.txt"
+split -l 25 -d "$FENS" "$OUT/chunk_"
+for chunk in "$OUT"/chunk_*; do
+  base=$(basename "$chunk")
+  {
+    echo uci
+    echo "setoption name Hash value 16"
+    echo "setoption name Threads value 1"
+    echo isready
+    printf '%s\n' "$S14"
+    echo isready
+    echo ucinewgame
+    echo isready
+    n=0
+    while IFS= read -r fen; do
+      [ -z "$fen" ] && continue
+      n=$((n+1))
+      echo "echo ---FEN $n $fen"
+      echo "position fen $fen"
+      echo isready
+      echo "go depth 10"
+      echo isready
+    done < "$chunk"
+    echo quit
+  } > "$OUT/$base.in"
+  timeout 900 "$EXE" < "$OUT/$base.in" > "$OUT/$base.out" 2> "$OUT/$base.err"
+  rc=$?
+  san=$(grep -cE 'AddressSanitizer|runtime error' "$OUT/$base.err" || true)
+  echo "$base rc=$rc sanitizer_lines=$san bestmoves=$(grep -c '^bestmove' "$OUT/$base.out")" | tee -a "$OUT/summary.txt"
+done

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/uci_drive.py b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/uci_drive.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..069993260
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job1/uci_drive.py
@@ -0,0 +1,210 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""uci_drive.py EXE CASEFILE OUTDIR [timeout_s]  --  drives one engine process per case.
+
+Case file format: blocks starting with "### name", then one UCI command per line.
+A line "go ..." is sent and then only waited on (no other command goes in until
+`bestmove` arrives, or the timeout fires: the case is recorded as a HANG and the
+process is killed). "# about-input" marks a case whose answer may legitimately be
+an "invalid ..." info string.
+
+Every `setoption` and `position` is followed by `isready`, and every line up to
+`readyok` is read before the next command is sent.
+
+Each case writes OUTDIR/<name>.json (record) and OUTDIR/<name>.err (raw stderr).
+"""
+import json
+import os
+import queue
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import threading
+import time
+
+BAD = ("unknown option", "invalid value", "invalid FEN", "illegal move")
+
+
+class LineReader:
+    def __init__(self, stream):
+        self.q = queue.Queue()
+        self.stream = stream
+        threading.Thread(target=self._pump, daemon=True).start()
+
+    def _pump(self):
+        while True:
+            try:
+                line = self.stream.readline()
+            except Exception:
+                break
+            if not line:
+                break
+            self.q.put(line)
+        self.q.put(None)
+
+    def readline(self, deadline):
+        remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
+        if remaining <= 0:
+            return None
+        try:
+            return self.q.get(timeout=remaining)
+        except queue.Empty:
+            return None
+
+
+def parse_cases(path):
+    cases, name, lines, about = [], None, [], False
+    for raw in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
+        line = raw.rstrip("\n")
+        if line.startswith("### "):
+            if name is not None:
+                cases.append((name, lines, about))
+            name, lines, about = line[4:].strip().split()[0], [], False
+            continue
+        if line.strip() == "# about-input":
+            about = True
+            continue
+        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        lines.append(line.strip())
+    if name is not None:
+        cases.append((name, lines, about))
+    return cases
+
+
+def run_case(exe, name, lines, about_input, outdir, timeout_s):
+    rec = {"case": name, "commands": lines, "violations": [], "sanitizer": [],
+           "hang": False, "bestmoves": [], "last_info": None, "exit": None, "seconds": None}
+    errpath = os.path.join(outdir, name + ".err")
+    errfh = open(errpath, "w", encoding="utf-8")
+    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                            stderr=errfh, text=True, bufsize=1)
+    started = time.monotonic()
+    reader = LineReader(proc.stdout)
+
+    def send(cmd):
+        try:
+            proc.stdin.write(cmd + "\n")
+            proc.stdin.flush()
+            return True
+        except Exception:
+            return False
+
+    def note(line):
+        if line.startswith("info string") and any(b in line for b in BAD):
+            rec["violations"].append(line.strip())
+        if line.startswith("info ") and " pv" in line:
+            rec["last_info"] = line.strip()
+
+    def drain(timeout=60):
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+        while True:
+            line = reader.readline(deadline)
+            if line is None:
+                return False
+            note(line)
+            if line.strip() == "readyok":
+                return True
+
+    send("uci")
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + 60
+    while True:
+        line = reader.readline(deadline)
+        if line is None or line.strip() == "uciok":
+            break
+    send("isready")
+    drain()
+
+    hanging = False
+    pending = list(lines)
+    while pending and not hanging:
+        cmd = pending.pop(0)
+        if cmd.startswith(("setoption", "position", "ucinewgame", "isready")):
+            send(cmd)
+            if not cmd.startswith("isready"):
+                send("isready")
+            drain()
+            continue
+        if not send(cmd):
+            break
+        if cmd.startswith("go"):
+            late = []
+            if "infinite" in cmd or "ponder" in cmd:
+                while pending and pending[0].startswith(("stop", "ponderhit")):
+                    late.append(pending.pop(0))
+            best = None
+            # An infinite/ponder search cannot answer before its stop line arrives.
+            deadline = time.monotonic() + (0.8 if late else timeout_s)
+            while True:
+                line = reader.readline(deadline)
+                if line is None:
+                    break
+                note(line)
+                if line.startswith("bestmove"):
+                    best = line.strip()
+                    break
+            if best is None and late:
+                for extra in late:
+                    send(extra)
+                deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
+                while True:
+                    line = reader.readline(deadline)
+                    if line is None:
+                        break
+                    note(line)
+                    if line.startswith("bestmove"):
+                        best = line.strip()
+                        break
+            if best is None:
+                rec["hang"] = True
+                hanging = True
+                break
+            rec["bestmoves"].append(best)
+    if not hanging:
+        send("quit")
+    try:
+        proc.wait(timeout=30)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        try:
+            proc.kill()
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+        try:
+            proc.wait()
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+    rec["exit"] = proc.returncode
+    errfh.flush()
+    errfh.close()
+    with open(errpath, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        for line in fh:
+            if "Sanitizer" in line or "runtime error" in line or "SUMMARY:" in line:
+                rec["sanitizer"].append(line.strip())
+    try:
+        if proc.poll() is None:
+            proc.kill()
+    except Exception:
+        pass
+    rec["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
+    if about_input:
+        rec["violations"] = [v for v in rec["violations"] if "invalid FEN" not in v]
+    with open(os.path.join(outdir, name + ".json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        json.dump(rec, fh, indent=1)
+    return rec
+
+
+def main():
+    exe, casefile, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
+    timeout_s = float(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 60.0
+    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
+    rows = []
+    for name, lines, about in parse_cases(casefile):
+        rec = run_case(exe, name, lines, about, outdir, timeout_s)
+        rows.append(rec)
+        last = rec["bestmoves"][-1] if rec["bestmoves"] else "-"
+        print(f"{name:28s} hang={int(rec['hang'])} san={len(rec['sanitizer'])} "
+              f"viol={len(rec['violations'])} bm={last[:20]:20s} {rec['seconds']}s", flush=True)
+    with open(os.path.join(outdir, "all.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        json.dump(rows, fh, indent=1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job10/go_stop_cycle.py b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job10/go_stop_cycle.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..9356b9417
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job10/go_stop_cycle.py
@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""go_stop_cycle.py EXE OUTDIR [ROUNDS]
+
+The normal-play shape a GUI produces: `position ...`, `go infinite`, wait, `stop`,
+`bestmove`, then the GUI plays the move and sends the next `position` + `go`.
+This program does that for ROUNDS plies and asserts, per round:
+
+  * a bestmove arrives within the timeout (a hang is a failure, recorded and the run stops);
+  * the bestmove is legal in the position that was sent (python-chess), or is 0000 exactly when
+    the position has no legal move;
+  * after `stop`, the very next `go` still searches (a stale stop flag would make it
+    answer instantly with 0 nodes, which is recorded rather than silently accepted).
+
+It also interleaves one `go ponder` + `ponderhit` round and one `go depth 200` + `stop` round,
+because those take different branches of uci.cpp's stop/quit handling.
+
+Every failure is printed with the round number and the raw lines involved.
+"""
+import os
+import queue
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import threading
+import time
+
+import chess
+
+
+class Reader:
+    def __init__(self, stream):
+        self.q = queue.Queue()
+        threading.Thread(target=self._pump, args=(stream,), daemon=True).start()
+
+    def _pump(self, s):
+        for line in s:
+            self.q.put(line)
+        self.q.put(None)
+
+    def get(self, timeout):
+        try:
+            return self.q.get(timeout=timeout)
+        except queue.Empty:
+            return None
+
+
+def main():
+    exe, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
+    rounds = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 40
+    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
+    log = open(os.path.join(outdir, "transcript.txt"), "w", encoding="utf-8")
+
+    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                            stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)
+    r = Reader(proc.stdout)
+    failures = []
+
+    def send(c):
+        proc.stdin.write(c + "\n")
+        proc.stdin.flush()
+        log.write(">> " + c + "\n")
+        log.flush()
+
+    def drain(tag, timeout=120):
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+        while True:
+            line = r.get(max(0.01, deadline - time.monotonic()))
+            if line is None:
+                failures.append(f"{tag}: no readyok")
+                return False
+            log.write("<< " + line)
+            if line.strip() == "readyok":
+                return True
+
+    def wait_bestmove(tag, timeout=60):
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+        nodes = None
+        while True:
+            line = r.get(max(0.01, deadline - time.monotonic()))
+            if line is None:
+                failures.append(f"{tag}: NO bestmove within {timeout}s (hang)")
+                return None, nodes
+            log.write("<< " + line)
+            if line.startswith("info depth") and " nodes " in line:
+                m = re.search(r" nodes (\d+) ", line)
+                if m:
+                    nodes = int(m.group(1))
+            if line.startswith("bestmove"):
+                return line.split()[1], nodes
+
+    send("uci")
+    while True:
+        line = r.get(30)
+        if line is None or line.strip() == "uciok":
+            break
+        log.write("<< " + line)
+    send("setoption name Hash value 16")
+    send("isready")
+    drain("setoption Hash")
+
+    board = chess.Board()
+    history = []
+    for round_no in range(1, rounds + 1):
+        fen = board.fen()
+        send("position fen " + fen)
+        send("isready")
+        if not drain(f"round {round_no} position"):
+            break
+        # Round types: mostly infinite+stop (the normal GUI shape), one ponderhit, one deep+stop.
+        if round_no == rounds // 2:
+            send("go ponder depth 8")
+            time.sleep(0.25)
+            send("ponderhit")
+            best, nodes = wait_bestmove(f"round {round_no} ponderhit", 60)
+        elif round_no == rounds - 1:
+            send("go depth 200")
+            time.sleep(0.20)
+            send("stop")
+            best, nodes = wait_bestmove(f"round {round_no} deep+stop", 60)
+        else:
+            send("go infinite")
+            time.sleep(0.10)
+            send("stop")
+            best, nodes = wait_bestmove(f"round {round_no} infinite+stop", 60)
+
+        if best is None:
+            break
+        legal = [m.uci() for m in board.legal_moves]
+        if best == "0000":
+            if legal:
+                failures.append(f"round {round_no}: bestmove 0000 but {len(legal)} legal moves in {fen}")
+                break
+        elif best not in legal:
+            failures.append(f"round {round_no}: ILLEGAL bestmove {best} in {fen} (legal: {len(legal)})")
+            break
+        if nodes is None:
+            # A missing nodes figure is NOT a pass (seat 19's rule): it means no depth line was
+            # parsed, so this round measured nothing about whether the search really ran.
+            failures.append(f"round {round_no}: no 'info depth ... nodes' line was parsed, so the "
+                            f"round measured nothing (bestmove {best})")
+            break
+        if nodes == 0:
+            failures.append(f"round {round_no}: search answered 0 nodes after a stop/ponderhit "
+                            f"(stale stop flag?) bestmove {best}")
+            break
+        if round_no % 7 == 0:
+            send("ucinewgame")
+            send("isready")
+            drain(f"round {round_no} ucinewgame")
+        board.push(chess.Move.from_uci(best))
+        history.append(best)
+
+    # Final sanity: one plain search must still work after all that.
+    send("position startpos")
+    send("isready")
+    drain("final position")
+    send("go depth 6")
+    final_best, final_nodes = wait_bestmove("final go depth 6", 60)
+    send("quit")
+    try:
+        proc.wait(timeout=30)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        proc.kill()
+    log.close()
+
+    print(f"rounds requested {rounds}, plies played {len(history)}")
+    print(f"final search after the cycle: bestmove {final_best} nodes {final_nodes}")
+    if final_nodes is None:
+        failures.append("final go depth 6 produced no nodes line: the engine never searched")
+    elif final_nodes == 0:
+        failures.append("final go depth 6 produced 0 nodes: the engine never searched")
+    for f in failures:
+        print("  FAIL " + f)
+    if failures:
+        print(f"RESULT: {len(failures)} failure(s)")
+        sys.exit(1)
+    if len(history) < rounds - 2:
+        print("RESULT: the cycle did not complete; see failures above")
+        sys.exit(1)
+    print("RESULT: every go/stop and go/ponderhit cycle returned a legal move with nodes > 0, "
+          "and a plain search still worked afterwards")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job11/clock_behaviour.py b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job11/clock_behaviour.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..54e07d44a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job11/clock_behaviour.py
@@ -0,0 +1,184 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""clock_behaviour.py EXE OUTDIR
+
+A GUI-style clock loop: for each time control, play a short self-game where every move is a
+`go wtime .. btime .. winc .. binc [movestogo ..]`, the engine's bestmove is played on a
+python-chess board, and the clock is decremented in real time. For every search it records:
+
+  * wall time from sending `go` to reading `bestmove` (monotonic),
+  * the engine's own reported `time` and `nodes`,
+  * whether the move was legal,
+  * whether the search exceeded the time the engine had left (a loss on time).
+
+It also checks the two things a clock bug shows as in normal play: answering with an illegal
+move under time pressure, and overrunning the remaining clock.
+"""
+import os
+import queue
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import threading
+import time
+
+import chess
+
+
+class Reader:
+    def __init__(self, stream):
+        self.q = queue.Queue()
+        threading.Thread(target=self._pump, args=(stream,), daemon=True).start()
+
+    def _pump(self, s):
+        for line in s:
+            self.q.put(line)
+        self.q.put(None)
+
+    def get(self, timeout):
+        try:
+            return self.q.get(timeout=timeout)
+        except queue.Empty:
+            return None
+
+
+def play_game(exe, wtime_ms, winc_ms, movestogo, max_plies, outdir, tag):
+    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                            stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)
+    r = Reader(proc.stdout)
+    rows = []
+    failures = []
+
+    def send(c):
+        proc.stdin.write(c + "\n")
+        proc.stdin.flush()
+
+    def drain():
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 60
+        while True:
+            line = r.get(max(0.01, deadline - time.monotonic()))
+            if line is None:
+                raise RuntimeError("no readyok")
+            if line.strip() == "readyok":
+                return
+
+    send("uci")
+    while True:
+        line = r.get(30)
+        if line is None or line.strip() == "uciok":
+            break
+    send("setoption name Hash value 16")
+    send("setoption name Threads value 1")
+    # The book answers clock searches (uci.cpp:525-527 game_search), with NO info depth line.
+    # A book move is legitimate, but it would leave this test measuring nothing, so the book
+    # is turned off here and book behaviour is reported separately.
+    send("setoption name OwnBook value false")
+    send("isready")
+    drain()
+
+    board = chess.Board()
+    white_ms = black_ms = wtime_ms
+    for ply in range(max_plies):
+        if board.is_game_over():
+            break
+        fen = board.fen()
+        send("position fen " + fen)
+        send("isready")
+        drain()
+        side = "w" if board.turn == chess.WHITE else "b"
+        left_ms = white_ms if board.turn == chess.WHITE else black_ms
+        go = (f"go wtime {white_ms} btime {black_ms} winc {winc_ms} binc {winc_ms}")
+        if movestogo > 0:
+            go += f" movestogo {movestogo}"
+        t0 = time.monotonic()
+        send(go)
+        best = None
+        eng_time = eng_nodes = None
+        while True:
+            line = r.get(max(0.01, 30.0))
+            if line is None:
+                failures.append(f"{tag} ply {ply}: no bestmove in 30 s (hang)")
+                break
+            if line.startswith("info depth") and " nodes " in line:
+                m = re.search(r" nodes (\d+) ", line)
+                if m:
+                    eng_nodes = int(m.group(1))
+                m = re.search(r" time (\d+) ", line)
+                if m:
+                    eng_time = int(m.group(1))
+            if line.startswith("bestmove"):
+                best = line.split()[1]
+                break
+        elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - t0) * 1000.0
+        if best is None:
+            break
+        legal = [m.uci() for m in board.legal_moves]
+        ok_move = (best in legal) if legal else (best == "0000")
+        overrun = elapsed_ms > left_ms + 5   # 5 ms of measurement slack
+        rows.append({"ply": ply, "side": side, "go": go, "left_ms": left_ms,
+                     "wall_ms": round(elapsed_ms, 2), "engine_time_ms": eng_time,
+                     "nodes": eng_nodes, "bestmove": best, "legal": ok_move,
+                     "overrun": overrun, "nodes_missing": eng_nodes is None})
+        if eng_nodes is None:
+            failures.append(f"{tag} ply {ply}: no 'info depth ... nodes' line, so this search "
+                            f"measured nothing (bestmove {best})")
+            break
+        if not ok_move:
+            failures.append(f"{tag} ply {ply}: illegal bestmove {best} in {fen}")
+            break
+        if overrun:
+            failures.append(f"{tag} ply {ply}: took {elapsed_ms:.1f} ms with {left_ms} ms left")
+        spend = int(min(elapsed_ms, left_ms))
+        if board.turn == chess.WHITE:
+            white_ms = max(0, white_ms - spend) + winc_ms
+        else:
+            black_ms = max(0, black_ms - spend) + winc_ms
+        board.push(chess.Move.from_uci(best))
+
+    send("quit")
+    try:
+        proc.wait(timeout=20)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        proc.kill()
+    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(os.path.join(outdir, tag + ".txt"), "w") as fh:
+        fh.write("go | left_ms | wall_ms | engine_time_ms | nodes | bestmove | legal | overrun\n")
+        for row in rows:
+            fh.write(f"{row['go']} | {row['left_ms']} | {row['wall_ms']} | "
+                     f"{row['engine_time_ms']} | {row['nodes']} | {row['bestmove']} | "
+                     f"{row['legal']} | {row['overrun']}\n")
+    return rows, failures
+
+
+def main():
+    exe, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
+    controls = [
+        ("sudden_1000", 1000, 10, 0, 24),
+        ("sudden_10000", 10000, 100, 0, 24),
+        ("mtg_1", 1000, 0, 1, 12),
+        ("mtg_2", 1000, 0, 2, 12),
+        ("mtg_40", 1000, 0, 40, 16),
+        ("tiny_100", 100, 0, 0, 12),
+        ("tiny_30", 30, 0, 0, 10),
+        ("tiny_10", 10, 0, 0, 8),
+        ("zero_0", 0, 0, 0, 6),
+    ]
+    all_failures = []
+    for tag, wt, inc, mtg, plies in controls:
+        rows, failures = play_game(exe, wt, inc, mtg, plies, outdir, tag)
+        all_failures.extend(failures)
+        overruns = sum(1 for r in rows if r["overrun"])
+        missing = sum(1 for r in rows if r["nodes_missing"])
+        worst = max((r["wall_ms"] for r in rows), default=0.0)
+        print(f"{tag:14s} plies {len(rows):3d}  overruns {overruns}  rows without nodes {missing}  "
+              f"worst wall {worst:8.1f} ms", flush=True)
+    print()
+    for f in all_failures[:20]:
+        print("  FAIL " + f)
+    if all_failures:
+        print(f"RESULT: {len(all_failures)} failure(s)")
+        sys.exit(1)
+    print("RESULT: no illegal move under time pressure, no overrun of the remaining clock")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job12/eval_symmetry.py b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job12/eval_symmetry.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..a1c26e41f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job12/eval_symmetry.py
@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""eval_symmetry.py EXE FENS OUTDIR
+
+The engine's `eval` command prints `info string eval hce <a> nnue <b> total <c>`.
+
+`eval` prints WHITE-POSITIVE values regardless of the side to move: src/eval.cpp:509 returns
+`board.side_to_move() == White ? tapered : -tapered`, verified empirically (the same board with
+White to move prints +820 and with Black to move -800). Therefore the evaluation of a position
+must equal the NEGATION of the evaluation of its colour-flipped mirror.
+
+My first version of this script compared the two as equal and reported 588 "asymmetric"
+values that were in fact identical numbers -- the mirror was correct and my comparison was
+wrong. Fixed here; the control below is what makes the corrected comparison trustworthy.
+
+Asserts every number was PARSED (a missing `info string eval` line fails loudly, never passes),
+and asserts the control: a deliberately non-symmetric FEN pair must NOT be reported as equal.
+"""
+import os
+import re
+import queue
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import threading
+
+import chess
+
+EVAL_LINE = re.compile(r"info string eval hce (-?\d+) nnue (-?\d+) total (-?\d+)")
+
+
+class Reader:
+    def __init__(self, stream):
+        self.q = queue.Queue()
+        threading.Thread(target=self._pump, args=(stream,), daemon=True).start()
+
+    def _pump(self, s):
+        for line in s:
+            self.q.put(line)
+        self.q.put(None)
+
+    def get(self, timeout=60.0):
+        try:
+            return self.q.get(timeout=timeout)
+        except queue.Empty:
+            return None
+
+
+def eval_fens(exe, fens):
+    """One fresh process for all the FENs, evals only (no search), returns {fen: (hce,nnue,total)}."""
+    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                            stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)
+    r = Reader(proc.stdout)
+
+    def send(c):
+        proc.stdin.write(c + "\n")
+        proc.stdin.flush()
+
+    def drain():
+        while True:
+            line = r.get()
+            if line is None:
+                raise RuntimeError("no readyok")
+            if line.strip() == "readyok":
+                return
+
+    send("uci")
+    while True:
+        line = r.get(30)
+        if line is None or line.strip() == "uciok":
+            break
+    send("setoption name Hash value 16")
+    send("isready")
+    drain()
+    out = {}
+    for fen in fens:
+        send("position fen " + fen)
+        send("isready")
+        drain()
+        send("eval")
+        m = None
+        deadline_lines = 0
+        while m is None:
+            line = r.get(30)
+            if line is None:
+                raise RuntimeError(f"no eval answer for {fen}")
+            if line.startswith("info string eval"):
+                m = EVAL_LINE.search(line)
+                if m is None:
+                    raise RuntimeError(f"eval line did not parse: {line!r}")
+        out[fen] = tuple(int(g) for g in m.groups())
+        deadline_lines += 1
+    send("quit")
+    try:
+        proc.wait(timeout=20)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        proc.kill()
+    return out
+
+
+def mirror_fen(fen):
+    b = chess.Board(fen)
+    m = b.mirror()
+    return m.fen()
+
+
+def main():
+    exe, fens_path, outdir = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
+    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
+    fens = [l.strip() for l in open(fens_path, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
+    fens = [f for f in fens if len(f.split()) == 6]
+    mirrors = [mirror_fen(f) for f in fens]
+    vals = eval_fens(exe, fens + mirrors)
+
+    rows, bad = [], 0
+    for fen, mir in zip(fens, mirrors):
+        a = vals[fen]
+        b = vals[mir]
+        for i, name in enumerate(("hce", "nnue", "total")):
+            if a[i] != -b[i]:
+                bad += 1
+                rows.append(f"ASYMMETRIC {name}: {a[i]} vs mirrored {b[i]}  fen {fen}")
+    with open(os.path.join(outdir, "differences.txt"), "w") as fh:
+        fh.write("\n".join(rows) + ("\n" if rows else ""))
+
+    # Control: two clearly different positions must not compare equal, else the comparison is dead.
+    ctrl = ["4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w - - 0 1", "4k3/8/8/8/8/8/3Q4/4K3 w - - 0 1"]
+    cvals = eval_fens(exe, ctrl)
+    control_works = cvals[ctrl[0]][2] != cvals[ctrl[1]][2]
+
+    print(f"positions {len(fens)} (each also mirrored): {len(fens)*3} comparisons")
+    print(f"asymmetric values: {bad}")
+    for row in rows[:15]:
+        print("  " + row)
+    print(f"control (two different positions must differ): "
+          f"{cvals[ctrl[0]][2]} vs {cvals[ctrl[1]][2]} -> "
+          f"{'works' if control_works else 'BROKEN'}")
+    if not control_works:
+        print("RESULT: the comparison itself is broken; nothing can be concluded")
+        sys.exit(2)
+    if bad:
+        print(f"RESULT: {bad} asymmetric evaluation value(s)")
+        sys.exit(1)
+    print("RESULT: eval() is exactly colour-symmetric on every position tested")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job13/is_legal_probe.cpp b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job13/is_legal_probe.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..ce94b49d6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job13/is_legal_probe.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+// is_legal_probe.cpp -- cross-checks the fast legality path against brute force.
+//
+// Board::is_legal() (with FORGE_SPD_KING_LINES=1) takes a shortcut when the side is not in
+// check, the move is not en passant and the mover is not the king: it only consults the pin
+// set and the alignment test (board.cpp:747-751). The brute-force truth is: make the move and
+// ask whether the mover's own king is attacked.
+//
+// For every legal-looking move generated over random play this program compares:
+//   fast  = board.is_legal(move)          (the shipped shortcut)
+//   brute = make + square_attacked(king)  (unmake)
+// and reports every disagreement with its FEN and move.
+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <random>
+#include <string>
+
+using namespace forge;
+
+namespace {
+bool brute_legal(const Board& board, Move move) {
+    Board copy = board;
+    Undo undo;
+    (void)copy.make_move(move, undo);
+    // After make_move the side to move is the opponent; the mover's king must not be attacked
+    // by the new side to move.
+    const Color mover = opposite(copy.side_to_move());
+    return !copy.square_attacked(copy.king_square(mover), copy.side_to_move());
+}
+}  // namespace
+
+int main(int argc, char** argv) {
+    const int games = argc > 1 ? std::atoi(argv[1]) : 40;
+    const unsigned seed = argc > 2 ? static_cast<unsigned>(std::atoi(argv[2])) : 701u;
+    std::mt19937_64 rng(seed);
+
+    std::uint64_t compared = 0, mismatches = 0, fast_true_brute_false = 0, fast_false_brute_true = 0;
+    std::string first;
+    for (int game = 0; game < games; ++game) {
+        Board board;
+        for (int ply = 0; ply < 250; ++ply) {
+            MoveList pseudo;
+            board.generate_pseudo_legal(pseudo, false);
+            for (const Move move : pseudo) {
+                const bool fast = board.is_legal(move);
+                const bool brute = brute_legal(board, move);
+                ++compared;
+                if (fast != brute) {
+                    ++mismatches;
+                    if (fast && !brute) ++fast_true_brute_false;
+                    if (!fast && brute) ++fast_false_brute_true;
+                    if (first.empty()) {
+                        first = "fen " + board.fen() + " move " + Board::move_to_uci(move) +
+                                " fast " + (fast ? "legal" : "illegal") +
+                                " brute " + (brute ? "legal" : "illegal");
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            const auto legal = board.legal_moves();
+            if (legal.size() == 0) break;
+            const Move pick = legal[static_cast<std::size_t>(rng() % legal.size())];
+            Undo undo;
+            (void)board.make_move(pick, undo);
+        }
+    }
+    std::printf("games %d seed %u\n", games, seed);
+    std::printf("moves compared %llu  mismatches %llu (fast-says-legal-but-illegal %llu, "
+                "fast-says-illegal-but-legal %llu)\n",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(compared),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(mismatches),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(fast_true_brute_false),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(fast_false_brute_true));
+    if (compared == 0) {
+        std::printf("FAIL nothing compared\n");
+        return 2;
+    }
+    if (mismatches != 0) {
+        std::printf("FIRST MISMATCH %s\n", first.c_str());
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::printf("OK the fast legality path agreed with make/unmake brute force on every move\n");
+    return 0;
+}
