diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/board_probes.cpp b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/board_probes.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..6565d42dd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/board_probes.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,198 @@
+// board_probes.cpp -- three targeted probes for the board.cpp read, each with its own
+// positive control, on an unmodified build of 6b98f217 (this file is compiled against
+// the real src/board.cpp; nothing in the engine is changed).
+//
+// PROBE 1  castling rights surviving a rook capture on its home square.
+//          The risk: CastlingMasks clears rights on moves from OR to a corner. A capture
+//          that lands on a rook's home square must clear that side's right. If the mask
+//          were wrong, rights would survive after the rook is gone -- in normal play, an
+//          illegal castling some plies later.
+//
+// PROBE 2  an en-passant square set after a double push when no capturer exists.
+//          The risk: make_move sets ep_square_ for every double push. That is lawful for
+//          a FEN, but the ZOBRIST key must only include the ep term when a legal ep
+//          capture exists (has_legal_en_passant_capture). If the two disagree, the same
+//          position reached two ways gets two keys, and the TT mixes them up.
+//
+// PROBE 3  a king square that can go stale across a null move.
+//          The risk: make_null_move/unmake_null_move do not touch king_squares_. They do
+//          not move the king, so that is correct -- unless some other path updates
+//          king_squares_ based on side_. Probe: the king square must be unchanged by a
+//          null move, and equal to the square found by scanning the bitboard.
+
+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <string>
+#include <vector>
+
+using forge::Board;
+using forge::Move;
+using forge::Undo;
+
+namespace {
+
+int failures = 0;
+
+void check(bool condition, const std::string& what, const std::string& context) {
+    if (condition) return;
+    std::printf("FAIL %s   [%s]\n", what.c_str(), context.c_str());
+    ++failures;
+}
+
+int square_of(const Board& board, forge::Piece piece) {
+    const forge::Bitboard bb = board.pieces(piece);
+    if (bb == 0) return -1;
+    return forge::pop_lsb(const_cast<forge::Bitboard&>(bb));
+}
+
+}  // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    // ---------- PROBE 1: castling right must die when a rook is captured home ----------
+    {
+        // White may castle both ways; a black rook on a8 and h8, a black queen able to take a1.
+        const char* fen = "r3k2r/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K2R b KQkq - 0 1";
+        Board board;
+        check(board.set_fen(fen), "probe1 FEN accepted", fen);
+        // Black plays Rxh1? there is no rook on h1. Play Rxa1 from a8 along the empty rank.
+        const auto moves = board.legal_moves();
+        Move rxa1 = Move::none();
+        for (const Move move : moves) {
+            if (Board::move_to_uci(move) == "a8a1") { rxa1 = move; break; }
+        }
+        check(!rxa1.is_none(), "probe1 a8a1 is available", board.fen());
+        Undo undo;
+        (void)board.make_move(rxa1, undo);
+        const std::uint8_t rights = board.castling_rights();
+        // White's queen-side right must be gone (the a1 rook was captured).
+        check((rights & 2U) == 0U, "probe1 White queen-side right cleared by Rxa1", board.fen());
+        // a8 is Black's QUEEN-side rook, so right 8 must go and right 4 (h8 rook, untouched)
+        // must stay. My first version of this probe asserted 4 must be cleared: that was my
+        // error, not the engine's, and it is kept here as the corrected assertion.
+        check((rights & 8U) == 0U, "probe1 Black QUEEN-side right cleared by moving Ra8 away",
+              board.fen());
+        check((rights & 4U) != 0U, "probe1 Black king-side right survives (h8 rook never moved)",
+              board.fen());
+        // White king-side must still be there.
+        check((rights & 1U) != 0U, "probe1 White king-side right survives", board.fen());
+        std::printf("probe1 rights after Rxa1 = %u (fen %s)\n", static_cast<unsigned>(rights),
+                    board.fen().c_str());
+        board.unmake_move(rxa1, undo);
+        check(board.fen() == "r3k2r/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K2R b KQkq - 0 1",
+              "probe1 unmake restores the exact FEN", board.fen());
+    }
+
+    // ---------- PROBE 2: ep square vs. the ep term in the key ----------
+    {
+        // (a) a double push with NO black pawn able to capture: ep square is set,
+        //     the key must NOT carry an ep term, so the same position reached by a
+        //     different move order must have the same key.
+        const char* fen = "4k3/8/8/8/8/8/4P3/4K3 w - - 0 1";
+        Board board;
+        check(board.set_fen(fen), "probe2a FEN accepted", fen);
+        const auto moves = board.legal_moves();
+        Move e2e4 = Move::none();
+        for (const Move move : moves) {
+            if (Board::move_to_uci(move) == "e2e4") { e2e4 = move; break; }
+        }
+        check(!e2e4.is_none(), "probe2a e2e4 is available", board.fen());
+        Undo undo;
+        (void)board.make_move(e2e4, undo);
+        const std::string after = board.fen();
+        const std::uint64_t key_with_ep_field = board.key();
+        std::printf("probe2a after e2e4 fen=[%s] key=%llu\n", after.c_str(),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(key_with_ep_field));
+
+        // The same placement and side, with no ep square at all.
+        Board same;
+        const std::string no_ep = "4k3/8/8/8/4P3/8/8/4K3 b - - 0 1";
+        check(same.set_fen(no_ep), "probe2a control FEN accepted", no_ep);
+        const std::uint64_t key_without_ep_field = same.key();
+        std::printf("probe2a control fen=[%s] key=%llu\n", no_ep.c_str(),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(key_without_ep_field));
+        // The engine's stated rule: the ep term enters the key only when a legal ep
+        // capture exists. Here none does (no black pawn at all), so the two keys must
+        // be equal. If they differ, the TT sees two keys for one position.
+        check(key_with_ep_field == key_without_ep_field,
+              "probe2a no-capturer double push keeps the key ep-free", after + " vs " + no_ep);
+
+        // (b) positive control for the rule: WITH a black pawn next to the pushed pawn
+        //     but pinned so that no LEGAL ep capture exists -- the key must still be
+        //     ep-free, and the engine must agree with itself on that.
+        //     Black pawn d4, white pawn e2 pushes to e4; black pawn d4 could "capture"
+        //     e3, but the black king on d5 would then be in check from a white rook on a5?
+        //     Keep it simple and explicit: rook on e1 pins nothing, so use a real pin.
+        // Black pawn d4 could capture e3 en passant, but the black king on d5 would then be
+        // exposed to the white rook on a5 along the fifth rank -> no LEGAL ep capture, so
+        // the key must be ep-free. Reach the ep square by a real double push so the FEN
+        // validator is not the thing under test.
+        const char* pin_pre = "8/8/8/K6r/8/8/3p4/4k3 b - - 0 1";
+        Board pinned;
+        if (pinned.set_fen(pin_pre)) {
+            std::printf("probe2b pin construction accepted, key before push=%llu\n",
+                        static_cast<unsigned long long>(pinned.key()));
+        } else {
+            std::printf("probe2b pin construction REFUSED by the engine: not a result\n");
+        }
+    }
+
+    // ---------- PROBE 3: king square across a null move ----------
+    {
+        const char* fen = "r3k2r/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K2R w KQkq - 0 1";
+        Board board;
+        check(board.set_fen(fen), "probe3 FEN accepted", fen);
+        const int king_before = board.king_square(forge::White);
+        const int scan_before = square_of(board, forge::WK);
+        check(king_before == scan_before, "probe3 king square matches the bitboard before the null",
+              std::to_string(king_before) + " vs " + std::to_string(scan_before));
+        std::printf("probe3 before null: king_square=%d bitboard=%d\n", king_before, scan_before);
+        forge::NullUndo null_undo;
+        board.make_null_move(null_undo);
+        const int king_during = board.king_square(forge::White);
+        const int scan_during = square_of(board, forge::WK);
+        check(king_during == king_before, "probe3 king square survives the null move",
+              std::to_string(king_before) + " -> " + std::to_string(king_during));
+        check(king_during == scan_during, "probe3 king square matches the bitboard during the null",
+              std::to_string(king_during) + " vs " + std::to_string(scan_during));
+        board.unmake_null_move(null_undo);
+        const int king_after = board.king_square(forge::White);
+        check(king_after == king_before, "probe3 king square restored by unmake_null_move",
+              std::to_string(king_before) + " -> " + std::to_string(king_after));
+        std::printf("probe3 during/after null: %d / %d (expected %d)\n", king_during, king_after,
+                    king_before);
+        check(board.fen() == fen, "probe3 null move round-trip restores the exact FEN", board.fen());
+
+        // The stale-king risk that CAN bite: a real king move must update the square, and
+        // unmake must put it back. Then a null move after a king move must not resurrect
+        // the old square.
+        Board moving;
+        (void)moving.set_fen(fen);
+        const auto moves = moving.legal_moves();
+        Move e1e2 = Move::none();
+        for (const Move move : moves) {
+            if (Board::move_to_uci(move) == "e1e2") { e1e2 = move; break; }
+        }
+        check(!e1e2.is_none(), "probe3 e1e2 is available", moving.fen());
+        Undo undo;
+        (void)moving.make_move(e1e2, undo);
+        check(moving.king_square(forge::White) == 12, "probe3 king square updated by e1e2",
+              std::to_string(moving.king_square(forge::White)));
+        forge::NullUndo nundo;
+        moving.make_null_move(nundo);
+        check(moving.king_square(forge::White) == 12, "probe3 king square correct after a null move",
+              std::to_string(moving.king_square(forge::White)));
+        moving.unmake_null_move(nundo);
+        moving.unmake_move(e1e2, undo);
+        check(moving.king_square(forge::White) == 4, "probe3 king square restored by unmake",
+              std::to_string(moving.king_square(forge::White)));
+        std::printf("probe3 after e1e2 + null + unmake: king_square=%d (expected 4)\n",
+                    moving.king_square(forge::White));
+        check(moving.fen() == fen, "probe3 king-move round-trip restores the exact FEN", moving.fen());
+    }
+
+    std::printf("\n%s (%d failure(s))\n", failures == 0 ? "ALL PROBES PASSED" : "PROBES FAILED",
+                failures);
+    return failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
+}

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/epkey_probe.cpp b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/epkey_probe.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..3935e89c2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/epkey_probe.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+// epkey_probe.cpp -- control for PROBE 2 of board_probes.cpp.
+//
+// board_probes.cpp showed that a double push with NO possible capturer leaves the key
+// unchanged (the ep term is correctly absent). That result only means something if the ep
+// term is really included when a LEGAL ep capture exists. This program shows both sides:
+//   (A) ep capture legal  -> key WITH ep term must differ from the same board without it
+//   (B) ep capture illegal (the capturing pawn is pinned) -> key must NOT differ
+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdio>
+
+using namespace forge;
+
+int main() {
+    // (A) ep capture legal. Black pawn d4, White pawn just arrived on e4, Black to move,
+    //     ep square e3. The only difference between the two FENs is the ep field, and the
+    //     side to move is the SAME in both, so any key difference is the ep term alone.
+    Board a; (void)a.set_fen("4k3/8/8/8/3pP3/8/8/4K3 b - e3 0 1");
+    Board a_ref; (void)a_ref.set_fen("4k3/8/8/8/3pP3/8/8/4K3 b - - 0 1");
+    std::printf("A with ep   fen=[%s] key=%llu\n", a.fen().c_str(), (unsigned long long)a.key());
+    std::printf("A no   ep   fen=[%s] key=%llu\n", a_ref.fen().c_str(), (unsigned long long)a_ref.key());
+    const bool a_differs = a.key() != a_ref.key();
+    std::printf("A keys differ = %s (must be yes: the ep term has to enter the key when a legal "
+                "ep capture exists, otherwise probe2a's equality proved nothing)\n",
+                a_differs ? "yes" : "NO");
+
+    // (A2) ep capture ILLEGAL because the capturing pawn is pinned: the black pawn on d4 is
+    //      pinned to its king on d8 by a white rook on d1. Capturing e3 would open the file.
+    Board pin; (void)pin.set_fen("3k4/8/8/8/3pP3/8/8/3RK3 b - e3 0 1");
+    Board pin_ref; (void)pin_ref.set_fen("3k4/8/8/8/3pP3/8/8/3RK3 b - - 0 1");
+    std::printf("A2 pinned ep fen=[%s] key=%llu\n", pin.fen().c_str(), (unsigned long long)pin.key());
+    std::printf("A2 pinned ref fen=[%s] key=%llu\n", pin_ref.fen().c_str(), (unsigned long long)pin_ref.key());
+    const bool pinned_differs = pin.key() != pin_ref.key();
+    std::printf("A2 keys differ = %s (must be NO: no legal ep capture, so the ep term must be absent)\n",
+                pinned_differs ? "YES" : "no");
+
+    // (B) ep capture illegal: the black pawn on d4 is pinned by the white rook on h4 down
+    // the fourth rank to the black king on a4... construct with the king on the same rank as
+    // the capturing pawn's destination, which is what an ep capture would vacate.
+    Board b; (void)b.set_fen("k7/8/8/8/K2pP2r/8/8/8 b - - 0 1");
+    std::printf("B constructed fen=[%s]\n", b.fen().c_str());
+    std::printf("B key=%llu\n", (unsigned long long)b.key());
+
+    return a_differs ? 0 : 1;
+}

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/key_after_test.cpp b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/key_after_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..18f2f074e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job6/key_after_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+// key_after_test.cpp -- compares Board::key_after() with make_move()'s own key,
+// exhaustively over random legal play, on an instrumented COPY of 6b98f217.
+//
+// Why this matters for normal play: search.cpp:1504 and :1964 call key_after() to
+// prefetch the child's transposition-table cluster before make_move. Its only
+// in-tree guard is `assert(!early_key || child_key == board.key())` at
+// search.cpp:1505 / :1965, and NDEBUG removes assertions from the Release build,
+// so in the shipped engine nothing checks that the prefetched key is the real one.
+// A wrong key puts the prefetch on the wrong cluster: not a crash, just a slower
+// search -- unless a caller ever trusts the value.
+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <random>
+#include <vector>
+
+using forge::Board;
+using forge::Move;
+using forge::Undo;
+
+int main(int argc, char** argv) {
+    const int games = argc > 1 ? std::atoi(argv[1]) : 200;
+    const unsigned seed = argc > 2 ? static_cast<unsigned>(std::atoi(argv[2])) : 701u;
+    std::mt19937_64 rng(seed);
+
+    std::uint64_t checked = 0, refused = 0, mismatches = 0, first_mismatch_game = 0;
+    std::string first_fen, first_move;
+    std::uint64_t first_got = 0, first_want = 0;
+
+    for (int game = 0; game < games; ++game) {
+        Board board;  // startpos
+        for (int ply = 0; ply < 400; ++ply) {
+            const auto moves = board.legal_moves();
+            if (moves.size() == 0) break;
+            for (const Move move : moves) {
+                std::uint64_t predicted = 0;
+                const bool ok = board.key_after(move, predicted);
+                if (!ok) { ++refused; continue; }
+                Board copy = board;
+                Undo undo;
+                (void)copy.make_move(move, undo);
+                const std::uint64_t actual = copy.key();
+                ++checked;
+                if (predicted != actual) {
+                    ++mismatches;
+                    if (mismatches == 1) {
+                        first_mismatch_game = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(game);
+                        first_fen = board.fen();
+                        first_move = Board::move_to_uci(move);
+                        first_got = predicted;
+                        first_want = actual;
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            // random continuation
+            const Move pick = moves[static_cast<std::size_t>(rng() % moves.size())];
+            Undo undo;
+            (void)board.make_move(pick, undo);
+        }
+    }
+
+    std::printf("games %d seed %u\n", games, seed);
+    std::printf("key_after checked %llu  refused %llu\n",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(checked), static_cast<unsigned long long>(refused));
+    std::printf("mismatches %llu\n", static_cast<unsigned long long>(mismatches));
+    if (mismatches != 0) {
+        std::printf("FIRST MISMATCH game %llu fen %s move %s got %llu want %llu\n",
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(first_mismatch_game), first_fen.c_str(),
+                    first_move.c_str(), static_cast<unsigned long long>(first_got),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(first_want));
+        return 1;
+    }
+    if (checked == 0) {
+        std::printf("FAIL nothing was checked: this run proves nothing\n");
+        return 2;
+    }
+    std::printf("OK every predicted key equalled make_move's key\n");
+    return 0;
+}

new file mode 100644
index 000000000..b88f5ba9f

+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/SEE_NOTES.txt
@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+SEE cross-check: NOT a result.
+I wrote see_crosscheck.cpp as an independent static-exchange evaluator to compare with
+Board::see_ge(). It disagreed on captures, so I checked its first disagreeing cases with
+python-chess by hand:
+  fen 2b1kbn1/2r3p1/p1Pp1q2/5p2/2BpPP2/1P2Q2r/P1R4P/RNB1K3 w Q - 2 29, move e4f5
+  -> after exf5 Black's legal captures are only h3e3 and d4e3 (python-chess, printed list);
+     nothing recaptures on f5; see_ge(exf5,100)=true is CORRECT and my reference was wrong.
+  fen r1bqkbnr/pppppppp/2n5/8/8/2P5/PP1PPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 1 2, move b2b4
+  -> my FIRST reference version called this losing; python-chess shows White wins a knight
+     for a pawn (+200), so the engine was right there too.
+Conclusion: my oracle is the unreliable side. I fixed two bugs in it and it still differs, so
+it is not fit to be an oracle and I draw NO conclusion about see_ge from it. The engine's SEE
+is exercised indirectly by the 14-position perft agreement and by bench pins, and both are
+unchanged; that is all I can honestly say.
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/check_repetition.py b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/check_repetition.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..f457e6ee1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/check_repetition.py
@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""check_repetition.py EXE_OR_PROBE
+
+Feeds move lists to repetition_probe and compares its `rep=` column against python-chess.
+
+python-chess semantics:
+  * board.is_repetition(2) -> twofold (any earlier occurrence)
+  * board.is_repetition(3) -> threefold (the FIDE draw)
+
+The engine's no-argument is_repetition() returns "seen twice before", i.e. this position plus
+two earlier occurrences = threefold. So the comparison target is python-chess's
+is_repetition(3), computed ONCE per ply, and the driver ASSERTS a rep= column and a key were
+found for every ply (no missing line may pass as agreement).
+
+Prints one row per ply where the two disagree, and a total. Exit 1 on any disagreement or any
+missing measurement.
+"""
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import chess
+
+HERE = __file__.rsplit("/", 1)[0]
+
+LISTS = [
+    # a clean threefold: knights out and back twice
+    "g1f3 g8f6 f3g1 f6g8 g1f3 g8f6 f3g1 f6g8",
+    # same, but the second return happens after a pawn move resetting the clock: NOT a draw
+    "g1f3 g8f6 f3g1 f6g8 e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 g8f6 f3g1 f6g8",
+    # a twofold only (one return): must NOT be a draw
+    "g1f3 g8f6 f3g1 f6g8",
+    # repetition with queens: 1.e4 e5 2.Qh5 Nc6 3.Qf3 Nf6 4.Qh5 Nc6 5.Qf3 Nf6 -> wait, use a clean one
+    "e2e4 e7e5 d1h5 b8c6 h5f3 g8f6 f3h5 c6b8 h5f3 b8c6",
+    # the fifty-move counter interaction: 8 reversible plies then a reset, then 8 more
+    "b1c3 b8c6 c3b1 c6b8 b1c3 b8c6 c3b1 c6b8 d2d4 d7d5 b1c3 b8c6 c3b1 c6b8",
+    # a long shuffle that repeats many times
+    "b1c3 b8c6 c3b1 c6b8 b1c3 b8c6 c3b1 c6b8 b1c3 b8c6 c3b1 c6b8 b1c3 b8c6 c3b1 c6b8",
+]
+
+PLY = re.compile(r"^PLY (\d+)(?: (\S+) clock=(\d+) key=(\d+) rep=(\d+) rep0=(\d+))?$")
+
+
+def main():
+    probe = sys.argv[1]
+    text = "\n".join(LISTS) + "\n"
+    out = subprocess.run([probe], input=text, capture_output=True, text=True)
+    if out.returncode != 0:
+        raise SystemExit(f"FAIL probe exited {out.returncode}: {out.stderr[:400]}")
+
+    rows, list_index, board, disagreements = [], -1, None, 0
+    seen_plies = 0
+    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
+        if line.startswith("BROKEN"):
+            raise SystemExit(f"FAIL {line}: a move list in this test is not legal, so the "
+                             f"comparison would measure nothing")
+        if line.startswith("LIST "):
+            list_index += 1
+            board = chess.Board()
+            continue
+        if line.startswith("END"):
+            continue
+        m = PLY.match(line)
+        if not m:
+            continue
+        ply = int(m.group(1))
+        if m.group(2) is None and ply == 0:
+            engine_rep = m.group(5)
+            # the PLY 0 line has a different field layout: re-parse it
+            m0 = re.match(r"^PLY 0 clock=(\d+) key=(\d+) rep=(\d+) rep0=(\d+)$", line)
+            if not m0:
+                raise SystemExit(f"FAIL could not parse ply 0 line [{line}]")
+            engine_rep = int(m0.group(3))
+        else:
+            engine_rep = int(m.group(5))
+        if ply > 0:
+            # advance python-chess by replaying the move named on this line
+            move_uci = m.group(2)
+            board.push(chess.Move.from_uci(move_uci))
+        seen_plies += 1
+        ref = board.is_repetition(3)
+        got = bool(engine_rep)
+        if got != ref:
+            disagreements += 1
+            rows.append((list_index, ply, m.group(2) if m.group(2) else "start",
+                         got, ref, board.fen()))
+
+    if seen_plies == 0:
+        raise SystemExit("FAIL no PLY lines were parsed: nothing was measured")
+    print(f"plies compared: {seen_plies}")
+    for li, ply, move, got, ref, fen in rows:
+        print(f"  DISAGREE list {li} ply {ply} move {move}: engine rep={got} "
+              f"python-chess threefold={ref}  fen {fen}")
+    if disagreements:
+        print(f"\nRESULT: {disagreements} disagreement(s)")
+        sys.exit(1)
+    print("RESULT: engine is_repetition() agrees with python-chess threefold at every ply")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/repetition_probe.cpp b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/repetition_probe.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..ee0299ceb
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/repetition_probe.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+// repetition_probe.cpp -- does Board::is_repetition() agree with the real rule?
+//
+// Plays each move list given on stdin (one list per line, UCI moves separated by spaces,
+// starting from startpos) and after every move prints:
+//   ply, move, halfmove_clock, key, is_repetition(), is_repetition(root=0)
+// A python driver compares is_repetition() with python-chess's is_repetition(3)
+// (threefold) so a wrong answer in normal play -- declaring a draw where there is none, or
+// missing a real one -- shows up as a disagreement.
+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <sstream>
+#include <string>
+
+using namespace forge;
+
+int main() {
+    std::string line;
+    while (std::getline(std::cin, line)) {
+        if (line.empty()) continue;
+        Board board;
+        std::istringstream moves(line);
+        std::string token;
+        int ply = 0;
+        std::printf("LIST %s\n", line.c_str());
+        std::printf("PLY 0 clock=%u key=%llu rep=%d rep0=%d\n",
+                    static_cast<unsigned>(board.halfmove_clock()),
+                    static_cast<unsigned long long>(board.key()),
+                    int(board.is_repetition()), int(board.is_repetition(0)));
+        while (moves >> token) {
+            const auto move = board.parse_uci(token);
+            if (!move.has_value()) {
+                std::printf("BROKEN %s at ply %d (not legal)\n", token.c_str(), ply + 1);
+                break;
+            }
+            Undo undo;
+            (void)board.make_move(*move, undo);
+            ++ply;
+            std::printf("PLY %d %s clock=%u key=%llu rep=%d rep0=%d\n", ply, token.c_str(),
+                        static_cast<unsigned>(board.halfmove_clock()),
+                        static_cast<unsigned long long>(board.key()),
+                        int(board.is_repetition()), int(board.is_repetition(0)));
+        }
+        std::printf("END\n");
+    }
+    return 0;
+}
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/see_crosscheck.cpp b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/see_crosscheck.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..fb07be59a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job7/see_crosscheck.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,211 @@
+// see_crosscheck.cpp -- compares Board::see_ge(move, t) with an independent, slow,
+// obviously-correct SEE implemented here from the definition, over random legal play.
+//
+// The independent implementation:
+//   * simulates the capture on a local copy,
+//   * repeatedly finds the least valuable attacker of the destination square for the side
+//     to recapture, using the engine's own attack tables on the simulated occupancy,
+//   * runs the standard swap algorithm from the back of the exchange list,
+//   * handles en passant (the victim stands on a different square) and promotions.
+// It deliberately does NOT reuse Board::see_ge or its helpers.
+//
+// For every legal move and a set of thresholds t in {-1, 0, 1, 50, 100, 900}, the engine's
+// boolean see_ge(move, t) must equal (reference_see >= t).
+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+
+#include <array>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <random>
+#include <vector>
+
+using namespace forge;
+
+namespace {
+
+// The engine's SEE prices a king at 0 (see include/forge/eval.hpp:32 SeePieceValue and the
+// comment at src/search.cpp:157 "the SEE table stores king as 0"). Match that convention,
+// otherwise every line where a king can recapture differs for a reason that is a documented
+// engine choice, not a fault.
+constexpr std::array<int, 7> Val{0, 100, 300, 300, 500, 900, 0};
+
+struct Sim {
+    std::array<Piece, 64> sq{};
+    Bitboard occ = 0;
+    Bitboard side_bits[2] = {0, 0};
+
+    static Sim from(const Board& b) {
+        Sim s;
+        for (int i = 0; i < 64; ++i) s.sq[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)] = b.piece_at(i);
+        s.occ = b.occupied();
+        s.side_bits[0] = b.occupied(White);
+        s.side_bits[1] = b.occupied(Black);
+        return s;
+    }
+    void erase(int s) {
+        const Piece p = sq[static_cast<std::size_t>(s)];
+        if (p == Empty) return;
+        sq[static_cast<std::size_t>(s)] = Empty;
+        occ &= ~square_bb(s);
+        side_bits[static_cast<std::size_t>(color_of(p))] &= ~square_bb(s);
+    }
+    void place(int s, Piece p) {
+        erase(s);
+        sq[static_cast<std::size_t>(s)] = p;
+        occ |= square_bb(s);
+        side_bits[static_cast<std::size_t>(color_of(p))] |= square_bb(s);
+    }
+    [[nodiscard]] Bitboard side(Color c) const { return side_bits[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)]; }
+    [[nodiscard]] Bitboard type(Color c, PieceType t) const {
+        Bitboard r = 0;
+        for (int i = 0; i < 64; ++i) {
+            const Piece p = sq[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)];
+            if (p != Empty && color_of(p) == c && piece_type(p) == t) r |= square_bb(i);
+        }
+        return r;
+    }
+};
+
+// All pieces of `by` that attack square `to` on the simulated board, ignoring pins.
+Bitboard attackers(const Sim& s, Color by, int to) {
+    Bitboard r = 0;
+    r |= attacks::pawn(opposite(by), to) & s.type(by, Pawn);
+    r |= attacks::knight(to) & s.type(by, Knight);
+    r |= attacks::king(to) & s.type(by, King);
+    const Bitboard diag = (s.type(by, Bishop) | s.type(by, Queen));
+    const Bitboard orth = (s.type(by, Rook) | s.type(by, Queen));
+    r |= attacks::bishop(to, s.occ) & diag;
+    r |= attacks::rook(to, s.occ) & orth;
+    return r & s.side(by);
+}
+
+int cheapest_valuer(const Sim& s, Color by, int to, int& from_square) {
+    int best = 1000000;
+    from_square = -1;
+    Bitboard a = attackers(s, by, to);
+    while (a != 0) {
+        const int from = pop_lsb(a);
+        const int v = Val[static_cast<std::size_t>(piece_type(s.sq[static_cast<std::size_t>(from)]))];
+        if (v < best) { best = v; from_square = from; }
+    }
+    return best;
+}
+
+// Returns true when the static exchange for `move` gains at least `threshold`.
+bool reference_see_ge(const Board& board, Move move, int threshold) {
+    const Color us = board.side_to_move();
+    Sim s = Sim::from(board);
+    const int from = move.from;
+    const int to = move.to;
+    const bool ep = (move.flags & EnPassant) != 0U;
+    const int victim_square = ep ? to - pawn_push_delta(us) : to;
+    const Piece moving = s.sq[static_cast<std::size_t>(from)];
+    const Piece victim = s.sq[static_cast<std::size_t>(victim_square)];
+
+    // Gain list: gain[0] = value of the first victim (+ promotion delta).
+    std::vector<int> gain;
+    gain.push_back(Val[static_cast<std::size_t>(piece_type(victim))]);
+    if (move.is_promotion()) {
+        gain[0] += Val[move.promotion] - Val[Pawn];
+    }
+
+    s.erase(victim_square);
+    s.erase(from);
+    s.place(to, move.is_promotion() ? make_piece(us, move.promotion) : moving);
+
+    // Swap-list algorithm. gain[i] must be the value the side to move at step i-1 stands to
+    // lose if the exchange stops after its own capture, which requires carrying the value of
+    // the piece currently standing on `to` -- not merely the cheapest attacker's value. My
+    // first version used `v - gain.back()` and was wrong: it reported b2b4 here as a losing
+    // capture when White wins a knight for a pawn (settled independently with python-chess).
+    Color stm = opposite(us);
+    int standing_value = Val[static_cast<std::size_t>(
+        piece_type(move.is_promotion() ? make_piece(us, move.promotion) : moving))];
+    while (true) {
+        int next_from = -1;
+        const int v = cheapest_valuer(s, stm, to, next_from);
+        if (next_from < 0) break;
+        // The side now to move captures the piece standing on `to`, whose value is
+        // standing_value: gain = standing_value - (what it may lose next).
+        gain.push_back(standing_value - gain.back());
+        standing_value = v;
+        s.erase(next_from);
+        PieceType standing = Pawn;
+        for (int t = Pawn; t <= King; ++t) {
+            if (Val[static_cast<std::size_t>(t)] == v) { standing = static_cast<PieceType>(t); break; }
+        }
+        s.place(to, make_piece(stm, standing));
+        stm = opposite(stm);
+    }
+
+    // Standard back-propagation.
+    for (int i = static_cast<int>(gain.size()) - 1; i > 0; --i) {
+        gain[static_cast<std::size_t>(i - 1)] =
+            -std::max(-gain[static_cast<std::size_t>(i - 1)],
+                      gain[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)]);
+    }
+    return gain[0] >= threshold;
+}
+
+}  // namespace
+
+// ABANDONED as an oracle (kept for the record): this reference disagreed with the engine on
+// exf5 in "2b1kbn1/2r3p1/p1Pp1q2/5p2/2BpPP2/1P2Q2r/P1R4P/RNB1K3 w Q - 2 29". python-chess
+// settles that case the engine's way: after exf5 Black's only legal captures are h3e3 and
+// d4e3, so nothing recaptures on f5, and see_ge(exf5, 100)=true is right. The reference's
+// attacker list was wrong (it invented a queen recapture), so ITS disagreements are not
+// evidence about the engine. No finding is drawn from this program.
+int main(int argc, char** argv) {
+    const int games = argc > 1 ? std::atoi(argv[1]) : 60;
+    const unsigned seed = argc > 2 ? static_cast<unsigned>(std::atoi(argv[2])) : 701u;
+    std::mt19937_64 rng(seed);
+    constexpr std::array<int, 6> thresholds{-1, 0, 1, 50, 100, 900};
+
+    std::uint64_t compared = 0, mismatches = 0;
+    std::string first;
+    for (int game = 0; game < games; ++game) {
+        Board board;
+        for (int ply = 0; ply < 200; ++ply) {
+            const auto moves = board.legal_moves();
+            if (moves.size() == 0) break;
+            for (const Move move : moves) {
+                // SEE of a NON-capture is not defined by the exchange algorithm alone (the
+                // engine and my reference legitimately differ there), so this cross-check
+                // covers captures only and says so in its own output.
+                if (!move.is_capture()) continue;
+                for (const int t : thresholds) {
+                    const bool engine = board.see_ge(move, t);
+                    const bool ref = reference_see_ge(board, move, t);
+                    ++compared;
+                    if (engine != ref) {
+                        ++mismatches;
+                        if (first.empty()) {
+                            first = "fen " + board.fen() + " move " + Board::move_to_uci(move) +
+                                    " threshold " + std::to_string(t) +
+                                    " engine " + (engine ? "true" : "false") +
+                                    " reference " + (ref ? "true" : "false");
+                        }
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+            const Move pick = moves[static_cast<std::size_t>(rng() % moves.size())];
+            Undo undo;
+            (void)board.make_move(pick, undo);
+        }
+    }
+    std::printf("games %d seed %u (CAPTURES ONLY, all thresholds)\n", games, seed);
+    std::printf("see_ge comparisons %llu  mismatches %llu\n",
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(compared),
+                static_cast<unsigned long long>(mismatches));
+    if (compared == 0) {
+        std::printf("FAIL nothing compared: this run proves nothing\n");
+        return 2;
+    }
+    if (mismatches != 0) {
+        std::printf("FIRST MISMATCH %s\n", first.c_str());
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::printf("OK engine see_ge agreed with the reference at every threshold\n");
+    return 0;
+}

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job8/check_legal_move.py b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job8/check_legal_move.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..80e6b3837
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job8/check_legal_move.py
@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""check_legal_move.py PROBE
+
+Compares repetition_probe-style output from legal_move_probe.cpp with python-chess.
+Asserts every line parses and that has_legal_move == (legal_count > 0) internally too,
+so a missing or unparsable line can never pass as agreement.
+"""
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import chess
+
+
+def main():
+    probe = sys.argv[1]
+    out = subprocess.run([probe, "60", "701"], capture_output=True, text=True)
+    if out.returncode != 0:
+        raise SystemExit(f"FAIL probe exit {out.returncode}: {out.stderr[:300]}")
+
+    checked = disagree_count = 0
+    problems = []
+    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
+        if not line or line.startswith(("GAMES", "END", "REFUSED")):
+            if line.startswith("REFUSED"):
+                problems.append(f"engine REFUSED a FEN the test wanted: {line}")
+            continue
+        try:
+            fen, rest = line.split(" | ")
+            fields = dict(kv.split("=") for kv in rest.split())
+            hm = int(fields["has_legal_move"])
+            lc = int(fields["legal_count"])
+        except Exception:
+            problems.append(f"unparsable line: {line[:120]}")
+            continue
+        checked += 1
+        board = chess.Board(fen)
+        ref = board.legal_moves.count() > 0
+        if bool(hm) != ref:
+            disagree_count += 1
+            problems.append(f"has_legal_move={hm} but python-chess says {ref} for {fen}")
+        if bool(hm) != (lc > 0):
+            disagree_count += 1
+            problems.append(f"INTERNAL: has_legal_move={hm} vs legal_count={lc} for {fen}")
+
+    if checked == 0:
+        raise SystemExit("FAIL nothing was checked")
+    print(f"positions checked: {checked}")
+    for p in problems[:40]:
+        print("  " + p)
+    if disagree_count:
+        print(f"\nRESULT: {disagree_count} disagreement(s)")
+        sys.exit(1)
+    print("RESULT: has_legal_move() agreed with python-chess and with legal_moves().size() "
+          "on every position")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job8/legal_move_probe.cpp b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job8/legal_move_probe.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..726341d42
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job8/legal_move_probe.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+// legal_move_probe.cpp -- is Board::has_legal_move() ever wrong?
+//
+// has_legal_move() decides stalemate and checkmate at the search root and in
+// is_draw()/draw_leaf_score(), so a wrong answer is a wrong game result, not a
+// cosmetic difference.
+//
+// The reference is python-chess over a pipe: this program prints, for every position it
+// reaches, the FEN and the engine's answer; a python driver recomputes the truth from the
+// same FEN and compares. Positions are reached by random legal play plus the special
+// families that stress the fast witness path: pawn pushes blocked, promotions only,
+// en passant only, pinned-pawn-only pushes.
+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <random>
+#include <string>
+
+using namespace forge;
+
+namespace {
+void emit(const Board& board) {
+    std::printf("%s | has_legal_move=%d legal_count=%zu\n", board.fen().c_str(),
+                int(board.has_legal_move()), board.legal_moves().size());
+}
+}  // namespace
+
+int main(int argc, char** argv) {
+    const int games = argc > 1 ? std::atoi(argv[1]) : 60;
+    const unsigned seed = argc > 2 ? static_cast<unsigned>(std::atoi(argv[2])) : 701u;
+    std::mt19937_64 rng(seed);
+    std::printf("GAMES %d SEED %u\n", games, seed);
+
+    long positions = 0;
+    for (int game = 0; game < games; ++game) {
+        Board board;
+        emit(board);
+        ++positions;
+        for (int ply = 0; ply < 300; ++ply) {
+            const auto moves = board.legal_moves();
+            if (moves.size() == 0) break;
+            const Move pick = moves[static_cast<std::size_t>(rng() % moves.size())];
+            Undo undo;
+            (void)board.make_move(pick, undo);
+            // Bias toward endings where the fast witness path matters: once few pieces are
+            // left, emit every position (promotion races, blocked pawns, lone kings).
+            const int pieces = popcount(board.occupied());
+            if (pieces <= 12 || (rng() % 8) == 0) {
+                emit(board);
+                ++positions;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // Targeted families, each a handful of FENs.
+    const char* family[] = {
+        // blocked pawns with a king that has no square: stalemate
+        "7k/5Q2/6K1/8/8/8/8/8 b - - 0 1",
+        // checkmate
+        "7k/6Q1/6K1/8/8/8/8/8 b - - 0 1",
+        // lone king with moves
+        "8/8/8/8/8/8/8/K6k w - - 0 1",
+        // only move is a promotion
+        "8/8/8/8/8/8/6p1/6Kk b - - 0 1",
+        // pawn blocked, king stalemated
+        "8/8/8/8/8/5k2/5p2/5K2 w - - 0 1",
+        // en passant is the only legal move
+        "8/8/8/8/3pP3/8/8/K6k b - e3 0 1",
+        // pinned pawn cannot push, king has no square
+        "8/8/8/8/8/2k5/2p5/2K5 w - - 0 1",
+    };
+    for (const char* fen : family) {
+        Board board;
+        if (!board.set_fen(fen)) {
+            std::printf("REFUSED %s\n", fen);
+            continue;
+        }
+        emit(board);
+        ++positions;
+    }
+    std::printf("END %ld\n", positions);
+    return 0;
+}

+2r5/p2k3p/8/1N2Q2P/2p1P1p1/6PN/P2bKP2/7R b - - 3 51 | has_legal_move=1 legal_count=26
+2r5/p6p/2k2Q2/1N4bP/2p1P1p1/6PN/P3KP1R/8 b - - 7 53 | has_legal_move=1 legal_count=5

diff --git a/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job9/s14_sums.py b/forge-combo29/swarm/07/job9/s14_sums.py

@@ -0,0 +1,128 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""s14_sums.py EXE FENS OUTDIR DEPTH
+
+Repeats the brief's "known sums" check, which is simultaneously:
+  * a test of uci.cpp's setoption path (if any S14 option silently fails to apply, the node
+    count cannot land on the published number), and
+  * a check that this seat's harness sends exactly what the brief specifies
+    (ucinewgame + isready before every `go`, Threads 1, Hash 16).
+
+Asserts each number was FOUND and parses as an integer. A missing "nodes" field, a timeout or a
+zero is a hard error, never a pass.
+"""
+import json
+import os
+import queue
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import threading
+
+S14 = [
+    "LmrQuietBase value 93", "LmrQuietDivisor value 205", "LmrNoisyBase value 13",
+    "LmrNoisyDivisor value 333", "LmrHistoryDivisor value 5643", "NullMoveBase value 5",
+    "LmpBase value 8", "HistoryPruneMultiplier value 2220",
+    "HistoryBonusQuadratic value 24", "HistoryBonusLinear value 54",
+    "HistoryBonusMax value 2212", "SingularDepth value 6", "IirDepth value 2",
+    "NonPawnCorrection value true",
+]
+
+
+class Reader:
+    def __init__(self, stream):
+        self.q = queue.Queue()
+        threading.Thread(target=self._pump, args=(stream,), daemon=True).start()
+
+    def _pump(self, stream):
+        for line in stream:
+            self.q.put(line)
+        self.q.put(None)
+
+    def readline(self, timeout=180.0):
+        try:
+            return self.q.get(timeout=timeout)
+        except queue.Empty:
+            return None
+
+
+def go(exe, fen, depth):
+    proc = subprocess.Popen([exe], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                            stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, bufsize=1)
+    r = Reader(proc.stdout)
+
+    def send(c):
+        proc.stdin.write(c + "\n")
+        proc.stdin.flush()
+
+    def drain(tag):
+        while True:
+            line = r.readline()
+            if line is None:
+                raise SystemExit(f"FAIL no readyok after {tag}")
+            if line.strip() == "readyok":
+                return
+
+    send("uci")
+    while True:
+        line = r.readline()
+        if line is None or line.strip() == "uciok":
+            break
+    for opt in ["Hash value 16", "Threads value 1"] + S14:
+        send("setoption name " + opt)
+        send("isready")
+        drain(opt)
+    send("ucinewgame")
+    send("isready")
+    drain("ucinewgame")
+    send("position fen " + fen)
+    send("isready")
+    drain("position")
+    send(f"go depth {depth}")
+    nodes = None
+    score = None
+    while True:
+        line = r.readline(300.0)
+        if line is None:
+            raise SystemExit(f"FAIL no bestmove for fen {fen}")
+        if line.startswith("info depth") and " nodes " in line and " pv " in line:
+            m = re.search(r" nodes (\d+) ", line)
+            if m:
+                nodes = int(m.group(1))
+        if line.startswith("info depth") and " score " in line:
+            m = re.search(r" score (cp|mate) (-?\d+)", line)
+            if m:
+                score = line.strip()
+        if line.startswith("bestmove"):
+            break
+    send("quit")
+    try:
+        proc.wait(timeout=30)
+    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+        proc.kill()
+    if nodes is None:
+        raise SystemExit(f"FAIL no nodes figure parsed for fen {fen}: cannot compare")
+    return nodes, score
+
+
+def main():
+    exe, fens_path, outdir, depth = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], int(sys.argv[4])
+    os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
+    fens = [l.strip() for l in open(fens_path, encoding="utf-8") if l.strip()]
+    rows = []
+    total = 0
+    for i, fen in enumerate(fens):
+        nodes, score = go(exe, fen, depth)
+        rows.append({"index": i, "fen": fen, "nodes": nodes, "last_score_line": score})
+        total += nodes
+        if i < 3:
+            print(f"  first{i+1}: nodes {nodes}")
+    print(f"positions {len(rows)} depth {depth}")
+    print(f"SUM {total}")
+    json.dump({"depth": depth, "fens": fens_path, "rows": rows, "sum": total},
+              open(os.path.join(outdir, f"sum_d{depth}.json"), "w"), indent=1)
+    if total == 0:
+        raise SystemExit("FAIL sum is zero: nothing was measured")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
